Investigators struggled to decode the cryptic message left by the suspect. 调查人员努力解码嫌疑人留下的神秘晦涩信息。

cub.note:
A playful bear cub followed its mother through the dense mountain forest. 一只顽皮的小熊跟着母亲穿过密集的山地森林。

Lions usually protect their newborn cubs fiercely from external threats. 狮子通常会激烈地保护它们刚出生的幼兽免受外部威胁。

cubicle.meaning: n. 小隔间（如办公室隔间或更衣室）
cubicle.note:
He sat at his computer inside a small office cubicle all day. 他整天坐在一个小办公室隔间里的电脑前。

Changing cubicles at the public swimming pool were cleaned every morning. 公共游泳池的更衣室隔间每天早晨都会打扫干净。

culinary.note:
She enrolled in a prestigious culinary school to become a professional chef. 她考入了一家著名的烹饪学校，想成为一名专业厨师。

Local restaurants offer a rich variety of exceptional culinary delights. 当地的餐厅提供丰富多样的卓越烹饪美食。

culmination.meaning: n. 顶点；高潮；圆满结果
culmination.note:
Winning the championship was the glorious culmination of years of hard training. 赢得冠军是多年艰苦训练的光辉顶点。

The celebrations will reach their culmination with a spectacular concert. 庆典将在一场壮观的音乐会上迎来最高潮。

culpable.meaning: adj. 应受责备的，有罪的
culpable.note:
The company was held culpable for the environmental disaster. 公司被认为对这场环境灾难负有责任。

She felt culpable for not speaking up sooner. 她为没有早点站出来说话而感到内疚。

cult.meaning: n. 邪教，宗教狂热；狂热崇拜群体 adj. 极受崇拜的，形成邪教般追捧的
cult.note:
The leader of the religious cult controlled his followers through manipulation. 那个邪教的头目通过操控来控制他的追随者。

This indie film has developed a cult following over the years. 这部独立电影多年来积累了一批狂热的追随者。

cultivated.meaning: adj. 有教养的，文雅的；种植的，耕种的
cultivated.note:
He is a cultivated man with a deep appreciation for classical art. 他是一个对古典艺术有着深厚鉴赏力的有教养的人。

They walked through acres of cultivated land. 他们穿过了数英亩的耕地。

cumbersome.meaning: adj. 笨重的，难处理的；冗长的，复杂的
cumbersome.note:
The heavy machinery proved to be too cumbersome for transport. 这台重型机械被证明在运输上过于笨重。

They replaced the cumbersome paperwork with an efficient digital system. 他们用高效的数字化系统取代了繁琐的纸质工作。

cumulus.note:
Bright white cumulus clouds dotted the summer sky. 明亮的白色积云点缀着夏日的天空。

Fluffy cumulus formations usually indicate fair weather. 毛茸茸的积云通常预示着好天气。

cunning.meaning: adj. 狡猾的，狡诈的 n. 诡计，狡猾
cunning.note:
The cunning thief managed to bypass the security system. 那个狡猾的小偷设法绕过了安保系统。

She used sheer cunning to outsmart her opponents. 她利用纯粹的狡猾智胜了她的对手。

cupidity.note:
His financial decisions were driven by pure cupidity. 他的财务决策完全是由贪婪驱动的。

Greed and cupidity often lead to moral corruption. 贪婪和唯利是图往往会导致道德沦丧。

curator.meaning: n. 馆长，（博物馆、美术馆等的）管理员
curator.note:
The museum curator organized a stunning exhibition of ancient artifacts. 博物馆馆长组织了一场精美的古代文物展览。

She works as a chief curator at the national gallery. 她在国家美术馆担任首席馆长。

curdle.meaning: v. 使凝固，使结块；（血液等）吓得凝固，使惊恐
curdle.note:
Adding lemon juice to milk will cause it to curdle. 在牛奶中加入柠檬汁会导致其凝固。

A sudden scream made her blood curdle in fear. 突然的尖叫声吓得她血液都要凝固了。

curmudgeon.meaning: n. 脾气坏的老头，顽固暴躁的人
curmudgeon.note:
The old man was often dismissed as a grumpy curmudgeon. 老人常常被认为是个脾气暴躁的老头。

Beneath his curmudgeon exterior lay a very kind heart. 在他暴躁的外表下藏着一颗非常善良的心。

curriculum.note:
The school updated its science curriculum to include computer coding. 学校更新了科学课程，将计算机编程纳入其中。

Extracurricular activities are an important part of the school curriculum. 课外活动是学校课程的重要组成部分。

cursory.meaning: adj. 草率的，粗略的，仓促的
cursory.note:
He gave the report only a cursory glance before signing it. 他在签字前只是对报告进行了草草的浏览。

A cursory inspection revealed several major flaws. 粗略的检查揭示了几个主要的缺陷。

curt.meaning: adj. 简慢的，唐突的，生硬的
curt.note:
His curt response indicated that he was not in the mood to talk. 他生硬的回答表明他没有聊天的心情。

She apologized for her curt tone over the phone. 她为自己在电话里的唐突语气道歉。

curtail.note:
We had to curtail our trip due to bad weather. 由于天气不好，我们不得不缩短行程。

New regulations will curtail public spending. 新规定将削减公共开支。

custodian.meaning: n. 管理人，监护人，看守人
custodian.note:
He sees himself as a custodian of the family estate. 他把自己看作是家族庄园的看护人。

Museums act as custodians of our cultural heritage. 博物馆充当着我们文化遗产的守护者。

customary.meaning: adj. 习惯上的，惯常的，合乎习俗的
customary.note:
It is customary to tip the waiter in this country. 在这个国家，给服务员小费是惯例。

She sat in her customary chair by the window. 她坐在窗边她惯常坐的那把椅子上。

cuticle.meaning: n. 表皮，角质层（尤指指甲根部的皮）
cuticle.note:
Be careful not to damage your cuticles when doing a manicure. 做美甲时注意不要损伤指甲根部的表皮。

Plants have a waxy cuticle to prevent water loss. 植物具有蜡质表皮以防止水分流失。

cyclone.meaning: n. 旋风，气旋，热带风暴
cyclone.note:
A severe tropical cyclone struck the coastal region. 一场强烈的热带气旋袭击了沿海地区。

Strong winds and heavy rain accompanied the cyclone. 强风和大雨伴随着这场旋风。

cylinder.note:
The engine has a four-cylinder configuration. 这台发动机采用四缸配置。

The shape of the container is a hollow cylinder. 容器的形状是一个空心圆柱体。

cynic.meaning: n. 认为人皆自私者，悲观主义者，愤世嫉俗者
cynic.note:
He is a cynic who believes no one acts purely out of kindness. 他是一个认为没有人会纯粹出于善意行事的悲观主义者。

Despite the cynics, the project turned out to be a huge success. 尽管有那些愤世嫉俗的人唱反调，该项目最终取得了巨大成功。

cypress.note:
Tall cypress trees lined the entrance to the old villa. 高大的柏树排列在老别墅的入口两侧。

The furniture was made of durable cypress wood. 这套家具是由耐用的柏木制成的。

cytology.note:
She specialized in cytology during her medical studies. 她在医学学习期间专攻细胞学。

Cytology plays a crucial role in cancer detection. 细胞学在癌症检测中起着至关重要的作用。

dabble.meaning: v. 涉猎，浅尝；玩水，溅水
dabble.note:
He likes to dabble in painting during his free time. 他喜欢在空闲时间涉猎绘画。

The children loved to dabble their feet in the cool stream. 孩子们喜欢把脚泡在凉爽的小溪里玩水。

daft.meaning: adj. 愚蠢的，荒唐的；疯狂的
daft.note:
What a daft idea to go hiking without a map. 不带地图去远足真是个荒唐的主意。

Don't pay attention to his daft comments. 别理会他那些愚蠢的评论。

dagger.meaning: n. 短剑，匕首；剑标（排版符号 †）
dagger.note:
The assassin drew a silver dagger from his cloak. 刺客从斗篷里拔出一把银质匕首。

His sharp words felt like daggers to her heart. 他尖锐的话语像匕首一样刺痛了她的心。

daguerreotype.meaning: n. 银版摄影法，银版照片
daguerreotype.note:
The museum displays rare 19th-century daguerreotypes. 博物馆展出了珍贵的19世纪银版照片。

Early photography often relied on the daguerreotype process. 早期的摄影技术通常依赖于银版摄影法。

dainty.meaning: adj. 小巧精致的，娇美的；讲究的，挑剔的 n. 美味佳肴
dainty.note:
She wore a pair of dainty shoes to the party. 她穿着一双小巧精致的鞋子去参加派对。

The tea party featured a selection of sweet dainties. 茶话会上准备了一系列精选的甜美点心。

dally.meaning: v. 虚度光阴，磨蹭；调情，玩弄
dally.note:
We cannot afford to dally if we want to catch the train. 如果我们想赶上火车，就不能再磨蹭了。

He should not dally with her feelings if he isn't serious. 如果他不是认真的，就不该玩弄她的感情。

damp.meaning: adj. 潮湿的，微湿的 n. 潮湿，湿气 v. 使潮湿，抑制
damp.note:
The walls feel damp after the heavy rain. 大雨过后墙壁感觉很潮湿。

Rain can quickly dampen spirits during an outdoor festival. 户外音乐节期间下雨会迅速浇灭人们的热情。

damped.meaning: adj. 阻尼的，减幅的，抑制的
damped.note:
The oscillation was damped by a specialized shock absorber. 振动被一个专门的减震器抑制了。

A damped harmonic motion gradually loses energy over time. 阻尼谐振运动随时间推移逐渐失去能量。

dampen.meaning: v. 使潮湿；使沮丧，泼冷水
dampen.note:
A sudden shower did nothing to dampen our excitement. 一阵突如其来的阵雨并没有减弱我们的兴奋之情。

She used a wet cloth to dampen the fabric. 她用湿布把织物弄潮湿。

dandy.meaning: n. 花花公子，穿着讲究的男子 adj. 极好的，出色的
dandy.note:
He dressed like a dandy in a tailored velvet suit. 他穿着剪裁合体的天鹅绒西装，打扮得像个花花公子。

That sounds like a dandy plan for the weekend. 听起来这真是个周折的好计划。

dapper.meaning: adj. 衣冠楚楚的，整洁利落的
dapper.note:
He looked very dapper in his new tuxedo. 他穿着新礼服，看起来衣冠楚楚。

The dapper gentleman tipped his hat as he passed. 那位衣冠楚楚的绅士路过时行了个脱帽礼。

dappled.note:
Sunlight created a dappled pattern on the forest floor. 阳光在森林地面上形成了斑驳的光影。

A dappled horse stood quietly under the tree. 一匹身上有斑点的马安静地站在树下。

daredevil.meaning: n. 蛮勇的人，喜欢冒险的人 adj. 胆大妄为的，拼命三郎式的
daredevil.note:
The stuntman was known for his daredevil motorcycle jumps. 这名特技演员以其惊险的摩托车飞跃而闻名。

Only a daredevil would attempt such a dangerous climb. 只有不要命的人才会尝试如此危险的攀爬。

dart.meaning: n. 飞镖，标枪；急驰，猛冲 v. 猛冲，飞奔
dart.note:
He threw the dart and hit the bullseye. 他掷出飞镖，正中靶心。

The rabbit gave a quick look and darted into the bushes. 兔子飞快地看了一眼，便钻进了灌木丛。

dawdle.note:
Stop dawdle and get your shoes on right now. 别磨蹭了，现在就去把鞋穿上。

She likes to dawdle in bookstore aisles for hours. 她喜欢在书店的过道里闲逛好几个小时。

deactivate.meaning: v. 使无效，使停止运转，解除激活
deactivate.note:
You can deactivate your account in the settings menu. 你可以在设置菜单中停用你的账户。

Experts were called in to deactivate the unexploded bomb. 专家被请来解除未爆炸炸弹的武装。

deaden.meaning: v. 减弱（声音、感觉等），消除，使麻木
deaden.note:
Heavy curtains helped to deaden the noise from the street. 厚重的窗帘有助于减弱街上的噪音。

The injection was used to deaden the pain in his tooth. 注射用于减轻他牙齿的疼痛。

deadlock.meaning: n. 僵局，僵持 v. 陷入僵局
deadlock.note:
Peace talks reached a deadlock after both sides refused to compromise. 双方拒绝妥协后，和平谈判陷入了僵局。

Negotiations were deadlocked for over a week. 谈判陷入僵局超过了一个星期。

deadpan.meaning: adj. 面无表情的，一本正经的
deadpan.note:
He delivered the funny joke with a completely deadpan expression. 他面无表情地讲了这个有趣的笑话。

Her deadpan humor always takes people a moment to catch. 她那一本正经的幽默总让人需要一会儿才能反应过来。

dealing.meaning: n. 交易，生意往来；处理方式
dealing.note:
The company has business dealings with international firms. 这家公司与国际企业有业务往来。

We must ensure honesty in all our financial dealings. 我们必须确保所有金融交易的诚实度。

debacle.note:
The product launch turned out to be a complete debacle. 这款产品的发布最终成了一场彻底的惨败。

Historians analyzed the causes of the military debacle. 历史学家分析了军事惨败的原因。

debark.note:
Passengers began to debark once the ship docked. 船停靠后，乘客们开始下船。

Troops prepared to debark on the hostile shore. 部队准备在敌对海岸登陆。

debase.meaning: v. 降低（品质、价值等），贬低，使堕落
debase.note:
Corruption tends to debase the political system. 腐败往往会腐蚀政治体制。

Printing too much money can debase the currency. 印制过多货币会贬低货币价值。

debate.meaning: n. 辩论，讨论 v. 辩论，仔细考虑
debate.note:
The parliament held a heated debate on healthcare reform. 议会对医疗改革展开了激烈的辩论。

I am still debating whether to accept the job offer. 我仍在考虑是否接受这份工作邀请。

debilitate.meaning: v. 使虚弱，削弱（体力或势力）
debilitate.note:
The long illness left him completely debilitated. 长期生病使他彻底虚弱了。

A debilitating disease prevented her from traveling. 一种令人衰弱的疾病使她无法旅行。

debouch.meaning: v. 从狭窄处流出（或涌出），走出
debouch.note:
The narrow path finally debouched onto a wide plain. 那条小路最终通向了一个开阔的平原。

Crowds debouched from the subway station. 人群从地铁站里涌了出来。

debunk.meaning: v. 揭穿，揭露（虚假观点、神话等），驳斥
debunk.note:
Science aims to debunk common misconceptions. 科学旨在揭穿常见的误解。

The scientist easily debunked the urban legend. 这位科学家轻松地驳斥了那个都市传说。

decadence.note:
Critics accused modern society of sliding into decadence. 批评家指责现代社会正在滑向颓废。

They lived a life of luxury and moral decadence. 他们过着奢华且道德堕落的生活。

deceit.note:
His whole business empire was built on a web of deceit. 他整个商业帝国都是建立在谎言与欺骗之上的。

She achieved her goals through cunning deceit. 她通过狡猾的欺骗达到了目的。

decency.meaning: n. 得体，正派，规范行为
decency.note:
He didn't even have the decency to apologize. 他甚至没有体面到说声道歉。

Basic human decency requires us to help those in need. 基本的人性尊严要求我们帮助那些需要帮助的人。

decibel.meaning: n. 分贝（声音响度单位）
decibel.note:
The noise level at the concert exceeded one hundred decibels. 音乐会的噪音水平超过了一百分贝。

Prolonged exposure to high decibel sounds can cause hearing loss. 长期暴露在高分贝声音中会导致听力丧失。

deciduous.meaning: adj. 落叶的（非常绿的），脱落性的
deciduous.note:
Oak and maple are common deciduous trees. 橡树和枫树是常见的落叶树。

Deciduous forests look entirely different in autumn. 落叶林在秋天呈现出完全不同的景色。

decimate.meaning: v. 大批杀害，严重破坏，削减
decimate.note:
The pest outbreak threatened to decimate the local crops. 害虫的爆发威胁要摧毁当地的大部分庄稼。

Disease decimated the animal population in the valley. 疾病使山谷里的动物数量锐减。

declaim.meaning: v. 高声朗诵，慷慨激昂地演讲
declaim.note:
The actor stood on stage and began to declaim Shakespeare. 演员站在舞台上，开始高声朗诵莎士比亚的作品。

He liked to declaim against the injustices of society. 他喜欢慷慨激昂地抨击社会的不公。

declamation.meaning: n. 慷慨激昂的演说，高声朗诵
declamation.note:
His speech sounded more like an empty declamation than policy. 他的演讲听起来更像是一场空洞的演说，而不是政策阐述。

She practiced her poetic declamation before the contest. 她在比赛前练习了她的诗歌朗诵。

decline.meaning: v. 下降，衰退，谢绝 n. 下降，衰落
decline.note:
Economic growth began to decline in the second quarter. 经济增长在第二季度开始下降。

I had to decline his invitation due to a prior commitment. 由于已有安排，我只好谢绝了他的邀请。

decode.note:
Intelligence agents worked quickly to decode the intercepted message. 情报特工迅速破获了截获的信息。

It can be difficult to decode complex body language. 破译复杂的肢体语言可能会很困难。

decompose.meaning: v. 分解，腐烂，使（化合物等）分解
decompose.note:
Organic waste will naturally decompose in a compost bin. 有机废物会在堆肥箱中自然分解。

Microorganisms help to decompose dead plant matter. 微生物有助于分解死去的植物物质。

decomposition.note:
Scientists studied the chemical decomposition of the material. 科学家研究了该材料的化学分解过程。

The process of decomposition releases nutrients back into the soil. 分解过程将养分释放回土壤中。

decorum.note:
Students are expected to maintain strict decorum in the library. 学生在图书馆里必须保持严格的安静与端庄。

She handled the awkward situation with great decorum. 她以极大的得体处理了那个尴尬的局面。

decrepit.meaning: adj. 破旧的，衰老的，破烂不堪的
decrepit.note:
They lived in a decrepit house on the edge of town. 他们住在镇边缘一栋破旧的房子里。

The old bridge was too decrepit to carry heavy traffic. 那座老桥年久失修，无法承载重型交通。

decry.meaning: v. 公开谴责，强烈反对，贬低
decry.note:
Leaders came together to decry the acts of violence. 各国领导人聚集在一起谴责暴力行为。

Critics decry the commercialization of modern art. 批评家强烈反对现代艺术的商业化。

deduce.note:
From these facts, we can deduce that the plan will work. 从这些事实中，我们可以推断这个计划会成功。

Detectives tried to deduce the suspect's movements. 侦探们试图推断嫌疑人的行动轨迹。

deductive.note:
Sherlock Holmes is famous for his brilliant deductive reasoning. 夏洛克·福尔摩斯以其出色的演绎推理而闻名。

Deductive logic moves from general principles to specific conclusions. 演绎逻辑从一般原则推导到具体结论。

deed.meaning: n. 行为，功绩；契约，房契
deed.note:
Good deeds often bring unexpected happiness. 善行往往会带来意想不到的快乐。

She signed the deed to transfer ownership of the property. 她签署了契约以转让该房产的所有权。

deface.meaning: v. 损坏外貌，污损，涂画
deface.note:
Vandals tried to deface the public monument with graffiti. 蓄意破坏者试图用涂鸦污损公共纪念碑。

It is illegal to deface paper currency. 损坏纸币是违法的。

defeatist.meaning: adj. 失败主义的 n. 失败主义者
defeatist.note:
We must not adopt a defeatist attitude before the match begins. 在比赛开始前，我们绝不能采取失败主义态度。

He was labeled a defeatist for suggesting they surrender early. 因为建议早点投降，他被贴上了失败主义者的标签。

defendant.note:
The defendant pleaded not guilty to all charges. 被告对所有指控均表示不认罪。

His lawyer advised the defendant to remain silent. 他的律师建议被告保持沉默。

defer.meaning: v. 推迟，延期；听从，顺从
defer.note:
The committee decided to defer the decision until next week. 委员会决定将该决定推迟到下周。

I will defer to your better judgment on this matter. 在这件事上我听从你更高明的判断。

deferential.meaning: adj. 恭顺的，表现出敬意的
deferential.note:
The young employee was very deferential to his boss. 这名年轻员工对他的老板非常恭顺。

She spoke in a quiet, deferential tone. 她用安静、恭敬的语气说话。

defile.meaning: v. 污损，玷污，弄脏 n. 狭窄通道，山峡
defile.note:
Pollution can defile pristine natural environments. 污染会玷污原始的自然环境。

The army marched carefully through the mountain defile. 军队小心翼翼地穿过山间峡谷。

defined.note:
The project has a well-defined scope and timeline. 该项目有明确的范围和时间表。

Muscles became more defined after weeks of training. 经过几周的训练，肌肉线条变得更清晰了。

definite.meaning: adj. 确切的，肯定的，明确的
definite.note:
We need a definite answer by tomorrow morning. 我们需要在明天早上前得到一个确切的答案。

There is no definite proof that he was involved. 没有确切的证据表明他牵涉其中。

definition.note:
Please give me a clear definition of the term. 请给我这个术语下一个清晰的定义。

The new camera offers incredible image definition. 这款新相机提供了令人难以置信的图像清晰度。

deflated.meaning: adj. 气馁的，泄气的；（气球等）气放掉的
deflated.note:
He felt completely deflated after receiving the rejection letter. 收到拒绝信后，他感到彻底泄气了。

We found a deflated football on the playground. 我们在操场上发现了一个瘪了的足球。

deflect.meaning: v. 偏离，使转向，转移（注意力等）
deflect.note:
The shield was able to deflect the incoming projectile. 盾牌能够挡开飞来的抛射物。

She tried to deflect criticism by changing the subject. 她试图通过转移话题来避开批评。

defoliator.meaning: n. 脱叶剂，落叶剂（常用于清除植物叶子的化学物质或昆虫）
defoliator.note:
Chemical defoliants were widely used in past conflicts. 化学落叶剂在过去的冲突中曾被广泛使用。

Certain caterpillars act as natural defoliators in the forest. 某些毛虫在森林中充当自然的落叶催化者。

deforestation.meaning: n. 森林砍伐，森林破坏
deforestation.note:
Rapid deforestation has threatened many wildlife species. 快速的森林砍伐威胁到了许多野生动物物种。

Governments are taking measures to combat illegal deforestation. 政府正在采取措施打击非法的森林砍伐。

defraud.note:
He was convicted of trying to defraud the tax office. 他因试图诈骗税务局而被定罪。

The scheme was designed to defraud vulnerable investors. 该计划旨在欺骗脆弱的投资者。

defuse.meaning: v. 拆除（炸弹引信），缓和（紧张局势）
defuse.note:
Diplomats worked frantically to defuse the brewing crisis. 外交官们拼命工作以缓和酝酿中的危机。

Police managed to defuse the bomb safely. 警察设法安全拆除了炸弹。

dehydrate.note:
Athletes must drink plenty of water to avoid becoming dehydrated. 运动员必须喝大量的水以避免脱水。

Sunlight and wind can quickly dehydrate fruit. 阳光和风可以迅速使水果脱水。

deify.note:
Some ancient cultures used to deify their rulers. 一些古代文化曾将他们的统治者神化。

Media often tends to deify celebrities. 媒体往往倾向于将名人神化。

deign.note:
He didn't even deign to answer my question. 他甚至不屑于回答我的问题。

She finally deigned to notice the crowd waiting outside. 她终于屈尊注意到外面等待的人群。

dejected.note:
The players walked off the field looking deeply dejected. 球员们沮丧地走下了球场。

She looked dejected after failing her driving test. 没通过驾考后，她显得很沮丧。

delectable.meaning: adj. 美味的，令人愉悦的
delectable.note:
The chef prepared a delectable array of desserts. 厨师准备了一系列美味的甜点。

The aroma of delectable food filled the kitchen. 美味食物的香气弥漫了整个厨房。

delicacy.meaning: n. 佳肴，美味；（处理时的）微妙，精细
delicacy.note:
Caviar is considered a rare and expensive delicacy. 鱼子酱被认为是一种罕见且昂贵的美味佳肴。

The situation requires extreme tact and delicacy. 这种情况需要极大的机智与微妙的处理。

delimit.note:
A fence was built to delimit the property boundaries. 建起了一道栅栏来划定财产界限。

It is important to delimit the scope of the investigation. 界定调查范围是很重要的。

delinquency.meaning: n. 青少年犯罪，失职，违法行为
delinquency.note:
Community programs aim to reduce youth delinquency. 社区项目的目标是减少青少年犯罪。

The company faced issues related to financial delinquency. 该公司面临与财务违约相关的问题。

delinquent.meaning: adj. 青少年犯罪的，拖欠债务的 n. 违法者，犯法青年
delinquent.note:
Juvenile delinquents are often offered counseling and support. 青少年违法者通常会得到心理咨询和支持。

He received a warning notice for delinquent payments. 他因拖欠付款收到了一份警告通知。

delirious.meaning: adj. 神志不清的，说胡话的；极度兴奋的
delirious.note:
High fever left the patient delirious. 高烧导致患者神志不清。

Fans were delirious with joy after the team won the championship. 球队赢得冠军后，球迷们欣喜若狂。

delirium.meaning: n. 谵妄，精神错乱；极度兴奋
delirium.note:
The infection caused a state of temporary delirium in the elderly man. 感染导致这位老人在一段时间内处于谵妄状态。

The stadium erupted in a delirium of excitement. 体育场爆发出狂热的兴奋状态。

delta.meaning: n. （河流的）三角洲；希腊字母的第四个字母（Δ）
delta.note:
The Nile Delta is one of the most fertile regions in the world. 尼罗河三角洲是世界上最肥沃的地区之一。

Data scientists use the symbol delta to represent change. 数据科学家用德尔塔符号来表示变化。

delude.note:
Don't delude yourself into thinking it will be easy. 不要自欺欺人地认为这会很简单。

He managed to delude investors with false promises. 他设法用虚假的承诺欺骗了投资者。

deluge.meaning: n. 暴雨，洪水；大量涌现的事物 v. 泛滥，使应接不暇
deluge.note:
A sudden deluge flooded the downtown streets. 一场突如其来的暴雨淹没了市中心的街道。

The office was deluged with applications after the ad ran. 广告刊登后，办公室涌入了大量申请。

demagogue.note:
The politician was dismissed as a dangerous demagogue. 那名政客被斥为一个危险的煽动家。

History shows how easily a demagogue can manipulate the masses. 历史表明煽动政客操纵大众是多么容易。

demanding.meaning: adj. 苛求的，要求高的，费力的
demanding.note:
Being a surgeon is a highly demanding profession. 外科医生是一个要求极高的职业。

She found the hiking trail physically demanding. 她发现这条远足小路对体力要求很高。

demean.note:
He felt that doing menial tasks would demean him. 他觉得做低下的杂务会贬低自己的身份。

She refused to accept such demeaning treatment. 她拒绝接受这种带有贬低性质的对待。

demography.meaning: n. 人口统计学，人口学
demography.note:
Demography studies changes in human population size and structure. 人口统计学研究人类群体规模和结构的变化。

Changes in demographics affect housing markets. 人口统计特征的变化会影响房地产市场。

demolition.note:
The old factory is scheduled for demolition next month. 那座老工厂计划在下个月被拆除。

Debris flew everywhere during the controlled demolition. 在爆破拆除过程中，碎片到处飞溅。

demonstrate.meaning: v. 证明，示范；游行示威
demonstrate.note:
The teacher will demonstrate how to solve the math equation. 老师会示范如何解这个数学方程。

Workers gathered to demonstrate against low wages. 工人们聚集在一起抗议低工资。

demonstrative.meaning: adj. 感情外露的，喜怒形于色的；指示的
demonstrative.note:
His family is very warm and demonstrative. 他的家庭非常热情且感情外露。

Words like 'this' and 'that' are demonstrative pronouns. 诸如“这个”和“那个”之类的词是指示代词。

demoralize.meaning: v. 使泄气，使士气低落
demoralize.note:
Repeated defeats can severely demoralize a team. 连续的失败会严重打击团队的士气。

They felt completely demoralized by the unexpected news. 突如其来的消息让他们感到彻底泄气。

demote.note:
He was demoted to a lower position due to poor performance. 由于表现不佳，他被降职到了较低的岗位。

Demotion can be a hard pill to swallow for ambitious employees. 对于有上进心的员工来说，降职是一个很难接受的现实。

demotic.meaning: adj. 通俗的，大众化的，日常语言的
demotic.note:
The text was written in demotic Greek rather than classical style. 这篇文章是用大众希腊语而非古典风格写的。

He preferred using demotic expressions in his writing. 他更喜欢在写作中使用通俗的表达方式。

demur.meaning: v. 反对，面露异议 n. 异议，反对
demur.note:
She accepted the task without a moment of demur. 她没有丝毫异议地接受了这项任务。

He demurred at the suggestion to work overtime on Sunday. 他对周日加班的建议提出了异议。

demystify.meaning: v. 使神秘感消失，阐明，揭开谜底
demystify.note:
The book aims to demystify the complex world of finance. 这本书旨在揭开复杂金融世界的神秘面纱。

A good teacher can demystify difficult concepts for students. 一个好的老师能为学生把困难的概念讲明白。

denigrate.note:
You should not denigrate other people's hard work. 你不应该贬低其他人的辛勤工作。

She felt hurt when her colleagues tried to denigrate her ideas. 当同事们试图诋毁她的想法时，她感到很受伤。

denim.meaning: n. 牛仔布，粗斜纹棉布
denim.note:
He wore a classic blue denim jacket. 他穿着一件经典的蓝色牛仔夹克。

Denim is known for its durability and comfort. 牛仔布以其耐用和舒适而闻名。

denizen.meaning: n. 居民，（某地的）动物或植物
denizen.note:
Fish are denizens of the deep ocean. 鱼类是深海的居民。

Local denizens gathered in the square for the festival. 当地的居民聚集在广场上庆祝节日。

denomination.meaning: n. 宗派，教派；（货币的）面额
denomination.note:
People of various religious denominations attended the conference. 来自不同宗教教派的人士出席了会议。

The ATM machine dispenses bank notes of different denominations. 自动取款机分发不同面额的纸币。

denote.note:
A red traffic light is used to denote stop. 红色的交通灯用于表示停车。

Her facial expression seemed to denote anxiety. 她的面部表情似乎预示着焦虑。

denouement.meaning: n. （小说、戏剧等的）结局，收场
denouement.note:
The mystery novel had an unexpected and thrilling denouement. 这部悬疑小说有一个出人意料且惊心动魄的结局。

Everyone waited eagerly for the final denouement of the play. 每个人都在热切等待这出戏的最终大结局。

dent.meaning: n. 凹痕，凹陷 v. 使凹陷，打击
dent.note:
A stray ball left a deep dent in the car door. 一个飞来的球在车门上留下了一个深凹痕。

The scandal did little to dent his political career. 这桩丑闻几乎没有动摇他的政治生涯。

denture.note:
He takes out his dentures every night before going to bed. 他每天晚上睡觉前都会把假牙取下来。

Proper care is essential to keep dentures clean. 正确的护理对于保持假牙清洁至关重要。

denude.meaning: v. 剥夺，使裸露，剥去（覆盖物）
denude.note:
Strong winds can denude trees of their leaves. 强风会把树木的叶子剥落干净。

Uncontrolled logging will denude the hillsides. 无节制的伐木会使山坡变得光秃秃的。

denunciation.note:
The speech was a fierce denunciation of government corruption. 这篇演讲是对政府腐败的猛烈抨击。

He issued a public denunciation of the treaty. 他发表了对该条约的公开谴责。

deplore.note:
We all deplore the loss of innocent lives in the conflict. 我们都对冲突中无辜生命的丧失深感痛心。

She strongly deplored the lack of safety measures. 她强烈谴责缺乏安全措施的做法。

depose.meaning: v. 罢免，废黜（君主等）；作证宣誓
depose.note:
The dictator was eventually deposed by a military coup. 独裁者最终被一场军事政变废黜。

The witness agreed to depose before the court. 证人同意在法庭前作证宣誓。

deposition.meaning: n. 罢免，废黜；宣誓证言；沉积
deposition.note:
The king's deposition led to a civil war. 国王的被废黜引发了一场内战。

Lawyers recorded the witness's deposition in advance. 律师提前录下了证人的宣誓证言。

depraved.meaning: adj. 堕落的，邪恶的，腐化的
depraved.note:
He was convicted of committing depraved acts against society. 他因犯下危害社会的邪恶罪行而被定罪。

The detective was shocked by the criminal's depraved mind. 侦探对罪犯堕落的心理感到震惊。

depravity.meaning: n. 堕落，道德败坏，腐败
depravity.note:
The trial exposed a shocking level of moral depravity. 审判暴露了令人震惊的道德堕落程度。

Living on the streets can expose people to deep depravity. 街头生活可能会使人陷入极度的堕落中。

deprecate.note:
He tended to deprecate his own achievements. 他往往会贬低自己的成就。

Experts deprecate the use of outdated medical practices. 专家反对使用过时的医疗实践。

depreciate.note:
New cars tend to depreciate quickly in their first year. 新车在第一年往往会迅速贬值。

Real estate generally does not depreciate as fast as technology. 房地产通常不像科技那样贬值得快。

depressed.meaning: adj. 沮丧的，患抑郁症的；萧条的
depressed.note:
She felt depressed after facing a series of failures. 在遭遇一连串失败后，她感到十分沮丧。

The economic downturn left many local businesses in a depressed state. 经济低迷使许多当地企业陷入了萧条状态。

depression.meaning: n. 抑郁症；经济萧条；凹地
depression.note:
He sought professional help to cope with his severe depression. 他寻求专业帮助来应对他的严重抑郁症。

The global economic depression lasted for several years. 全球经济大萧条持续了好几年。

deprivation.note:
Sleep deprivation can seriously affect cognitive function. 睡眠剥夺会严重影响认知功能。

Many families suffered extreme hardship and deprivation during the war. 许多家庭在战争期间经受了极端的艰难困苦和匮乏。

deracinate.meaning: v. 根除，使脱离根基，使流离失所
deracinate.note:
War can deracinate thousands of innocent citizens. 战争会使数千名无辜公民流离失所。

Immigrants often struggle not to feel deracinated in a new country. 移民常常挣扎着不在新国家感到根基尽失。

deranged.meaning: adj. 精神错乱的，疯狂的
deranged.note:
The suspect appeared mentally deranged during the interrogation. 嫌疑人在审讯期间显得精神错乱。

Her mind was deranged by grief and trauma. 她的心灵因悲伤和精神创伤而错乱了。

dereliction.meaning: n. 玩忽职守，疏忽；荒废
dereliction.note:
He was fired for gross dereliction of duty. 他因严重玩忽职守而被解雇。

The dereliction of the old industrial site attracted vandals. 旧工业用地的荒废吸引了蓄意破坏者。

deride.note:
Critics derided his new proposal as completely impractical. 批评家嘲笑他的新提议完全不切实际。

She was derided by her peers for her unusual ideas. 她因不寻常的想法而遭到同龄人的嘲笑。

derivation.note:
Etymologists study the derivation of English words. 词源学家研究英语单词的词源。

The scientist traced the derivation of the experimental drug. 科学家追溯了这种实验药物的来源。

dermatologist.note:
She consulted a dermatologist about her persistent skin rash. 她就自己持续不断的皮疹咨询了一位皮肤科医生。

A dermatologist can recommend the best skincare routine. 皮肤科医生可以推荐最佳的护肤流程。

derogate.meaning: v. 贬低，减损（尊严或权利）
derogate.note:
Such actions tend to derogate from his professional reputation. 这种行为往往会损害他的职业声誉。

Nothing in this agreement should derogate from statutory rights. 本协议中的任何内容均不得减损法定权利。

derogatory.meaning: adj. 贬损的，侮辱性的，批评的
derogatory.note:
He made derogatory comments about her background. 他对她的背景发表了贬损的评论。

Company policy prohibits derogatory remarks among colleagues. 公司政策禁止同事之间出现侮辱性言论。

descry.note:
Through the thick fog, they could barely descry the shoreline. 通过浓雾，他们勉强能隐约看到海岸线。

She looked through the telescope and descried a distant ship. 她透过望远镜隐约看到了一艘远处的船。

desecrate.meaning: v. 亵渎，玷污（神圣事物）
desecrate.note:
The vandals tried to desecrate the ancient temple. 那些破坏者试图亵渎那座古老的寺庙。

To desecrate a war memorial is a serious crime. 亵渎战争纪念碑是一项严重的罪行。

deserted.meaning: adj. 荒芜的，废弃的，空无一人的
deserted.note:
The streets were completely deserted late at night. 深夜时分街道上空无一人。

They explored a deserted village in the mountains. 他们探索了山里的一座荒废村庄。

deserter.note:
The army caught the deserter near the border. 军队在边境附近抓获了那个逃兵。

He was branded as a deserter after fleeing the front line. 在逃离前线后，他被烙上了逃兵的烙印。

desiccate.meaning: v. 使脱水，使干燥；使枯竭
desiccate.note:
Hot desert winds can quickly desiccate vegetation. 炎热的沙漠风会迅速使植被枯竭。

Desiccated coconut is often used in baking. 椰丝常用于烘焙。

designation.meaning: n. 称号，名称；指定，委派
designation.note:
The region received official designation as a national park. 该地区获得了作为国家公园的官方称号。

His official job designation is senior project manager. 他的官方职位名称是高级项目经理。

designer.meaning: n. 设计师，设计者 adj. 设计师品牌的
designer.note:
She works as a fashion designer for a major clothing brand. 她是一家大型服装品牌的时装设计师。

He likes to wear expensive designer suits. 他喜欢穿昂贵的设计师品牌西装。

despicable.note:
Stealing from charity is a truly despicable act. 从慈善机构偷窃是一种真正卑鄙的行为。

His despicable behavior shocked everyone in the room. 他卑鄙的行为震惊了房间里的所有人。

despise.note:
She tends to despise people who are dishonest. 她往往会看不起不诚实的人。

He grew to despise the corrupt political system. 他渐渐鄙视起那个腐败的政治体制。

despondent.meaning: adj. 沮丧的，失望的，绝望的
despondent.note:
He became deeply despondent after losing his job. 失业后他变得极其沮丧。

She looked despondent when her project was rejected. 当她的项目被拒绝时，她显得很失望。

despot.note:
The brutal despot ruled the country with an iron fist. 那个残暴的暴君以铁腕统治着国家。

Citizens fought hard to overthrow the cruel despot. 公民们奋力推翻那个残酷的独裁者。

despotic.note:
The population suffered under a despotic regime for decades. 人口在专制政权下受苦了几十年。

They protested against the despotic laws. 他们抗议那些专制的法律。

despotism.note:
The revolution aimed to replace despotism with democracy. 革命旨在用民主取代专制统治。

History is full of examples of the fall of despotism. 历史充满了专制统治崩溃的例子。

destitution.note:
The economic crisis drove thousands of families into utter destitution. 经济危机将数千个家庭推入了彻底的赤贫之中。

Charity organizations work to lift people out of destitution. 慈善组织致力于将人们从极端贫困中解救出来。

desultory.meaning: adj. 散漫的，草率的，无系统的
desultory.note:
They had a desultory conversation while waiting for the bus. 等公交车时，他们进行了一次随意的交谈。

His desultory efforts yielded no meaningful results. 他散漫的努力没有产生任何有意义的结果。

detach.note:
You can detach the keyboard from the tablet screen. 你可以把键盘从平板屏幕上拆下来。

Please detach the coupon and mail it back. 请把优惠券撕下来并寄回。

detached.meaning: adj. 超然的，冷漠的；独立的（房屋）
detached.note:
She maintained a cool, detached attitude toward the drama. 她对这场闹剧保持着冷漠、超然的态度。

They live in a quiet, detached house in the suburbs. 他们住在郊区一栋安静的独立房屋里。

deter.note:
High walls are meant to deter potential intruders. 高墙旨在威慑潜在的入侵者。

Bad weather did not deter them from climbing the mountain. 恶劣的天气并没有阻止他们爬山。

deterioration.note:
Doctors noted a sudden deterioration in his health. 医生注意到他的健康状况突然恶化。

Air pollution causes the rapid deterioration of stone buildings. 空气污染导致石制建筑迅速老化。

determination.meaning: n. 决心，果断；测定，确定
determination.note:
With fierce determination, she completed the marathon. 凭借坚定的决心，她跑完了马拉松。

The precise determination of the chemical structure took months. 化学结构的精确测定花了好几个月。

detest.note:
I completely detest dishonesty in relationships. 我极其厌恶感情中的不诚实。

She detests waking up early on cold mornings. 她讨厌在寒冷的早晨早起。

detonation.note:
Experts prepared for the controlled detonation of the explosive. 专家们准备对炸药进行受控引爆。

The loud detonation shook the windows of nearby houses. 巨大的爆炸声震动了附近房屋的窗户。

detraction.note:
Her achievements are beyond the reach of cheap detraction. 她的成就是卑劣的诽谤无法触及的。

He made his comments without any malicious detraction. 他的评论没有任何恶意的诋毁。

detritus.note:
The storm left a mess of plastic detritus on the beach. 风暴在海滩上留下一堆塑料碎屑。

Workers cleared away the detritus after the concert. 音乐会结束后，工人们清理了残余的垃圾。

deviant.meaning: adj. 异常的，偏离常规的 n. 偏离常轨者
deviant.note:
The study analyzed deviant behavior in teenagers. 这项研究分析了青少年的异常行为。

Society tends to ostracize those considered social deviants. 社会往往会排斥那些被认为是社会另类的人。

deviate.note:
You should not deviate from the approved flight plan. 你不应该背离已批准的飞行计划。

Drivers must not deviate from traffic regulations. 司机不得违反交通法规。

devious.meaning: adj. 狡猾的，不正直的；曲折的
devious.note:
He used devious methods to achieve his career goals. 他用狡猾的手段达到了自己的职业目标。

They traveled along a devious mountain path. 他们沿着一条曲折的山路前行。

devoid.note:
His speech was completely devoid of any real substance. 他的演讲完全缺乏任何实质内容。

The room felt cold and devoid of human warmth. 房间里感觉冷冰冰的，缺乏人情味。

devoted.meaning: adj. 忠诚的，深爱的，投入的
devoted.note:
She is a devoted mother who puts her children first. 她是一个把孩子放在第一位的慈爱母亲。

He remained devoted to his research throughout his life. 他一生都致力于自己的研究。

devotee.meaning: n. 爱好者，狂热追随者，信徒
devotee.note:
He is a devoted devotee of classical music. 他是古典音乐的狂热爱好者。

Art devotees gathered for the gallery opening. 艺术爱好者们聚集在一起参加美术馆的开幕式。

devotional.meaning: adj. 献给神的，宗教崇拜的，虔诚的
devotional.note:
The choir sang traditional devotional songs during the service. 唱诗班在礼拜期间唱了传统的宗教赞美诗。

She starts her day with personal devotional reading. 她以个人灵修阅读开始新的一天。

devour.meaning: v. 吞食，狼吞虎咽；吞没，热切地阅读
devour.note:
The hungry wolf quickly began to devour its prey. 饿狼迅速开始吞食它的猎物。

She loves to devour mystery novels in a single weekend. 她喜欢在单个周末里津津有味地读完悬疑小说。

devout.meaning: adj. 虔诚的，笃信宗教的；深切的
devout.note:
They are a devout family who attend church every Sunday. 他们是一个每个星期天都去教堂的虔诚家庭。

It is my devout wish that peace will soon return. 我深切的愿望是和平能很快回归。

dexterity.note:
Playing the piano requires finger dexterity. 弹钢琴需要手指的灵活性。

He handled the delicate negotiation with great diplomatic dexterity. 他以极高的外交机敏处理了这场微妙的谈判。

dexterous.note:
The craftsman made intricate carvings with dexterous hands. 工匠用灵巧的双手做出了复杂的雕刻。

She is a dexterous writer who handles complex plots easily. 她是一位熟练的作家，能轻松驾驭复杂的剧情。

diabolical.meaning: adj. 恶魔般的，极其残忍的；极坏的
diabolical.note:
The villain hatched a diabolical plot to take over the city. 那个反派策划了一个夺取城市的恶魔般阴谋。

The weather today is absolutely diabolical. 今天的糟糕天气简直坏透了。

dialect.note:
People in this rural region speak a distinct local dialect. 这个乡村地区的人们说着一种独特的本地方言。

Linguists study how a dialect changes over generations. 语言学家研究方言如何在世代间发生变化。

diaphanous.note:
She wore a dress made of light, diaphanous silk. 她穿着一件用轻薄透明丝绸做成的裙子。

Diaphanous curtains allowed the morning sunlight to filter through. 轻透的窗帘让晨光透过。

diatribe.meaning: n. 抨击，痛斥，长篇指责
diatribe.note:
The newspaper published a bitter diatribe against the new tax policy. 报纸发表了一篇针对新税收政策的尖锐抨击文章。

He launched into a long diatribe about modern culture. 他发起了关于现代文化的一场长篇指责。

didactic.note:
The novel was criticized for being too didactic and preachy. 这部小说因过于说教和好为人师而受到批评。

Her plays often combine entertainment with a didactic message. 她的戏剧经常将娱乐性与说教性的信息结合起来。

diehard.meaning: n. 顽固保守分子，死忠粉 adj. 顽固的，死不改悔的
diehard.note:
He remains a diehard supporter of the local football club. 他依然是当地足球俱乐部的死忠球迷。

Diehard habits are hard to break. 顽固的习惯很难打破。

diffident.meaning: adj. 羞怯的，缺乏自信的
diffident.note:
Despite her talent, she remained shy and diffident. 尽管她很有才华，但她依然害羞且缺乏自信。

He gave a diffident smile when praised for his work. 当因工作受到表扬时，他露出了一个羞怯的微笑。

diffuse.meaning: adj. 散开的，弥漫的；冗长的 v. 扩散，传播
diffuse.note:
The lampshade helped to diffuse the harsh light. 灯罩有助于使刺眼的光线变柔和漫射开来。

His writing style is often considered too diffuse. 他的写作风格常被认为过于冗长。

digestion.note:
Eating heavy meals late at night can disrupt digestion. 深夜吃大餐会打乱消化过程。

Walking after a meal is believed to aid digestion. 人们认为饭后散步有助于消化。

digit.note:
The password must contain at least six digits. 密码必须包含至少六位数字。

Primates have five digits on each hand and foot. 灵长类动物每只手和脚都有五个指（趾）。

digress.note:
Let me digress for a moment to tell you a short story. 请允许我离题一会儿，给你们讲个短故事。

The speaker tended to digress during his lengthy lectures. 演讲者在他的冗长讲座中往往会偏离主题。

digression.meaning: n. 离题，偏离主题的话
digression.note:
After a brief digression, the professor returned to the main topic. 经过短暂的离题后，教授回到了主题。

His speech was full of interesting historical digressions. 他的演讲充满了有趣的解题历史插曲。

dilapidate.note:
Years of neglect can dilapidate even the finest buildings. 多年的荒废甚至能使最精美的建筑破败不堪。

The harsh climate helped to dilapidate the structure. 恶劣的气候导致该建筑逐渐残破。

dilapidated.meaning: adj. 破旧的，荒废的，倒塌半坏的
dilapidated.note:
They lived in a dilapidated farmhouse on the hill. 他们住在山上一栋破旧的农舍里。

The city council planned to renovate the dilapidated warehouse. 市议会计划翻修那个破旧的仓库。

dilettante.meaning: n. 业余爱好者，浅尝辄止者
dilettante.note:
He was dismissed as a mere dilettante in the world of art. 他在艺术界被认为只是个业余爱好者。

She explored various hobbies without ever becoming a professional, like a true dilettante. 她探索了各种爱好却从未成为专业人士，就像一个真正的业余爱好者。

diligence.note:
With hard work and diligence, she passed the exam. 凭借努力和勤勉，她通过了考试。

Due diligence is required before signing the contract. 在签署合同前需要进行尽职调查。

dilute.meaning: v. 稀释，冲淡 adj. 稀释的
dilute.note:
You should dilute the juice with water before drinking. 喝之前你应该用水把果汁稀释一下。

The company issued more shares, which served to dilute the stock value. 公司发行了更多股票，这起到了稀释股票价值的作用。

diminution.note:
There has been a noticeable diminution in crime rates. 犯罪率有了明显的下降。

The company faced a sudden diminution of profits. 公司面临利润的突然缩减。

dimple.meaning: n. 酒窝，笑靥 v. 现酒窝
dimple.note:
She has a charming dimple on her left cheek. 她的左脸颊上有一个迷人的酒窝。

A light breeze caused the surface of the lake to dimple. 微风使湖面泛起了涟漪般的微凹。

din.meaning: n. 喧闹声，嘈杂声 v. 喋喋不休地灌输
din.note:
We had to shout to make ourselves heard above the traffic din. 我们不得不大喊大叫，以便在交通噪音中让别人听见。

The constant noise created an unbearable din. 持续的噪音制造了令人难以忍受的喧嚣。

dingy.meaning: adj. 肮脏的，褪色的，昏暗的
dingy.note:
They stayed in a dingy hotel room near the station. 他们住在车站附近一个肮脏昏暗的酒店房间里。

The walls of the office were painted a dingy gray. 办公室的墙壁被刷成了暗淡无光的灰色。

dire.meaning: adj. 可怕的，极端的，危急的
dire.note:
The refugees are in dire need of food and medical supplies. 难民们极度需要食物和医疗物资。

Warnings were issued about the dire consequences of climate change. 有关气候变化可怕后果的警告已经发出。

dirge.note:
A slow, melancholy dirge was played at the funeral. 葬礼上奏起了缓慢而忧伤的挽歌。

The sad song sounded like a funeral dirge. 那首悲伤的歌听起来像是一首葬礼哀乐。

disabuse.meaning: v. 打消（某人的）错误想法，使醒悟
disabuse.note:
Let me disabuse you of the notion that it will be easy. 让我来打破你认为这会很简单的不切实际的想法吧。

She tried to disabuse him of his false beliefs. 她试图纠正他错误的信念。

disaffect.note:
Poor management can quickly disaffected the workforce. 管理不善会迅速引起员工的不满。

Disaffected citizens took to the streets to protest. 对现状不满的市民走上街头抗议。

disagreeable.meaning: adj. 令人讨厌的，不愉快的，脾气坏的
disagreeable.note:
He had a disagreeable habit of interrupting others. 他有一个打断别人说话的令人讨厌的习惯。

The medicine had a rather disagreeable taste. 这药有一种相当难喝的味道。

disarm.meaning: v. 解除武装，缴械；消除（敌意等）
disarm.note:
The country agreed to disarm under the international treaty. 该国同意根据国际条约解除武装。

Her warm smile managed to disarm his anger. 她温暖的微笑设法化解了他的愤怒。

disarray.meaning: n. 混乱，无秩序 v. 使混乱
disarray.note:
The sudden resignation left the department in complete disarray. 突然的辞职让该部门陷入了彻底的混乱。

Papers were scattered in disarray across the desk. 文件杂乱无章地散落在桌子上。

disbar.meaning: v. 取消律师资格，开除出律师公会
disbar.note:
The corrupt lawyer was disbarred for financial fraud. 那名腐败的律师因金融诈骗被取消了律师资格。

Being convicted of a felony will likely disbar you. 被判重罪很可能会使你被取消律师资格。

disburse.note:
Funds will be disbursed to research projects next month. 资金将于下个月拨付给研究项目。

The accountant carefully tracked how money was disbursed. 会计仔细追踪了资金的支出情况。

discernible.meaning: adj. 可辨别的，看得清的，看得出来的
discernible.note:
There was no discernible change in her condition. 她的病情没有明显的改变。

A faint light was discernible through the trees. 透过树木可以隐约看到微弱的光线。

discerning.meaning: adj. 有识别力的，眼光敏锐的，有品味的
discerning.note:
The restaurant caters to discerning food lovers. 这家餐厅迎合了眼光挑剔的美食爱好者。

She has a discerning eye for authentic antiques. 她对真正的古董有着敏锐的鉴赏眼光。

disciple.note:
The philosopher gathered a small group of loyal disciples. 那位哲学家聚集了一小群忠诚的信徒。

He considers himself a disciple of modern design principles. 他认为自己是现代设计原则的追随者。

disclaim.meaning: v. 放弃，拒绝承认，声明无关
disclaim.note:
The company was quick to disclaim responsibility for the defect. 公司很快就发表声明否认对该缺陷负有责任。

He chose to disclaim any interest in the property. 他选择放弃对该房产的任何权益。

discography.meaning: n. 唱片目录，录音作品集
discography.note:
The book includes a complete discography of the jazz musician. 这本书收录了这位爵士音乐家的完整唱片目录。

Fans often check the artist's discography to find rare tracks. 粉丝经常查看这位艺术家的作品集以寻找罕见的曲目。

discombobulate.meaning: v. 使混乱，使困惑，使心烦意乱
discombobulate.note:
The unexpected question completely discombobulated him. 这个意想不到的问题把他彻底搞糊涂了。

Jet lag tends to discombobulate travelers for days. 时差往往会让旅行者困惑好几天。

discombobulated.meaning: adj. 混乱的，心烦意乱的，不知所措的
discombobulated.note:
She felt a bit discombobulated after waking up in a strange room. 在一个陌生的房间醒来后，她感到有点不知所措。

His confusing instructions left everyone discombobulated. 他那令人困惑的指示让每个人都感到一团糟。

discomfit.meaning: v. 使窘迫，使尴尬，挫败
discomfit.note:
She tried not to let the difficult question discomfit her. 她努力不让那个困难的问题使自己感到尴尬。

Their sudden appearance seemed to discomfit the host. 他们的突然出现似乎让主人感到有些局促。

discomfited.meaning: adj. 窘迫的，尴尬的，受挫的
discomfited.note:
He looked slightly discomfited by the unexpected praise. 面对突如其来的表扬，他显得略微有些尴尬。

The discomfited politician refused to answer further questions. 那位感到难堪的政客拒绝回答更多问题。

discomfiture.note:
He tried to hide his discomfiture behind a polite smile. 他试图用礼貌的微笑掩饰自己的尴尬。

To her absolute discomfiture, she dropped her notes on stage. 令她极其尴尬的是，她的笔记在舞台上掉了。

discompose.meaning: v. 使不安，使心烦意乱，使失去镇静
discompose.note:
She remained calm and refused to be discomposed by the insults. 她保持镇静，拒绝被侮辱所激怒。

The sudden loud noise discomposed the speaker for a second. 突然的巨响让演讲者有那么一秒钟感到心神不定。

disconcert.meaning: v. 使窘迫，使惊慌，打乱（计划等）
disconcert.note:
Her intense gaze tended to disconcert him. 她热烈的目光往往会使他感到局促不安。

A sudden change in schedule can disconcert travel plans. 日程的突然改变会打乱旅行计划。

discredit.meaning: v. 败坏…的名声，使怀疑 n. 丧失名誉，怀疑
discredit.note:
Critics tried to discredit the scientist's latest findings. 批评家试图败坏这位科学家最新研究成果的信誉。

The theory has fallen into total discredit. 该理论已经彻底失去了信誉。

discreet.meaning: adj. 谨慎的，言行审慎的，不张扬的
discreet.note:
Please be discreet about what I told you. 对于我告诉你的人，请务必保密谨慎。

They made discreet inquiries about his background. 他们对他的背景进行了审慎的打听。

discretionary.meaning: adj. 自由决定的，自主的，酌情使用的
discretionary.note:
Employees have a certain amount of discretionary spending money. 员工拥有一定数额的自由支配资金。

Attendance at the optional workshop is entirely discretionary. 参加可选的工作坊完全是自主决定的。

discriminatory.meaning: adj. 歧视性的，差别对待的
discriminatory.note:
The law prohibits discriminatory practices in hiring and employment. 该法律禁止在招聘和就业中采取歧视性做法。

They faced discriminatory treatment because of their background. 他们因出身背景而面临差别对待。

discursive.meaning: adj. 离题的，散漫的；推理的
discursive.note:
His lecture was somewhat discursive, jumping from one topic to another. 他的讲座有些漫无边际，从一个话题跳到另一个话题。

A discursive essay allows the writer to explore various related ideas. 一篇散漫议论的文章允许作者探讨各种相关想法。

disdain.meaning: n. 蔑视，鄙视；v. 鄙视，不屑做
disdain.note:
She looked at the proposal with obvious disdain. 她带着明显的鄙视看着这份提案。

He disdained to answer such insulting questions. 他不屑于回答这种侮辱性的问题。

disembodied.meaning: adj. 无实体凭依的，飘渺的，离体的
disembodied.note:
A strange, disembodied voice echoed through the empty hallway. 一个奇异的、飘渺的声音在空荡荡的走廊里回响。

The soul was viewed as a disembodied spirit after death. 灵魂在死后被视为一种无实体的精神。

disenchant.meaning: v. 使清醒，使幻想破灭
disenchant.note:
The harsh realities of politics soon disenchanted the young idealistic reformer. 残酷的政治现实很快使这位年轻的理想主义改革家幻想破灭。

Many voters feel disenchanted with the current administration. 许多选民对现政府感到失望和幻灭。

disengage.note:
The soldier tried to disengage his rifle from the mud. 这名士兵设法把步枪从泥里拔出来。

Both nations agreed to disengage their military forces from the border. 两国同意将其军事力量从边境撤离。

disentangle.meaning: v. 解开，分清，使脱离纠缠
disentangle.note:
It took hours to disentangle the knotted fishing lines. 花了好几个小时才解开打结的钓鱼线。

It is difficult to disentangle truth from fiction in his story. 要在他的故事中分清虚构与真实是很困难的。

disfigure.note:
The severe burn would permanently disfigure his face. 严重的烧伤将永远毁坏他的面容。

Graffiti began to disfigure the historic walls of the city. 涂鸦开始玷污这座城市历史悠久的墙壁。

disgorge.note:
The volcano began to disgorge lava and ash. 火山开始喷出熔岩和灰烬。

The bus stopped to disgorge a crowd of noisy tourists. 公共汽车停下来，吐出一群吵闹的游客。

disgruntle.note:
Low wages and poor benefits can disgruntle the workforce. 低工资和差福利会使员工感到不满。

The disgruntled manager refused to cooperate with the team. 心怀不满的经理拒绝与团队合作。

disgust.note:
She turned away in disgust at the sight of the mess. 看到这片混乱，她厌恶地转过头去。

His rude behavior began to disgust everyone at the table. 他粗鲁的行为开始让桌上的每个人感到恶心。

disillusion.meaning: v. 使醒悟，使幻灭；n. 醒悟
disillusion.note:
Travel can often disillusion you of romantic notions about foreign cultures. 旅行往往会打破你对外国文化的浪漫幻想。

The scandal led to widespread disillusion among the public. 丑闻导致公众普遍产生幻灭感。

disinfect.note:
You must thoroughly disinfect the wound to prevent infection. 你必须彻底给伤口消毒以防止感染。

It is important to disinfect kitchen surfaces after handling raw meat. 处理生肉后给厨房台面消毒是很重要的。

disinfectant.meaning: n. 消毒剂，杀菌剂；adj. 消毒的
disinfectant.note:
She wiped the floor with a strong disinfectant. 她用强效消毒剂擦洗了地板。

The hospital corridors smelled strongly of disinfectant. 医院走廊里弥漫着浓烈的消毒水味。

disinter.meaning: v. 掘出，挖出，使重见天日
disinter.note:
The police obtained a court order to disinter the body for forensic testing. 警方获得法院命令，将尸体掘出以进行法医检测。

Historians managed to disinter forgotten documents from the archive. 历史学家设法从档案中发掘出被遗忘的文件。

disinterested.meaning: adj. 无私的，公正的；不感兴趣的
disinterested.note:
A judge must remain completely disinterested during a trial. 法官在审判期间必须保持完全公正。

He seemed totally disinterested in sports and outdoor activities. 他似乎对体育和户外活动完全不感兴趣。

disjunction.note:
There is a clear disjunction between theory and practice in this project. 该项目的理论与实践之间存在明显的脱节。

The disjunction of economic classes created social tension. 经济阶层的割裂造成了社会紧张。

disjunctive.meaning: adj. 分离的，转折的，析取的
disjunctive.note:
The word 'or' is often used as a disjunctive conjunction. 单词“or”常被用作选择连词。

His ideas formed a disjunctive series of thoughts rather than a coherent theory. 他的想法构成了一系列不连贯的思考，而非连贯的理论。

dislocate.meaning: v. 使脱臼，扰乱，使错位
dislocate.note:
He fell off the horse and managed to dislocate his shoulder. 他从马摔了下来，把肩膀摔脱臼了。

The heavy snowstorm threatened to dislocate regional transport. 这场大雪可能打乱区域交通。

dislodge.note:
Strong winds tried to dislodge tiles from the roof. 强风试图把屋顶上的瓦片刮松移位。

The doctors performed surgery to dislodge the object from his throat. 医生实施手术以取出他喉咙里的异物。

dismal.meaning: adj. 阴沉的，凄凉的，低劣的
dismal.note:
They spent the afternoon under a dismal, rainy sky. 他们在阴沉下雨的天空下度过了下午。

The team's performance was a dismal failure. 该团队的表现是一场惨败。

dismantle.note:
Workers began to dismantle the old factory equipment. 工人们开始拆除旧工厂设备。

The government plans to dismantle the outdated bureaucratic structure. 政府计划废除过时的官僚体制。

dismay.note:
To their dismay, the flight was canceled due to bad weather. 令他们沮丧的是，航班因天气恶劣被取消了。

The scope of the destruction began to dismay the rescue workers. 破坏的范围开始让救援人员感到惊恐。

disparage.note:
You should not disparage your colleagues' contributions. 你不应该贬低同事们的贡献。

He always tries to disparage other people's achievements out of jealousy. 他总是出于嫉妒去贬低别人的成就。

dispassionate.meaning: adj. 冷静的，不带感情色彩的，客观的
dispassionate.note:
The investigator gave a dispassionate account of the incident. 调查人员对该事件作了客观公正的叙述。

It is important to maintain a dispassionate attitude during crisis management. 在危机处理中保持冷静的客观态度至关重要。

dispatch.meaning: v./n. 派遣，发送，迅速处理
dispatch.note:
The company will dispatch the order within 24 hours. 公司将在24小时内发送订单。

She handled the urgent tasks with remarkable dispatch. 她以惊人的高效迅速处理了紧急任务。

dispose.meaning: v. 处理，处置，倾倒；倾向于
dispose.note:
Please find a proper way to dispose of hazardous waste. 请寻找妥善的方法来处理有害废物。

Good management tends to dispose employees toward hard work. 良好的管理往往倾向于促使员工努力工作。

disposed.note:
I am not disposed to argue about this matter right now. 我现在不愿争论这件事。

She felt well disposed toward the charity project. 她对这个慈善项目抱有好感。

disproof.note:
The scientist offered clear disproof of the old theory. 这位科学家为旧理论提供了清晰的反证。

They sought absolute disproof for the false allegations. 他们寻找虚假指控的绝对反驳证据。

disprove.note:
New evidence emerged to disprove the suspect's alibi. 新证据的出现反驳了嫌疑人的不在场证明。

It is hard to disprove a widespread superstition. 消除一种广为流传的迷信是很难的。

disrepute.note:
The scandal brought the organization into serious disrepute. 这场丑闻使该组织声誉扫地。

His dishonest business practices fell into disrepute. 他不诚实的商业行径名誉扫地。

disruptive.meaning: adj. 破坏性的，扰乱的，分裂的
disruptive.note:
His disruptive behavior forced the teacher to send him outside. 他扰乱秩序的行为迫使老师把他赶到外面。

New technology can have a disruptive effect on traditional industries. 新技术可能对传统产业产生颠覆性的影响。

dissect.note:
Biology students had to dissect a frog in the laboratory. 生物课的学生必须在实验室里解剖一只青蛙。

Critics spent hours dissecting the meaning of the new policy. 评论家们花了几个小时仔细分析这项新政策的含义。

dissemble.note:
She managed to dissemble her true feelings behind a polite smile. 她勉强用礼貌的微笑掩饰自己真实的感受。

He could not dissemble his excitement when he won the prize. 当他获奖时，他无法掩饰自己的兴奋。

dissent.note:
There was widespread dissent among the members regarding the new policy. 成员们对新政策普遍存在异议。

Several judges chose to dissent from the majority verdict. 几位法官选择对多数裁决持不同意见。

dissident.meaning: n. 持异议者；adj. 持异议的
dissident.note:
Political dissidents were arrested for speaking out. 政治异见人士因直言不讳而被捕。

Dissident groups gathered to protest against the censorship. 持不同政见的群体聚集起来抗议审查制度。

dissimulate.meaning: v. 掩饰（真情或动机），假装
dissimulate.note:
He tried to dissimilate his anger with a calm expression. 他试图用平静的表情掩饰自己的愤怒。

She learned to dissimulate her ambition in front of her rivals. 她学会了在竞争对手面前掩饰自己的野心。

dissipate.note:
The morning sun quickly began to dissipate the fog. 早晨的太阳很快开始驱散大雾。

He tended to dissipate his inheritance on gambling and luxury. 他往往把继承的遗产挥霍在赌博和奢侈品上。

dissociation.note:
The chemical process involves the dissociation of molecules. 这个化学过程涉及分子的解离。

Trauma can sometimes lead to psychological dissociation. 创伤有时会导致心理上的解离现象。

dissolute.note:
He led a dissolute lifestyle full of heavy drinking and gambling. 他过着酗酒和赌博的放荡生活。

The play depicts the downfall of a dissolute nobleman. 该剧刻画了一个放荡贵族的没落。

dissonant.note:
Modern music often employs dissonant chords to create tension. 现代音乐经常运用不和谐的和弦来营造紧张感。

Several dissonant voices interrupted the harmonious meeting. 几种不和谐的声音打断了和谐的会议。

dissuade.note:
Her parents tried to dissuade her from traveling alone. 她的父母试图劝阻她独自旅行。

I managed to dissuade him from making such a risky investment. 我设法劝阻了他进行如此冒险的投资。

distant.meaning: adj. 遥远的，远亲的，冷漠的
distant.note:
They lived in a distant village across the mountains. 他们住在山那边的一个遥远村庄里。

She seemed rather distant and cold during the party. 派对期间她显得相当冷漠疏离。

distend.note:
The patient's abdomen began to distend due to the illness. 由于病情，病人的腹部开始膨胀。

Eating too much can cause the stomach to distend. 吃得太多会引起胃部扩张。

distension.note:
Abdominal distension is a common symptom of digestive issues. 腹部膨胀是消化系统问题的常见症状。

Pressure inside the pipe caused severe distension. 管子内部的压力造成了严重的膨胀。

distract.meaning: v. 分散注意力，使分心
distract.note:
Don't let the noise outside distract you from your studies. 别让外面的噪音分散你学习的注意力。

He tried to distract her attention while planning the surprise. 在筹划惊喜时，他设法分散了她的注意力。

distracted.meaning: adj. 心烦意乱的，分心的
distracted.note:
She looked distracted and failed to catch what I said. 她看起来心不在焉，没听清我说的话。

Drivers who use phones are easily distracted on the road. 使用手机的司机在路上很容易分心。

distraught.meaning: adj. 心烦意乱的，极度发狂的
distraught.note:
The distraught mother searched everywhere for her lost child. 悲痛欲绝的母亲到处寻找她走失的孩子。

He was too distraught to talk about the accident. 他心烦意乱得无法谈论这场事故。

district.note:
They live in the financial district of the city. 他们住在该市的金融区。

The school district approved a new budget for technology. 学区批准了一项新的技术预算。

ditty.note:
The children sang a cheerful little ditty as they walked. 孩子们边走边唱着一首欢快的小曲。

He hummed an old folk ditty while working in the garden. 他在花园里干活时哼着一首古老的民谣。

diva.meaning: n. 著名女歌唱家，歌剧女主角
diva.note:
The opera diva received a standing ovation from the audience. 这位歌剧女主角赢得了观众起立长时间的喝彩。

She acted like a demanding diva backstage. 她在后台表现得像个事儿多的傲慢女星。

diver.meaning: n. 潜水员，跳水运动员
diver.note:
Deep-sea divers explored the sunken shipwreck. 深海潜水员探索了沉没的沉船。

The Olympic diver won gold with a flawless performance. 这位奥运跳水运动员以完美的表现赢得了金牌。

divergent.meaning: adj. 分歧的，发散的，相异的
divergent.note:
The two brothers pursued divergent career paths. 这两兄弟走上了截然不同的职业道路。

They had divergent views on how to resolve the crisis. 他们对如何解决这场危机持有不同的看法。

divest.meaning: v. 剥夺，卸除，脱去（衣物等）
divest.note:
The company decided to divest itself of unprofitable assets. 公司决定剥离无利可图的资产。

He was forced to divest himself of his title and privileges. 他被迫放弃了自己的头衔和特权。

divestiture.note:
The anti-trust law required the corporate divestiture of the subsidiary. 反垄断法要求该企业剥离其子公司。

Investors pushed for the divestiture of fossil fuel holdings. 投资者敦促剥离化石燃料资产。

divulge.note:
Refusing to divulge the source of information is a journalist's code. 拒绝透露消息来源是记者的准则。

He promised never to divulge her secret to anyone. 他答应绝不把她的秘密泄露给任何人。

doctrinaire.meaning: adj. 教条主义的，迂腐的
doctrinaire.note:
His doctrinaire approach left no room for practical compromise. 他教条主义的方法没有留下任何务实妥协的空间。

She rejected the doctrinaire policies of the old regime. 她拒绝了旧政权的教条主义政策。

document.meaning: n. 文件，公文；v. 记录，用文件证明
document.note:
Please sign the important legal document before leaving. 请在离开前签署这份重要的法律文件。

Researchers will document the declining population of birds. 研究人员将记录不断下降的鸟类数量。

dodder.note:
The old man began to dodder across the room with a cane. 老人拄着手杖在房间里颤巍巍地走着。

He watched his doddering grandfather slowly climb the stairs. 他看着步履蹒跚的祖父慢慢爬上楼梯。

dodge.note:
He managed to dodge the flying baseball just in time. 他及时闪躲开了飞来的棒球。

She tried to dodge the difficult questions during the interview. 她试图在采访中避开那些棘手的问题。

doff.note:
He politely doffed his hat as she walked past. 她走过时，他礼貌地脱下帽子致意。

Workers must doff their safety gear before entering the cafeteria. 工人们在进入餐厅前必须脱下安全装备。

dogged.meaning: adj. 顽强的，坚持不懈的
dogged.note:
Her dogged determination finally brought her success. 她顽强的决心最终给她带来了成功。

Through dogged effort, they solved the complex puzzle. 经过不懈的努力，他们解开了这个复杂的谜题。

doggerel.note:
He wrote a funny piece of doggerel for his friend's birthday. 他为朋友的生日写了一首有趣的打油诗。

The newspaper printed some political doggerel mocking the mayor. 报纸刊登了一些嘲笑市长的政治打油诗。

dogma.note:
Scientists often question established religious dogma. 科学家经常质疑既定的宗教教条。

She refused to accept political dogma without rational proof. 她拒绝在没有理性证明的情况下接受政治教条。

dogmatism.note:
His intellectual dogmatism alienated many of his colleagues. 他学术上的教条主义疏远了许多同事。

We must avoid dogmatism when approaching new ideas. 在对待新观点时，我们必须避免教条主义。

doldrums.meaning: n. 低迷期，忧郁，赤道无风带
doldrums.note:
The housing market has been in the doldrums for months. 房地产市场已经低迷了好几个月。

He fell into the doldrums after losing his job. 失业后他陷入了情绪低谷。

doleful.note:
The dog gave him a doleful look when he left. 当他离开时，狗投给他一个悲伤的眼神。

A doleful tune played softly in the background. 背景中轻柔地播放着一首哀伤的曲子。

dolorous.note:
She sang a dolorous song that moved everyone to tears. 她唱了一首悲伤的歌，感动得每个人都落泪了。

The novel is filled with dolorous accounts of poverty. 这部小说充满了关于贫困的痛苦记述。

dolt.note:
He felt like a complete dolt when he forgot his own password. 当他忘记自己的密码时，他觉得自己像个十足的笨蛋。

Don't be such a dolt and read the instructions carefully. 别当个笨蛋了，仔细阅读说明书。

dome.note:
The golden dome of the cathedral shone in the sunlight. 大教堂的金色圆屋顶在阳光下闪闪发光。

An astronomical observatory is usually built with a large dome. 天文台通常建有一个巨大的圆顶。

domesticate.meaning: v. 驯养，驯化，使适应家庭生活
domesticate.note:
Humans began to domesticate wild animals thousands of years ago. 人类在几千年前就开始驯养野生动物。

It is hard to domesticate certain wild feline species. 很难驯化某些野生猫科动物。

domicile.meaning: n. 住所，法定住所；v. 设住所
domicile.note:
Tax laws often depend on your primary domicile. 税法往往取决于你的主要住所。

The corporation chose to domicile its headquarters offshore. 该公司选择将其总部设在境外。

domination.note:
The empire sought global domination through military power. 该帝国通过军事力量寻求全球统治。

They fought against economic domination by foreign corporations. 他们反对外国企业的经济支配。

donate.note:
She decided to donate a large sum of money to the hospital. 她决定向医院捐赠一大笔钱。

Many people volunteer to donate blood every year. 每年有许多人志愿献血。

doodle.meaning: v./n. 胡乱涂鸦，随手涂画
doodle.note:
He began to doodle on the margin of his notebook during the lecture. 讲课时他开始在笔记本的边缘涂鸦。

Her meeting notes were covered in random doodles. 她的会议记录上画满了随手涂鸦。

dormancy.meaning: n. 休眠，静止，蛰伏状态
dormancy.note:
Many plants enter a period of dormancy during the winter. 许多植物在冬季进入休眠期。

The volcano has been in dormancy for over a century. 这座火山已经休眠了一个多世纪。

dorsal.note:
The shark has a prominent dorsal fin. 这条鲨鱼有一个显眼的背鳍。

The lesion was located on the dorsal surface of the hand. 病变位于手背侧。

dossier.note:
The police compiled a comprehensive dossier on the suspect. 警方汇编了一份关于该嫌疑人的全面档案。

She reviewed the applicant's dossier before the interview. 面试前她审阅了申请人的档案材料。

dote.note:
Grandparents often dote on their grandchildren. 祖父母往往对孙辈百般溺爱。

He would dote on his new sports car every weekend. 他每个周末都会对他的新跑车爱不释手。

doting.meaning: adj. 溺爱的，过分宠爱的
doting.note:
The doting parents bought every toy their child wanted. 溺爱孩子的父母买下了孩子想要的所有玩具。

She received flowers from her doting husband on her birthday. 生日那天，她收到了溺爱她的丈夫送来的鲜花。

dour.meaning: adj. 严厉的，阴沉的，顽强的
dour.note:
He was a man of dour expression and few words. 他是一个表情严肃、话语不多的人。

Despite the setbacks, they maintained a dour persistence. 尽管遭遇挫折，他们依然保持着顽强的坚持。

douse.note:
Firefighters worked quickly to douse the flames. 消防员迅速扑灭了火焰。

She tried to douse her burning face with cold water. 她试图用冷水洗洗她发烫的脸。

downplay.meaning: v. 对...轻描淡写，贬低，低估
downplay.note:
The manager tried to downplay the severity of the crisis. 经理试图轻描淡写这场危机的严重性。

She always downplays her own achievements in the project. 她在项目中总是低估自己的成就。

downpour.note:
We got caught in a sudden downpour without an umbrella. 我们没带伞，淋在了一场突如其来的倾盆大雨中。

Street flooding occurred after the heavy downpour. 暴雨过后发生了街道积水。

doyen.meaning: n. 老前辈，资深专家，泰斗
doyen.note:
He is widely considered the doyen of French cinema. 他被广泛认为是法国电影界的泰斗。

The conference featured talks by several doyens of economics. 会议邀请了几位经济学界的资深专家做演讲。

drab.meaning: adj. 单调的，乏味的，灰褐色的
drab.note:
The town looked drab and dreary under the gray winter sky. 在灰色的冬日天空下，小镇显得单调而沉闷。

She wore a drab coat that matched the gloomy weather. 她穿着一件与阴郁天气相配的灰褐色大衣。

draconian.meaning: adj. 严厉的，残酷的，苛刻的
draconian.note:
The university imposed draconian rules on student behavior. 大学对学生的行为实施了严厉的规章制度。

Protesters complained about the draconian censorship laws. 抗议者抱怨严苛的审查法。

draft.meaning: n. 草稿，汇票；v. 起草，征兵
draft.note:
Please write a first draft of your essay by tomorrow. 请在明天前写好你的论文初稿。

The government decided to draft a new environmental bill. 政府决定起草一项新的环保法案。

draftsmanship.meaning: n. 制图术，起草水平，精湛的手艺
draftsmanship.note:
His exceptional draftsmanship was evident in the architectural drawings. 他出色的制图技巧在建筑图纸中显露无遗。

The artist's technical draftsmanship received high praise. 这位艺术家的技术制图水平受到了高度赞扬。

drastic.meaning: adj. 激烈的，严厉的，极端的
drastic.note:
The company had to take drastic measures to avoid bankruptcy. 公司不得不采取激烈的措施以避免破产。

There is a need for drastic action to tackle climate change. 需要采取极端的行动来应对气候变化。

drawbridge.note:
The castle guards raised the drawbridge to keep enemies out. 城堡守卫拉起吊桥以把敌人挡在外面。

Tourists watched the mechanical drawbridge lift up for a boat. 游客们看着机械吊桥为一艘船升起。

drawl.meaning: v./n. 拉长语调说，慢条斯理地讲
drawl.note:
He spoke with a slow, southern drawl. 他说话带有缓慢的南方腔调。

She answered his question with a lazy drawl. 她用懒洋洋的慢调回答了他的问题。

dreary.meaning: adj. 沉闷的，阴郁的，枯燥的
dreary.note:
Working indoors all day can be quite dreary. 整天在室内工作可能会相当枯燥。

She walked home through the dreary, wet streets. 她走在沉闷潮湿的街道上回家。

dregs.note:
He drained his coffee cup, leaving only the dark dregs. 他喝干了咖啡杯，只留下黑色的沉淀物。

Society must rid itself of the dregs of crime and corruption. 社会必须清除犯罪和腐败的渣滓。

drenched.note:
They arrived home completely drenched from the rain. 他们淋雨回到家时浑身都湿透了。

The morning grass was drenched with heavy dew. 清晨的草地上沾满了浓重的露水。

drill.meaning: n. 钻头，训练；v. 钻孔，反复训练
drill.note:
The worker used an electric drill to make a hole in the wall. 工人使用电钻在墙上钻了一个洞。

Fire drills are conducted monthly at the school. 学校每月举行一次消防演习。

drivel.meaning: n./v. 胡言乱语，废话，流口水
drivel.note:
I am not going to listen to his political drivel anymore. 我再也不想听他那些政治废话了。

The baby began to cry and drivel on his bib. 婴儿开始哭泣，口水流在了围嘴上。

drizzly.meaning: adj. 毛毛雨的，细雨蒙蒙的
drizzly.note:
It was a cold and drizzly morning in autumn. 那是一个寒冷而细雨蒙蒙的秋日清晨。

We decided to stay indoors on such a drizzly day. 在这样一个下毛毛雨的日子里，我们决定呆在室内。

droll.meaning: adj. 滑稽的，古怪有趣的
droll.note:
He entertained us with his droll sense of humor. 他用他滑稽的幽默感逗乐了我们。

She made a droll comment that made everyone smile. 她发表了一个古怪有趣的评论，让所有人都笑了。

droop.note:
The flowers began to droop from lack of water. 由于缺水，花朵开始下垂萎蔫。

His shoulders began to droop with fatigue. 疲惫使他的双肩渐渐耷拉下来。

droplet.note:
Tiny water droplets formed on the cold glass surface. 微小的水滴在冰冷的玻璃表面形成。

Sneezing can release thousands of infectious droplets. 打喷洒可能会释放数千个具传染性的飞沫。

dross.note:
The refining process removes the dross from the metal. 精炼过程去除了金属中的杂质。

We must separate valuable literature from historical dross. 我们必须将有价值的文学作品与历史糟粕区分开来。

drove.meaning: n. 一群（人或牲畜），畜群
drove.note:
Tourists arrived in droves to see the famous monument. 游客们成群结队地赶来观看这座著名的纪念碑。

The cowboy guided the cattle drove across the river. 牛仔赶着牛群过河。

duckling.note:
The mother duck swam across the pond followed by her ducklings. 母鸭身后跟着小鸭们游过了池塘。

A fluffy yellow duckling hatched in the spring. 一只毛茸茸的黄色小鸭在春天孵化出来。

duct.note:
Air conditioning ducts distribute cool air through the building. 空调管道将冷气输送到建筑物的各个角落。

Blocked tear ducts can cause eyes to water constantly. 泪管阻塞会导致眼睛经常流泪。

duel.note:
The two politicians engaged in a fierce televised duel. 这两位政治家在电视上展开了激烈的辩论竞争。

In the past, gentlemen would settle disputes with a duel. 过去，绅士们会通过决斗来解决争端。

duet.note:
The singers performed a beautiful love duet on stage. 两位歌手在舞台上表演了一首美妙的爱情二重唱。

They played a classical piano duet for the recital. 他们在独奏会上合奏了一首古典钢琴二重奏。

dull.meaning: adj. 枯燥的，迟钝的，阴暗的
dull.note:
The lecture was so long and dull that I almost fell asleep. 讲座太长太枯燥，我差点睡着。

The knife is too dull to cut the tomatoes easily. 这把刀太钝了，切西红柿很不方便。

dummy.meaning: n. 假人，仿制品，笨蛋；adj. 假的
dummy.note:
Crash test dummies are used to test vehicle safety. 碰撞测试假人被用来测试汽车安全性。

The store window featured stylish clothing on wooden dummies. 商店橱窗里摆放着穿着时尚服装的木制假人。

dupe.meaning: v. 欺骗，愚弄；n. 易受骗的人
dupe.note:
He managed to dupe investors into buying fake shares. 他设法欺骗投资者购买虚假股票。

She felt like a dupe after falling for his trick. 在中了对方的诡计后，她觉得自己像个傻瓜。

duplicitous.note:
His duplicitous behavior finally cost him his career. 他两面派的行为最终让他失去了事业。

She could no longer trust her duplicitous business partner. 她再也无法信任她那个奸诈的商业伙伴了。

duplicity.meaning: n. 欺骗，表里不一，两面派
duplicity.note:
He was found guilty of fraud and gross duplicity. 他因欺诈和严重的两面派行径而被判有罪。

Her duplicity shocked everyone who thought she was honest. 她的虚伪欺诈震惊了所有认为她诚实的人。

duration.note:
The course has a duration of three months. 这门课程为期三个月。

Mobile phones must be turned off for the duration of the flight. 在飞行期间必须关闭手机。

duress.note:
The confession was made under police duress. 这份口供是在警方胁迫下做出的。

He signed the contract while under financial duress. 他是在面临财务压力的胁迫下签署合同的。

dutiful.meaning: adj. 尽职的，顺从的，孝顺的
dutiful.note:
She was a dutiful daughter who visited her parents every week. 她是一个孝顺的女儿，每周都去看望父母。

He dutifully completed every task assigned to him. 他尽职尽责地完成了分派给他的每一项任务。

dwarf.meaning: n. 侏儒；v. 使相形见绌，使矮小
dwarf.note:
The tall skyscrapers dwarf the old houses nearby. 高耸的摩天大楼使附近的老房子相形见绌。

Gardeners grow dwarf trees in pots for decoration. 园丁们在花盆里种植矮化树木作装饰。

dwelling.note:
Ancient humans sought shelters as primitive dwellings. 古代人类将庇护所作为原始的住所。

The old stone dwelling was listed as a historic landmark. 这处古老的石制住宅被列为历史地标。

dynamic.meaning: adj. 动态的，充满活力的；n. 动力，动态
dynamic.note:
The modern tech industry requires a dynamic approach to management. 现代科技行业需要采取充满活力的管理方法。

We need to analyze the social dynamics of the community. 我们需要分析该社区的社会动力学。

dynamo.meaning: n. 发电机，精力充沛的人
dynamo.note:
A hydroelectric dynamo converts water power into electricity. 水力发电机将水能转化为电能。

She is a tireless dynamo who manages three projects at once. 她是一个不知疲倦的精力充沛者，同时管理着三个项目。

dysfunctional.meaning: adj. 机能失调的，不正常的
dysfunctional.note:
He grew up in a deeply dysfunctional family. 他在一个极度失调的家庭中长大。

The system became entirely dysfunctional after the cyber attack. 网络攻击后，该系统完全陷入瘫痪失调。

dyslexia.note:
Special teaching methods can help children with dyslexia. 特殊的教学方法可以帮助患有阅读障碍的儿童。

She was diagnosed with mild dyslexia at an early age. 她很小就被诊断出患有轻度阅读障碍。

dyspeptic.meaning: adj. 消化不良的，脾气暴躁的
dyspeptic.note:
He suffered from chronic dyspeptic symptoms after heavy meals. 他在大餐后长期患有消化不良症状。

The old man was famously dyspeptic and complained about everything. 这位老人出了名的脾气暴躁，对什么都抱怨。

earnest.note:
He made an earnest attempt to apologize for his mistakes. 他真诚地试图为自己的错误道歉。

Negotiations began in earnest on Monday morning. 谈判于周一上午正式严肃地开始。

earplug.note:
She wore earplugs to block out the noise from the street. 她戴上耳塞以隔绝街上的噪音。

Construction workers should wear earplugs to protect their hearing. 建筑工人应该佩戴耳塞来保护听力。

earring.note:
She wore a pair of diamond earrings to the party. 她戴了一对钻石耳环去参加派对。

He lost one of his gold earrings during the trip. 他在旅行中弄丢了一只金耳环。

earshot.meaning: n. 听力范围，听见距离
earshot.note:
Speak quietly so the children are not within earshot. 小声说话，别让孩子们听到。

She stepped out of earshot to make a private phone call. 她走到听不见的地方打私人电话。

earsplitting.note:
An earsplitting explosion shook the neighborhood. 一声震耳欲聋的爆炸声震动了整个社区。

They covered their ears when the jets made an earsplitting noise. 当喷气式飞机发出震耳欲聋的轰鸣时，他们捂住了耳朵。

earthly.meaning: adj. 尘世的，世俗的，可能的（常用于否定句）
earthly.note:
Monks renounce earthly possessions to focus on spiritual life. 修士放弃尘世的财产，专注于精神生活。

There is no earthly reason why we should delay the project. 没有任何世俗理由能让我们推迟这个项目。

earthy.meaning: adj. 泥土气息的，朴实的，粗俗的
earthy.note:
The wine had a rich, earthy flavor. 这款酒带有浓郁的泥土芳香。

He was known for his earthy humor and direct language. 他以粗俗幽默和直白的语言而闻名。

easel.note:
The artist set up his wooden easel in the middle of the garden. 艺术家在花园中央架起了他的木制画架。

She placed a blank canvas on the easel and began to paint. 她把一块空白画布放在画架上开始作画。

eavesdrop.note:
He tried to eavesdrop on his parents' private conversation. 他试图偷听父母的私密对话。

Never eavesdrop on other people's telephone calls. 绝不要偷听别人的电话。

ebb.note:
They waited on the beach for the tide to ebb. 他们在海滩上等待退潮。

His enthusiasm for the project began to ebb over time. 随着时间的推移，他对这个项目标热情开始减退。

ebullience.meaning: n. 热情洋溢，兴高采烈
ebullience.note:
Her natural ebullience brought joy to everyone around her. 她天生的热情洋溢给周围的每个人都带来了欢乐。

The children's ebullience could not be contained. 孩子们兴奋欢快的情绪无法抑制。

eclectic.meaning: adj. 折中主义的，兼收并蓄的，多元的
eclectic.note:
She has an eclectic taste in music, ranging from jazz to classical. 她对音乐的品味很杂，从爵士乐到古典乐无所不包。

The restaurant offers an eclectic menu featuring dishes from around the world. 这家餐厅提供兼收并蓄的菜单，涵盖了世界各地的菜肴。

eclecticism.meaning: n. 折中主义，兼收并蓄
eclecticism.note:
The building's architecture is a fine example of Victorian eclecticism. 该建筑的风格是维多利亚时期折中主义的典范。

His artistic style reflects a unique eclecticism. 他的艺术风格反映了一种独特的兼收并蓄。

ecologist.note:
Ecologists study the interactions between organisms and their environment. 生态学家研究生物与其环境之间的相互作用。

The ecologist warned about the rapid loss of biodiversity. 这位生态学家警告生物多样性的迅速丧失。

ecstasy.note:
She was in ecstasy when she heard she won the prize. 当她听说自己获奖时，她欣喜若狂。

Fans screamed in ecstasy as the rock star appeared on stage. 当摇滚明星出现在舞台上时，歌迷们狂喜地尖叫起来。

ecstatic.meaning: adj. 狂喜的，欣喜若狂的
ecstatic.note:
The children were ecstatic about going to Disneyland. 孩子们对去迪士尼乐园感到欣喜若狂。

She gave an ecstatic speech after winning the championship. 赢得冠军后，她发表了狂喜的演讲。

eddy.note:
Fallen leaves spun in a small eddy on the river surface. 落叶在河面上的一个小旋涡中旋转。

Water began to eddy around the bridge pier. 水流开始在桥墩周围形成回流。

edifice.meaning: n. 大厦，宏伟的建筑，体系
edifice.note:
The grand marble edifice serves as the city hall. 这座宏伟的大理石建筑用作市政厅。

He wanted to destroy the entire edifice of corruption. 他想要摧毁整个腐败体系。

edify.note:
Books should aim to both entertain and edify readers. 书籍的目的应当是既能娱乐又能启迪读者。

The documentary offered an edifying look at ancient philosophy. 这部纪录片对古代哲学提供了一个富有教益的视角。

efface.meaning: v. 抹去，擦掉，使自己默默无闻
efface.note:
Time could not efface the painful memories of war. 时间无法抹去战争痛苦的记忆。

She tried to efface herself during the formal gathering. 在正式聚会中，她尽量让自己不引人注目。

effervesce.meaning: v. 冒泡，起泡，热情洋溢
effervesce.note:
The sparkling drink began to effervesce in the glass. 碳酸饮料开始在杯中冒出气泡。

Her personality tended to effervesce with lively energy. 她的性格往往充满了生机勃勃的活力。

effete.meaning: adj. 软弱的，精疲力竭的，衰落的
effete.note:
Critics dismissed the old aristocracy as effete and decadent. 批评家斥责旧贵族软弱且腐朽。

The empire grew effete and eventually collapsed from within. 这个帝国日渐衰弱，最终从内部瓦解。

efficacious.note:
The new medicine proved to be highly efficacious against the virus. 证明这种新药对该病毒非常有效。

They sought a more efficacious remedy for the chronic cough. 他们为慢性咳嗽寻找更有效的疗法。

efficacy.note:
Scientists tested the clinical efficacy of the vaccine. 科学家测试了该疫苗的临床效力。

Doubts were raised about the efficacy of the new teaching method. 人们对这种新教学方法的有效性提出了质疑。

effluvia.meaning: n. 废气，恶臭，不良气味
effluvia.note:
The factory released foul effluvia into the night air. 工厂向夜空中排放了恶臭的废气。

They escaped the noxious effluvia of the chemical dump. 他们逃离了化学垃圾填埋场散发出的有毒恶臭。

effrontery.note:
He had the effrontery to ask for a raise after failing his tasks. 他在未完成任务后竟然厚颜无耻地要求加薪。

She was shocked by his utter effrontery during the meeting. 会议上他那十足的厚颜无耻令她大吃一惊。

effulgent.meaning: adj. 光辉灿烂的，光芒四射的
effulgent.note:
The bride looked effulgent in her white dress. 新娘穿着白裙，显得光彩照人。

An effulgent sunrise broke over the mountain tops. 一轮灿烂的日出破晓于山巅。

egalitarian.meaning: adj. 平等主义的；n. 平等主义者
egalitarian.note:
They built an egalitarian society based on shared labor. 他们建立了一个基于共同劳动的平等主义社会。

She is a staunch egalitarian who advocates for equal pay. 她是一位坚定的平等主义者，倡导同工同酬。

egocentric.meaning: adj. 利己的，自我中心的
egocentric.note:
His egocentric personality makes it hard to maintain friendships. 他以自我为中心的性格使得很难维持友谊。

Children are naturally egocentric in their early years. 孩子们在早年时期天生就是以自我为中心的。

egotist.meaning: n. 自大者，利己主义者
egotist.note:
He is an insufferable egotist who only talks about himself. 他是一个令人难以忍受的自大狂，满嘴都是自己。

Only an egotist would ignore everyone else's opinions. 只有自大狂才会忽视其他所有人的意见。

egregious.meaning: adj. 极坏的，震惊的，昭彰的
egregious.note:
Making such a basic math error was an egregious mistake. 犯下如此基础的数学错误是一个极大的失误。

The accountant was fired for egregious financial fraud. 这名会计因犯下严重的金融诈骗罪而被解雇。

egress.note:
The building had clear signs indicating emergency egress. 建筑内有标明紧急出口的清晰标志。

Fire regulations require unobstructed points of egress. 消防法规要求出口处畅通无阻。

elated.meaning: adj. 兴高采烈的，得意洋洋的
elated.note:
The team was elated after winning the championship game. 赢得冠军赛后，全队上下兴高采烈。

She felt elated when she received the university acceptance letter. 收到大学录取通知书时，她感到欢欣鼓舞。

elegy.note:
The poet wrote a moving elegy for his late friend. 这位诗人为他已故的朋友写了一首动人的挽歌。

The novel reads like an elegy for a lost way of life. 这部小说读起来像是一首针对逝去生活方式的哀歌。

elementary.note:
These are elementary rules that every beginner must learn. 这些是每个初学者都必须学习的基本规则。

Children attend elementary school from age six. 孩子从六岁起上小学。

elephantine.note:
He made an elephantine attempt to dance gracefully. 他笨拙地试图跳出优美的舞蹈。

The heavy machinery moved with an elephantine slowness. 这台重型机械以笨重缓慢的速度移动着。

eliminate.note:
The diet helps eliminate toxins from your body. 这种饮食有助于排除体内的毒素。

They hope to eliminate poverty in the next decade. 他们希望在未来十年内消除贫困。

ellipsis.note:
An ellipsis is often indicated by three dots (...). 省略号通常用三个点(...)来表示。

The writer used grammatical ellipsis for poetic effect. 作者为了取得诗意的效果使用了语法省略。

elliptical.meaning: adj. 椭圆形的，晦涩的，简略的
elliptical.note:
The planets move around the sun in elliptical orbits. 行星以椭圆形轨道绕太阳运行。

His remarks were so elliptical that few people understood him. 他的言论如此含糊晦涩，以至于没几个人听懂。

elm.note:
A massive old elm tree stood in the middle of the yard. 院子中央伫立着一棵巨大古老的榆树。

Dutch elm disease destroyed many trees in the region. 荷兰榆树病摧毁了该地区的许多树木。

elocution.meaning: n. 演讲术，朗诵法，发音法
elocution.note:
She took lessons in elocution to improve her public speaking. 她上了发音课以提高公众演讲能力。

Actors need proper elocution training for stage performances. 演员需要接受正规的朗诵培训才能进行舞台表演。

eloquence.note:
The politician won over the crowd with his eloquence. 这位政治家以其出色的雄辩口才赢得了群众的支持。

She spoke with such eloquence that everyone fell silent. 她的发言极具雄辩力，全场鸦雀无声。

elucidate.note:
The professor wrote an article to elucidate the complex theory. 教授写了一篇文章来阐述这个复杂的理论。

Could you please elucidate your previous statement? 你能解释一下你刚才的发言吗？

elude.meaning: v. 避开，逃避，使记不起
elude.note:
The thief managed to elude the police for weeks. 小偷设法躲避了警方几个星期。

Her name seemed to elude me for a moment. 我一时想不起她的名字了。

elusive.meaning: adj. 难捉摸的，难懂的，逃避的
elusive.note:
Success remained elusive despite all his hard work. 尽管他付出了所有努力，成功依然难以捉摸。

The elusive criminal was finally captured in another state. 这个行踪不定的罪犯最终在另一个州被捕。

emaciate.note:
Severe famine can emaciate a population rapidly. 严重的饥荒会迅速使人口消瘦衰弱。

The disease left the stray dog completely emaciated. 这种疾病让这只流浪狗瘦骨嶙峋。

emaciation.note:
Signs of severe emaciation were visible on the refugees. 难民身上有明显的严重消瘦迹象。

Medical staff treated the patient for extreme emaciation. 医务人员对该患者进行了极度消瘦的治疗。

emanate.note:
Delicious smells began to emanate from the kitchen. 美味的香味开始从厨房散发出来。

A sense of calm seemed to emanate from her. 一种平静感似乎从她身上散发出来。

embargo.note:
The government imposed a strict trade embargo on the country. 政府对该国实施了严厉的贸易禁运。

They hoped the oil embargo would force a policy change. 他们希望石油禁运能迫使政策改变。

embarrass.note:
He didn't mean to embarrass her with his question. 他并非有意用这个问题让她难堪。

I was afraid I might embarrass myself on stage. 我担心自己会在舞台上出丑。

embezzlement.note:
The former executive was arrested for embezzlement of funds. 这名前高管因挪用资金被捕。

Financial auditing helps prevent fraud and embezzlement. 财务审计有助于防止欺诈和贪污。

emblematic.note:
The bald eagle is emblematic of the United States. 白头海雕是美国的象征。

This single event is emblematic of a broader social crisis. 这一孤立事件象征着更广泛的社会危机。

embolden.note:
Emboldened by early success, they decided to expand the business. 在早期成功的鼓舞下，他们决定扩大业务。

Her supportive words emboldened him to speak up. 她支持的话语给了他开口说话的勇气。

emboss.note:
The company logo was embossed in gold on the business card. 公司标志以金色压印在名片上。

She used a special tool to emboss patterns on the leather. 她用特殊工具在皮革上压出图案。

embrace.note:
They shared a warm embrace at the airport terminal. 他们在机场航站楼温暖地拥抱。

We must embrace new technology to stay competitive. 我们必须拥抱新技术以保持竞争力。

embroider.meaning: v. 刺绣，修饰，渲染（故事）
embroider.note:
She likes to embroider flowers on cotton shirts. 她喜欢在棉质衬衫上绣花。

He tended to embroider the truth when telling stories. 他讲故事时往往会添枝加叶地渲染一番。

emend.note:
The editor had to emend several errors in the manuscript. 编辑必须修正手稿中的几个错误。

Scholars carefully emend ancient texts for publication. 学者们仔细修订古代文本以供出版。

emergency.meaning: n. 紧急情况，突发事件
emergency.note:
Call this number in case of a medical emergency. 如遇医疗紧急情况，请拨打此号码。

The pilot made an emergency landing due to engine failure. 飞行员因发动机故障作了紧急降落。

eminence.note:
He achieved international eminence in the field of physics. 他在物理学领域获得了国际显赫地位。

The scholar spoke from a position of academic eminence. 这位学者以其学术泰斗的崇高地位发言。

emissary.note:
The king sent a secret emissary to negotiate peace. 国王派出了一个秘密使者去谈判和平。

Diplomatic emissaries arrived in the capital for talks. 外交使节抵达首都进行会谈。

emit.meaning: v. 发出，放射（光、热、气等）
emit.note:
Vehicles emit harmful gases into the atmosphere. 汽车向大气中排放有害气体。

The device can emit a high-frequency sound to deter pests. 该装置能发出高频声音以驱赶害虫。

emollient.meaning: n. 润肤剂；adj. 润肤的，抚慰的
emollient.note:
Apply this emollient cream to soothe dry skin. 涂抹这款润肤霜以舒缓干燥皮肤。

Her emollient tone helped calm the angry customer. 她温和抚慰的语气有助于平息愤怒的顾客。

emote.meaning: v. 感情外露，戏剧性地表现感情
emote.note:
The actor was told not to over-emote during the dramatic scene. 演员被告知在戏剧场景中不要过度表现感情。

She tends to emote easily when discussing family topics. 谈到家庭话题时，她往往很容易情绪激动。

empiricism.note:
British empiricism emphasizes knowledge derived from sensory experience. 英国经验主义强调源自感官经验的知识。

His research is deeply rooted in scientific empiricism. 他的研究深深植根于科学经验主义。

empyreal.note:
The rocket soared into the empyreal heights. 火箭翱翔进入了高远的苍穹。

Artists often draw inspiration from empyreal beauty. 艺术家经常从天空的美丽中汲取灵感。

emulsify.note:
Vigorous shaking will help emulsify the oil and vinegar. 剧烈摇晃将有助于把油和醋乳化混合。

Certain chemicals are added to emulsify food ingredients. 添加某些化学物质是为了使食品成分乳化。

enamel.note:
Tooth enamel protects teeth from decay. 牙釉质保护牙齿免受侵蚀蛀牙。

The artist decorated the metal box with colorful enamel. 艺术家用彩色珐琅装饰了这个金属盒子。

enamored.note:
He was completely enamored of her charming personality. 他完全被她迷人的性格所倾倒。

She wasn't particularly enamored with the idea of moving. 她并不是特别热衷于搬家的想法。

encapsulate.note:
This single quote seems to encapsulate the entire movie. 这句单独的引言似乎概括了整部电影。

The software design helps encapsulate complex data. 软件设计有助于封装复杂的数据。

enchant.meaning: v. 施魔法，使陶醉，令着迷
enchant.note:
The magician tried to enchant the audience with illusions. 魔术师试图用幻术迷惑观众。

Children were enchanted by the fairy tale performance. 孩子们被童话表演深深迷住了。

enclosure.note:
Lions were kept in a large natural enclosure at the zoo. 狮子被养在动物园的一个大型自然围场里。

Please find my resume attached in the enclosure. 请查阅附件中附上的我的简历。

encomiast.meaning: n. 颂词撰写者，赞美者
encomiast.note:
The leader was surrounded by loyal encomiasts praising his rule. 领袖身边环绕着赞美其统治的忠实颂扬者。

He acted more as an encomiast than an objective biographer. 他与其说是个客观的传记作家，不如说是个赞美者。

encomium.note:
The book received high encomiums from literary critics. 这本书受到了文学评论家的高度赞誉。

She wrote a glowing encomium for her retiring mentor. 她为即将退休的导师写了一篇热烈的赞辞。

encounter.note:
We might encounter some minor traffic delays on the way. 我们在路上可能会遇到一些轻微的交通延误。

It was a brief encounter that left a lasting impression. 那是一次留下深刻印象的短暂邂逅。

encroach.note:
Urban development continues to encroach upon local wildlife habitats. 城市发展继续侵占当地的野生动物栖息地。

New laws aim to prevent companies from trying to encroach on privacy. 新法律旨在防止公司试图侵犯隐私。

encyclopedia.note:
She checked facts using an online encyclopedia. 她使用在线百科全书核对事实。

He has an encyclopedic knowledge of world history. 他对世界历史有着百科全书般的渊博知识。

endearing.meaning: adj. 可爱的，讨人喜欢的
endearing.note:
Her endearing smile won the hearts of the audience. 她那讨人喜欢的微笑赢得了观众的心。

He had several endearing quirks that people found amusing. 他有一些人们觉得挺有意思的可爱怪癖。

endow.note:
The wealthy philanthropist decided to endow a new university chair. 这位富有的慈善家决定资助一个新的大学讲席。

Nature has endowed dolphins with high intelligence. 大自然赋予了海豚高度的智慧。

enduring.note:
They formed an enduring friendship during their college years. 他们在大学期间建立了持久的友谊。

The play remains an enduring classic of modern theater. 这部戏剧依然是现代戏剧中不朽的经典。

enervate.meaning: v. 使衰弱，使失去活力
enervate.note:
The intense summer heat tended to enervate the workers. 强烈的夏日酷暑往往使工人们体力不支。

Chronic fatigue can enervate both body and mind. 慢性疲劳会使身心都感到衰弱。

enfetter.note:
Tyranny seeks to enfetter the freedom of speech. 暴政企图束缚言论自由。

They refused to let outdated traditions enfetter their creativity. 他们拒绝让过时的传统束缚他们的创造力。

enflame.note:
His angry speech only served to enflame the crowd. 他愤怒的演讲只会火上浇油地激怒群众。

Dry brushwood can easily enflame in the dry season. 干燥的灌木在旱季很容易被点燃。

engaged.meaning: adj. 订婚的，忙于...的，投入的
engaged.note:
They announced they were engaged to be married next spring. 他们宣布订婚，将于明年春天结婚。

She remained fully engaged throughout the lecture. 整个讲座过程中她都全神贯注地投入其中。

engender.note:
Trust can engender a positive working environment. 信任能够营造积极的工作环境。

His controversial remarks tended to engender deep division. 他具争议性的言论往往会引起深刻的分歧。

engulf.note:
High waves threatened to engulf the small fishing boat. 大海浪威胁要吞没这艘小型渔船。

Dark smoke began to engulf the burning building. 浓烟开始吞噬着燃烧的大楼。

enjoin.meaning: v. 命令，吩咐，禁止（法律用语）
enjoin.note:
The rules enjoin members from sharing confidential details. 规则禁止成员分享机密细节。

The judge chose to enjoin the company from selling the product. 法官选择颁布禁令禁止该公司销售该产品。

enlighten.note:
Could you enlighten me on the details of this policy? 你能向我阐明这项政策的细节吗？

Education helps enlighten young minds. 教育有助于启迪年轻的心灵。

enlightening.meaning: adj. 富有启迪性的，使人领悟的
enlightening.note:
The lecture on modern art was surprisingly enlightening. 关于现代艺术的讲座出人意料地富有启发性。

She found the discussion with the professor very enlightening. 她觉得与教授的讨论非常具有启发意义。

enlist.meaning: v. 征募，参军，争取（支持）
enlist.note:
He decided to enlist in the army after graduation. 他决定毕业后参军入伍。

The charity tried to enlist volunteers for the event. 慈善机构试图为该活动招募志愿者。

enliven.meaning: v. 使生动，使活跃，使有生气
enliven.note:
Bright flowers helped to enliven the dull room. 鲜艳的花朵有助于让沉闷的房间充满生机。

Some background music would enliven the party. 一些背景音乐会使派对更加活跃。

enmesh.note:
He found himself enmeshed in a web of complex debts. 他发现自己陷入了一张复杂的债务网中。
