The technical failure was a minor setback for the research team.技术故障对研究团队来说是一个小小的挫折。

We must not let this unexpected setback stop us from succeeding.我们决不能让这个意想不到的挫折阻止我们走向成功。

settled.meaning: adj. 安顿下来的；稳定的；确定的
settled.note:
After years of traveling, they finally lived a settled life in the suburbs.经过多年的旅行，他们终于在郊区过上了安顿下来的生活。

The weather remained warm and settled throughout the week.整个星期天气一直温暖且稳定。

sever.note:
A fallen tree branch managed to sever the power lines.树枝落下时切断了电力线。

The two countries decided to sever diplomatic ties after the conflict.冲突后两国决定断绝外交关系。

sextant.note:
The sailor used a brass sextant to calculate the ship's position at sea.水手用黄铜六分仪计算船在海上的位置。

Before modern GPS, navigators relied heavily on a traditional sextant.在现代GPS出现之前，航海员严重依赖传统的六分仪。

shackle.meaning: n. 脚镣；手铐；束缚 v. 束缚；加桎梏
shackle.note:
Prisoners were bound in heavy metal shackles during transport.囚犯在运送过程中被绑在沉重的金属脚镣里。

Regulations should not shackle the creative growth of small businesses.规章制度不应当束缚小企业的创新发展。

shale.note:
The mountain cliffs were composed of layered dark shale rock.山崖由层层叠叠的深色页岩组成。

Geologists found interesting fossils preserved inside the ancient shale.地质学家在古代页岩内部发现了保存完好的有趣化石。

sham.meaning: n. 虚假；骗局 adj. 虚假的 v. 假装
sham.note:
His friendly behavior turned out to be a complete sham.他的友好行为结果完全是个骗局。

She didn't really have a cold; she just shamed illness to stay home.她其实没有感冒；她只是假装生病留在家中。

shambles.meaning: n. 混乱状态；杂乱无章的地方；屠宰场
shambles.note:
The unexpected resignation left the department's schedule in a shambles.突如其来的辞职让部门的日程陷入了一片混乱。

After the wild party, the living room looked like an absolute shambles.疯狂派对过后，起居室看起来简直是一片杂乱无章。

shard.note:
He accidentally stepped on a sharp shard of broken glass.他不小心踩到了一块锋利的碎玻璃片。

Archaeologists carefully cataloged every pottery shard found in the dig.考古学家仔细编目了发掘中发现的每一块陶片。

shattered.meaning: adj. 粉碎的；极度疲惫的（动词shatter的过去分词）
shattered.note:
The stone caused the glass window to be completely shattered.石头导致玻璃窗被彻底粉碎。

After running the marathon, she felt completely shattered and tired.跑完马拉松后，她感到极度疲惫。

shavings.meaning: n. 刨花；削屑（名词shaving的复数形式）
shavings.note:
The floor of the woodworking shop was covered in wood shavings.木工车间的地板上铺满了木刨花。

He collected the dry pine shavings to start a campfire.他收集了干松木刨花来生营火。

shear.meaning: v. 剪（羊毛等）；修剪 n. 剪切
shear.note:
Farmers usually shear their sheep during the warm spring season.农民通常在温暖的春季给羊剪毛。

Strong winds can shear off the weak branches of old trees.强风可以剪断老树虚弱的树枝。

sheath.note:
He carefully slid his hunting knife back into its protective leather sheath.他小心翼翼地把猎刀滑回保护性的皮鞘里。

The wire is covered in a thick insulating plastic sheath.电线外面包裹着一层厚厚的绝缘塑料护套。

sheathe.meaning: v. 把（刀等）插入鞘；给…加护套
sheathe.note:
The warrior decided to sheathe his sword after the battle ended.战斗结束后，这位勇士决定把剑收入鞘中。

Cables are sheathed in rubber to protect them from moisture.电缆套上橡胶护套以防受潮。

sheer.meaning: adj. 纯粹的；陡峭的；薄而透明的
sheer.note:
The climb up the sheer rock face required immense physical strength.攀登陡峭的岩壁需要巨大的体力。

Her success was a result of sheer hard work and dedication.她的成功是纯粹的努力工作和奉献的结果。

shell.meaning: n. 贝壳；外壳；炮弹 v. 剥壳；炮击
shell.note:
Children collected pretty sea shells along the sandy beach.孩子们在沙滩上收集漂亮的贝壳。

He sat at the kitchen table to shell fresh green peas.他坐在餐桌旁剥新鲜的青豆。

shelter.meaning: n. 庇护所；掩蔽 v. 庇护；躲避
shelter.note:
Hikers built a temporary camp shelter to escape the rain storm.徒步旅行者搭建了一个临时的露营庇护所以躲避暴雨。

Trees provide natural shelter for small birds from strong winds.树木为小鸟提供防风的天然庇护。

shelve.meaning: v. 搁置；将…放置在架子上
shelve.note:
The committee decided to shelve the controversial plan indefinitely.委员会决定无限期搁置这个有争议的计划。

Books should be carefully classified and organized before you shelve them.在把书上架之前，应该仔细对它们进行分类和整理。

sheriff.note:
The county sheriff led the search for the missing hiker in the mountains.县治安官带队在山中搜寻失踪的徒步旅行者。

Local residents respected the fair and honest decisions of the sheriff.当地居民尊重警长公正诚实的决定。

shield.meaning: n. 盾；防护物 v. 保护；庇护
shield.note:
Ancient soldiers carried metal shields for protection in battle.古代士兵在战斗中携带金属盾牌以防身。

Sunglasses help shield your eyes from harmful ultraviolet rays.太阳镜有助于保护你的眼睛免受有害紫外线的伤害。

shiftiness.note:
His general shiftiness made everyone in the room distrust him.他总体的狡猾让房间里的每一个人都不信任他。

She sensed a subtle shiftiness in his answers to her questions.她在他对她问题的回答中察觉到了一种微妙的推诿。

shiftless.meaning: adj. 懒惰的；胸无大志的；没出息的
shiftless.note:
He was criticized for being a shiftless person who refused to work.他因是一个拒绝工作的没出息的人而受到批评。

Her shiftless attitude toward her career worried her parents.她对职业懒惰的态度让她的父母感到担忧。

shingle.meaning: n. 瓦；木板瓦；鹅卵石滩 v. 铺瓦
shingle.note:
Strong gales blew several wooden shingles off the roof.强烈的狂风把屋顶的几块木板瓦刮掉了。

Workers used new tiles to reshingle the leaking cottage roof.工人们用新瓦片重新铺了漏水的农舍屋顶。

shipshape.meaning: adj. 整洁的；井井有条的
shipshape.note:
They spent the whole morning cleaning and making the boat shipshape.他们花了一整个早上打扫卫生，把船收拾得井井有条。

Keep your work desk clean and shipshape before leaving.离开前把你的工作桌保持干净且井井有条。

shirk.meaning: v. 逃避；推卸（责任、工作等）
shirk.note:
A responsible employee should never try to shirk daily duties.负责任的员工绝不应该试图逃避日常职责。

He was fired because of his habitual tendency to shirk work.他因为习惯性地逃避工作而被解雇了。

shoal.note:
The boat ran aground on a hidden sand shoal near the coast.船在海岸附近的一个隐藏沙洲上搁浅了。

A massive shoal of silver fish swam past the coral reef.一大群银色的鱼游过了珊瑚礁。

shoddy.meaning: adj. 劣质的；偷工减料的
shoddy.note:
Consumers complained about the shoddy construction of the new houses.消费者抱怨新房屋的劣质施工。

He demanded a refund for the shoddy goods he bought online.他要求为他在网上买的劣质商品退款。

shoplift.meaning: v. 溜进商店偷窃；商店行窃
shoplift.note:
Security cameras caught the teenager trying to shoplift from the store.监控摄像头拍到那个青少年试图在店里行窃。

Shoplift is a serious crime that can result in criminal charges.商店行窃是一项严重的罪行，可能导致刑事指控。

shopworn.meaning: adj. 陈旧的；因陈列展示而磨损的
shopworn.note:
The bookstore offered a discount on shopworn paperback copies.书店对因陈列而磨损的平装书提供折扣。

These items look a bit shopworn after being on display for months.这些商品在展示了数月后看起来有点陈旧。

shoulder.meaning: n. 肩膀 v. 肩负；承担
shoulder.note:
He carried a heavy backpack strapped securely across his shoulders.他把一个沉重的背包牢牢地背在肩膀上。

Managers must be ready to shoulder the responsibility for failures.经理们必须准备好承担失败的责任。

shove.meaning: v. 推；挤；猛推 n. 推
shove.note:
He gave the heavy door a gentle shove to open it.他轻轻推了一下厚重的门把它打开。

People began to shove and push their way onto the crowded train.人们开始挤着进拥挤的火车。

shrewd.meaning: adj. 精明的；敏锐的；机灵的
shrewd.note:
She made a shrewd investment that doubled her savings in a year.她做了一笔精明的投资，在一年内使她的积蓄翻了一番。

His shrewd observations helped solve the business mystery.他精明的观察帮助解开了商业谜团。

shriek.meaning: n. 尖叫声 v. 尖叫
shriek.note:
Children let out a happy shriek as they jumped into the swimming pool.孩子们跳进游泳池时发出了快乐的尖叫声。

She heard a sudden shriek coming from the dark alleyway.她听到从黑暗的小巷里传出一声突如其来的尖叫。

shrine.note:
Pilgrims traveled long distances to visit the holy mountain shrine.朝圣者跋涉很远去参观那座神圣的山间神殿。

The family created a small memorial shrine for their lost pet.这个家里人为他们失去的宠物建立了一个小型纪念神龛。

shrink.note:
Washing this woolen sweater in hot water will make it shrink.用热水洗这件羊毛衫会使它缩水。

He refused to shrink from the difficult challenge ahead.他拒绝在面前的困难挑战前退缩。

shrub.note:
She planted green flowering shrubs along the edge of the garden.她在花园边缘种了绿色的开花灌木。

A small rabbit hid quietly behind a thick garden shrub.一只小兔子静静地藏在一株厚厚的园林灌木后面。

shuck.meaning: v. 剥去（壳、皮等） n. 外壳；包皮
shuck.note:
He sat on the porch to shuck fresh corn cobs for dinner.他坐在走廊上为晚餐剥新鲜的玉米棒皮。

She learned how to shuck oysters expertly at the seafood restaurant.她在海鲜餐厅学会了如何熟练地剥生蚝壳。

shudder.meaning: v. 发抖；战栗 n. 颤抖
shudder.note:
The cold wind made him shudder and pull his coat tighter.冷风让他直打哆嗦，把大衣裹得更紧了。

She felt a sudden shudder of fear run down her spine.她感到脊背一阵恐惧的战栗。

shunt.meaning: v. 分流；转轨；推卸 n. 分流器；转辙
shunt.note:
Railway workers had to shunt the damaged train cars onto a side track.铁路工人不得不把受损的火车车厢转轨到侧轨上。

Doctors used a medical tube to shunt fluids away from the brain.医生使用一根医疗管把脑部的液体分流出去。

sibilant.meaning: adj. 发嘶嘶声的 n. 齿擦音
sibilant.note:
She whispered a secret with a soft, sibilant sound.她用一种轻柔的、带有嘶嘶声的声音耳语了一个秘密。

Phonetics describes 's' and 'sh' as typical sibilant sounds.语音学将“s”和“sh”描述为典型的齿擦音。

sibling.note:
She grew up sharing a bedroom with her younger brother and sibling.她从小和弟弟等手足兄弟姐妹共用一间卧室。

Sibling rivalry is a common phenomenon in many families.兄弟姐妹间的竞争在许多家庭中是一种常见现象。

sibyl.note:
Ancient Greeks consulted the legendary Delphic sibyl for future advice.古希腊人向传说中的德尔斐女先知征求未来的建议。

Her mysterious predictions made people compare her to an ancient sibyl.她神秘的预言让人们把她比作古代女先知。

sidereal.note:
Astronomers use a sidereal clock to measure time based on stars.天文学家使用恒星钟根据星星来测量时间。

Sidereal time is different from standard solar time calculations.恒星时不同于标准太阳时计算。

sideshow.meaning: n. 杂耍；穿插节目；次要事件
sideshow.note:
The carnival featured a funny circus sideshow attraction.狂欢节上有一个有趣的马戏杂耍穿插节目。

The political dispute became just a sideshow to the main economic crisis.这场政治争端最终成了主要经济危机的一个次要插曲。

sidestep.meaning: v. 回避；侧身躲开 n. 侧步
sidestep.note:
The politician tried to sidestep the difficult question from reporters.这位政治家试图回避记者提出的尖锐问题。

She managed to sidestep the falling branch just in time.她及时侧身躲开了掉落的树枝。

siege.meaning: n. 围困；包围；长期围攻
siege.note:
The medieval castle successfully withstood a long military siege.这座中世纪城堡成功经受住了长时间的军事围困。

The city was placed under a tight military siege for months.这座城市被实施了数月的紧密军事包围。

sift.note:
She used a wire mesh to sift flour before baking the cake.她在烤蛋糕前用金属网筛面粉。

Detectives had to sift through thousands of documents for clues.侦探们必须仔细检查数千份文件以寻找线索。

signal.meaning: n. 信号；暗号 v. 发信号 adj. 显赫的
signal.note:
The traffic light changed to red as a stop signal.交通灯变成红色作为停止信号。

He raised his hand to signal the waiter for the bill.他举起手向服务员示意买单。

sill.note:
She placed a small pot of green flowers on the window sill.她在窗台上放了一小盆绿色的花。

Rainwater leaked under the wooden door sill during the storm.暴风雨期间，雨水从木门槛下方渗了进来。

silt.meaning: n. 淤泥；泥沙 v. 淤塞
silt.note:
Thick layers of river silt accumulated near the dam gates.厚厚的河道淤泥在水坝闸门附近积聚。

Sand and mud began to silt up the small harbor channel.沙子和泥土开始使小型港口航道淤塞。

silversmith.note:
The skilled silversmith crafted a beautiful ornamental silver bowl.这位熟练的银匠制作了一个精美的装饰性银碗。

He apprenticed with a master silversmith to learn metal engraving.他跟随一位银匠大师做学徒以学习金属雕刻。

simper.note:
She gave a silly simper when her name was called.当叫到她的名字时，她傻笑了一下。

He didn't like people who simper instead of speaking honestly.他不喜欢那些不诚实说话反而假笑的人。

simpleton.note:
Don't play the simpleton with me; you know what I mean. 别在我面前装傻充愣，你知道我的意思。

He was easily fooled because people thought him a simpleton. 他很容易被骗，因为人们认为他是个傻子。

sinecure.note:
The position looked like a comfortable sinecure with few actual duties.这个职位看起来像是一个没有什么实际职责的舒适闲职。

He resigned from the political sinecure to pursue independent writing.他辞去了政治挂名职务以从事独立写作。

sinew.note:
Sturdy physical labor developed the strong sinews of his arms.结实的体力劳动锻炼了他手臂强壮的肌肉腱。

Hard work is the true sinew of economic growth.努力工作是经济增长真正的力量之源。

singe.meaning: v.微烧焦；烫焦 n.烧焦痕迹
singe.note:
He accidentally managed to singe his eyebrows near the fireplace.他在壁炉旁时不小心把眉毛给微烧焦了。

The hot curling iron left a small singe mark on her hair.热卷发棒在她的头发上留下了一个小小的烧焦痕迹。

singularity.note:
Physicists study the black hole singularity at the center of galaxies.物理学家研究银河系中心的黑洞奇点。

Her writing style has a distinct singularity that charms readers.她的写作风格有一种吸引读者的鲜明独特性。

sinuous.note:
The river followed a sinuous path through the dense jungle.河水穿过密林走了一条蜿蜒的路径。

A sinuous mountain road led drivers up to the high peak.一条迂回曲折的山路引领司机们开往高峰。

sip.note:
She sat on the balcony to sip her warm morning tea.她坐在阳台上啜饮早晨的温茶。

He took a small sip of the hot soup to test its flavor.他喝了一小口热汤来尝尝它的味道。

skeleton.note:
Archaeologists uncovered a complete dinosaur skeleton in the desert.考古学家在沙漠中发掘出一具完整的恐龙骨骼。

The building was reduced to a bare steel skeleton after the fire.火灾过后，这栋建筑物只剩下一个光秃秃的钢骨架。

sketchy.meaning: adj.粗略的；不完全的；可疑的
sketchy.note:
Police only had sketchy details about the suspect's appearance.警察只有关于嫌疑人外貌的粗略细节。

They decided to avoid the neighborhood because it looked sketchy.他们决定避开那个街区，因为它看起来有些可疑。

skiff.note:
The fisherman rowed his small wooden skiff across the calm lake.渔民划着他的小木船穿过平静的湖面。

They tied the light skiff securely to the wooden dock.他们把轻舟稳稳地系在木质码头上。

skillet.note:
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. 在大煎锅中用中火加热油。

She fried the bacon and eggs in an iron skillet. 她在一个铁煎锅里煎了培根和鸡蛋。

skim.note:
Skim the fat off the surface of the soup. 把汤表面的油脂撇掉。

He had time only to skim through the newspaper. 他当时只有时间浏览一下报纸。

skimp.note:
Do not skimp on the ingredients if you want the cake to taste good. 如果你想让蛋糕好吃，就不要在食材上吝啬。

They had to skimp on heating to save money. 他们为了省钱不得不节省取暖开支。

skinflint.note:
The old skinflint refused to give any money to charity. 那个老吝啬鬼拒绝给慈善机构捐一分钱。

He is such a skinflint that he reuses paper towels. 他是个极其吝啬的人，连纸巾都要重复使用。

skirmish.meaning: n. 小冲突；v. 发生小冲突
skirmish.note:
A border skirmish broke out between the two patrols. 两支巡逻队之间爆发了一场边境小冲突。

Minor skirmishes occurred during the peaceful protest. 和平抗议期间发生了几起小型冲突。

skit.meaning: n. 幽默短剧；滑稽讽刺小品
skit.note:
The students performed a funny skit at the school assembly. 学生们在学校集会上表演了一个滑稽的短剧。

The TV show featured a political skit satirizing the election. 电视节目播放了一段讽刺选举的政治小品。

slack.meaning: adj. 松弛的；萧条的；v. 松懈；怠慢
slack.note:
The rope was pulled too slack and needed to be tightened. 绳子拉得太松了，需要拉紧。

Business is always slack during the winter months. 冬季几个月的生意总是很清淡。

slacken.note:
The runner began to slacken his pace near the finish line. 赛跑选手在终点线附近开始放慢速度。

Rain caused traffic to slacken in the downtown area. 下雨导致市中心交通缓慢下来。

slag.meaning: n. 炉渣；矿渣；v. 贬低
slag.note:
The steel plant produced tons of waste slag every day. 这家钢铁厂每天产生数吨废炉渣。

It is not polite to slag your colleagues behind their backs. 在背后贬低同事是不礼貌的。

slake.meaning: v. 熄灭；满足（欲望或口渴）
slake.note:
Cold water helped to slake his thirst after a long run. 长跑过后，冷水帮他解了渴。

Nothing could slake her immense curiosity about history. 什么也无法满足她对历史的巨大好奇心。

slander.note:
He sued the newspaper for commercial slander. 他因商业诽谤起诉了这家报社。

She claimed that the rumors were intended to slander her reputation. 她声称这些谣言旨在诋毁她的名誉。

slanderous.note:
The politician threatened to sue over the slanderous article. 这位政治家威胁要就这篇诽谤性文章起诉。

He made several slanderous remarks about his former business partner. 他对前商业伙伴发表了几处诽谤性的言论。

slate.meaning: n. 板岩；石板；候选人名单；v. 计划；安排
slate.note:
The roof of the old cottage is made of dark slate. 那座老农舍的屋顶是用深色板岩铺成的。

She is slated to become the next department director. 她被预定为下一任部门主任。

sleigh.note:
They went for a festive ride on a horse-drawn sleigh. 他们乘坐马拉雪橇进行了一次节日游玩。

Children played happily with a wooden sleigh in the snow. 孩子们在雪地里开心地玩着木制雪橇。

slew.meaning: n. 大量；许多；v. 旋转；扭转
slew.note:
The company faced a whole slew of financial problems this year. 这家公司今年面临着一大堆财务问题。

The car suddenly slewed across the icy road. 汽车突然在结冰的路面上打滑旋转。

slight.meaning: adj. 轻微的；纤细的；n./v. 轻视；冷落
slight.note:
There is a slight chance of rain this afternoon. 今天下午有微小的降雨可能。

He felt insulted by her intentional slight at the party. 他对她在派对上的故意冷落感到受辱。

slippage.note:
There was some slippage in our production schedule this month. 我们这个月的生产进度有些许滞后。

We must prevent any slippage in product quality. 我们必须防止产品质量出现任何下滑。

slippery.note:
The wet pavement made walking very slippery. 湿漉漉的人行道走起来非常滑。

He is a slippery character who cannot be trusted. 他是一个不可信赖的滑头人物。

slipshod.note:
Her slipshod work resulted in numerous errors in the report. 她草率的工作导致报告中出现大量错误。

We cannot tolerate such slipshod maintenance practices. 我们不能容忍这种草率的维护做法。

slither.note:
A large snake began to slither through the tall grass. 一条大蛇开始穿过高高的草丛滑行。

Children love to slither down the muddy bank. 孩子们喜欢顺着泥泞的河岸往下滑。

sliver.meaning: n. 细片；狭长的碎片；v. 切成薄片
sliver.note:
A tiny wooden sliver got stuck in his finger. 一根极小的木刺扎进了他的手指。

Only a sliver of hope remained for their rescue. 他们获救的希望只剩下一线。

sloppy.meaning: adj. 马虎的；邋遢的；多水的
sloppy.note:
His sloppy handwriting made the note difficult to read. 他潦草的字迹让人很难看清便条上的字。

She wore a sloppy sweater and jeans on the weekend. 周末她穿着一件宽松邋遢的毛衣和牛仔裤。

slot.meaning: n. 狭缝；凹槽；时间段；v. 把…放入狭缝
slot.note:
Insert the coin into the slot to start the machine. 把硬币投入狭缝以启动机器。

We managed to secure a prime time slot for our advertisement. 我们设法为广告争取到了一个黄金时段。

sloth.note:
He struggled hard to overcome his natural sloth and work harder. 他努力克服自己天生的懒惰，更加努力地工作。

A three-toed sloth hung quietly from the branch of the tree. 一只三趾树懒静静地挂在树枝上。

slouch.meaning: v./n. 没精打采地站/坐/走；驼背
slouch.note:
Sit up straight and do not slouch in your chair. 坐直，不要在椅子上驼背。

He slouched against the wall while waiting for the bus. 他靠在墙上，没精打采地等车。

slough.meaning: n. 绝境；沼泽；v. 蜕皮；脱落
slough.note:
Many snakes slough their skin as they grow larger. 许多蛇在长大时会蜕皮。

She managed to slough off her feelings of depression. 她设法摆脱了抑郁的情绪。

sluggard.note:
The lazy manager called his inactive employees sluggards. 这位懒散的经理称他懒惰的员工为懒汉。

Rise early and do not act like a sluggard in the morning. 早起，清晨不要像个懒汉一样。

sluice.meaning: n. 水闸；冲洗槽；v. 用水冲洗
sluice.note:
Workers opened the sluice to drain excess water from the dam. 工人们打开水闸排空大坝多余的水。

He used a hose to sluice the mud off the driveway. 他用软管把车道上的泥巴冲洗干净。

slumber.note:
The tired baby finally drifted into a peaceful slumber. 疲惫的婴儿终于进入了安稳的睡眠。

The small village slumbered quietly under the moonlight. 小村庄在月光下寂静地沉睡着。

slur.meaning: n. 诋毁；模糊不清的发音；v. 含糊不清地说；连奏
slur.note:
Drinking too much caused him to slur his words. 饮酒过度导致他说话含糊不清。

He wanted to clear his name from the malicious slur. 他想洗清恶意诋毁给他的清白带来的污点。

slurp.meaning: v./n. 出声地吃或喝；吸溜
slurp.note:
It is considered bad manners to slurp your soup in public. 在公共场合喝汤发出声响被认为是不礼貌的。

He happily slurped down the rest of his noodles. 他开心地把剩下的面条吸溜着吃完了。

sly.meaning: adj. 狡猾的；机密的；偷偷的
sly.note:
He gave her a sly smile as if he knew a secret. 他向她露出一抹狡猾的微笑，仿佛他知道一个秘密。

With a sly movement, he hid the card behind his back. 凭借一个偷偷的动作，他把牌藏在了身后。

smarmy.meaning: adj. 虚情假意的；谄媚的
smarmy.note:
I disliked the salesman because of his smarmy attitude. 我不喜欢那个推销员，因为他那虚情假意的态度。

He gave a smarmy compliment that sounded totally insincere. 他说了一句听起来毫无诚意的谄媚奉承话。

smart.meaning: adj. 聪明的；敏捷的；时髦的；v. 刺痛
smart.note:
She is a smart student who always gets top grades. 她是一个聪明的学生，总是拿最高分。

His eyes began to smart from the heavy smoke. 浓烟熏得他的眼睛开始刺痛。

smattering.meaning: n. 略知；少数；浅显知识
smattering.note:
He has only a smattering of knowledge about French art. 他对法国艺术只有一点浅薄的了解。

Only a smattering of people attended the morning lecture. 只有寥寥少数人听了早上的讲座。

smear.meaning: v. 涂抹；弄脏；n. 污迹；诽谤
smear.note:
The child managed to smear jam all over the table. 这孩子把果酱抹得满桌子都是。

Political opponents tried to run a smear campaign against him. 政治对手试图对其实施诽谤运动。

smirk.meaning: n./v. 得意洋洋的笑；假笑
smirk.note:
He wore a self-satisfied smirk after winning the game. 赢得比赛后，他脸上挂着一副自鸣得意的假笑。

Do not smirk when someone else makes a mistake. 别人犯错时不要幸灾乐祸地笑。

smooth.meaning: adj. 光滑的；平稳的；v. 使平滑；弄平
smooth.note:
The surface of the lake was as smooth as glass. 湖面平静得像一面镜子。

She tried to smooth her ruffled hair before entering the office. 她在进办公室前试图把弄乱的头发抚平。

smother.meaning: v. 闷死；窒息；掩盖；厚厚地覆盖
smother.note:
He tried to smother the small campfire with soil. 他试图用泥土把小型营火扑灭。

She loved to smother her steak in mushroom sauce. 她喜欢在牛排上厚厚地浇上一层蘑菇汁。

smudge.meaning: n. 污迹；痕迹；v. 弄脏；涂模糊
smudge.note:
There was an ink smudge on the student's homework sheet. 学生的作业纸上有一处墨迹。

Be careful not to smudge the freshly written ink. 小心别把刚写的墨水弄模糊了。

smug.meaning: adj. 自满的；自以为是的
smug.note:
He looked entirely too smug after passing the test easily. 他轻松通过考试后显得十分自鸣得意。

Avoid a smug attitude when dealing with peers. 与同伴相处时要避免自以为是的态度。

smuggle.note:
Customs officers caught the man trying to smuggle diamonds. 海关官员抓住了这个试图走私钻石的男子。

They attempted to smuggle the prohibited items across the border. 他们试图把违禁品走私过境。

snarl.meaning: v. 咆哮，怒骂；（交通等）混乱堵塞
snarl.note:
The angry dog began to snarl at the approaching stranger. 生气的狗开始向走近的陌生人咆哮。

A minor accident caused a huge traffic snarl on the bridge. 一起小事故导致桥上交通大拥堵。

snatch.meaning: v./n. 夺取；抢夺；抓紧时间获取
snatch.note:
The thief tried to snatch her handbag from her shoulder. 小偷试图从她肩上抢走手提包。

She managed to snatch a few minutes of rest before lunch. 她设法在午饭前抽空休息了几分钟。

sneaking.meaning: adj. 暗中生出的；隐约的
sneaking.note:
He had a sneaking suspicion that he was being followed. 他隐约有一种自己被人跟踪的怀疑。

She felt a sneaking admiration for his bold decision. 她对他的果断决定油生了一种暗暗的敬佩。

sneer.note:
He responded with a sneer when told about the new idea. 听到这个新想法时，他冷笑了一声作为回应。

Do not sneer at other people's honest efforts. 不要嘲笑别人真诚的努力。

snide.meaning: adj. 讽刺的；含沙射影的；卑鄙的
snide.note:
She made several snide remarks about his new outfit. 她对他的新衣服发表了几句讽刺的话。

He dislikes working with people who make snide comments behind backs. 他不喜欢与那些在背后说风凉话的人共事。

snip.note:
She used scissors to snip the loose thread from her coat. 她用剪刀剪掉了大衣上的松散线头。

At this price, the jacket is an absolute snip. 这个价格买这件夹克绝对是大便宜。

snitch.note:
Someone chose to snitch on the students breaking the rules. 有人选择向老师告发违纪的学生。

He was accused of trying to snitch a pen from the office desk. 他被指控企图偷走办公桌上的一支笔。

snobbish.meaning: adj. 势利的；自命不凡的
snobbish.note:
She has a snobbish attitude toward people from small towns. 她对小城镇来的人有一种势利的态度。

His snobbish behavior made it difficult to make friends. 他那种高傲势利的行为让人很难交到朋友。

snowdrift.meaning: n. 雪堆；风吹成的雪堆
snowdrift.note:
The car got stuck in a massive snowdrift on the rural road. 汽车陷在乡间公路上一个巨大的雪堆里。

Children played by jumping into a soft snowdrift. 孩子们通过跳进松软的雪堆里玩耍。

snub.note:
She deliberately chose to snub him at the reception. 她在招待会上故意选择冷落他。

The director's proposal suffered a major snub from the board. 董事会无情地拒绝了这位总监的提议。

sober.meaning: adj. 清醒的；严肃的；朴素的
sober.note:
He remained totally sober throughout the entire evening. 他一整晚都保持完全清醒。

The news of the accident put everyone in a sober mood. 事故的消息让每个人的心情都变得沉重严肃。

sobriety.note:
He has maintained his sobriety for over five years now. 他已经保持戒酒清醒五年多了。

The occasion demanded a high degree of sobriety and respect. 这一场合需要高度的严肃和尊重。

sod.meaning: n. 草皮；草皮地；v. 铺草皮
sod.note:
Workers laid fresh sod in the front yard of the house. 工人们在房子的前院铺上了新鲜草皮。

The green sod was damp from the morning dew. 绿色的草皮被早晨的露水打湿了。

sodden.note:
His clothes were completely sodden after walking in the rain. 在雨中行走后，他的衣服完全湿透了。

The sodden ground made it impossible to pitch a tent. 浸透水分的地面让人无法搭帐篷。

soggy.meaning: adj. 湿漉漉的；软塌塌的
soggy.note:
The cereal became soggy after sitting too long in the milk. 麦片在牛奶里泡太久后变得软塌塌的。

We had to walk through soggy fields during our hike. 我们在远足时不得不穿过湿漉漉的田野。

solace.note:
She found great solace in reading books during tough times. 在艰难时期，她从读书中找到了极大的慰藉。

Music can solace the soul when you are feeling sad. 当你感到悲伤时，音乐可以慰藉心灵。

solder.meaning: n. 焊料；焊锡；v. 焊接
solder.note:
He used an iron tool to melt the solder onto the circuit board. 他用电烙铁将焊锡熔化到电路板上。

The technician needs to solder the loose wire back into place. 技术员需要把松动的电线焊接回原位。

solemn.meaning: adj. 庄严的；严肃的；隆重的
solemn.note:
They made a solemn promise to support each other forever. 他们作出了永远互相支持的庄严承诺。

The funeral was held in a very solemn atmosphere. 葬礼在非常严肃的氛围中举行。

solemnity.note:
Everyone maintained quiet solemnity during the national anthem. 在国歌奏响期间，所有人都保持着静默与庄严。

The solemnity of the ceremony impressed all the guests. 仪式的隆重给所有客人都留下了深刻印象。

solicit.note:
The organization plans to solicit donations for local schools. 该组织计划为当地学校募集捐款。

Management decided to solicit feedback from all staff members. 管理层决定向所有员工征求反馈意见。

solicitous.note:
She was always solicitous about the health of her elderly parents. 她总是十分关切年迈父母的健康。

He showed a solicitous interest in her well-being. 他对她的近况表现出了关切的兴趣。

solicitude.note:
He appreciated the warm solicitude shown by his neighbors. 他很感激邻居们表现出的热切关怀。

Her constant solicitude sometimes felt a bit overwhelming. 她无微不至的牵挂有时让人觉得有点难以承受。

solidarity.note:
Workers went on strike in solidarity with their colleagues. 工人们罢工以声援他们的同事。

The international community showed great solidarity with the disaster victims. 国际社会对灾民表现出了极大的团结。

solitary.meaning: adj. 独自的；单独的；荒凉的
solitary.note:
He enjoyed taking solitary walks along the empty beach. 他喜欢沿着空无一人的海滩独自散步。

She lived a solitary life in a remote mountain cabin. 她在一间偏远的山间小屋里过着隐居的生活。

solo.meaning: adj./adv. 独奏的；单独的；n. 独奏曲
solo.note:
She performed a stunning violin solo at the concert. 她在音乐会上表演了一场惊艳的小提琴独奏。

He successfully completed his first solo flight across the country. 他成功完成了他的第一次全国单飞飞行。

somatic.note:
Stress can sometimes manifest as physical or somatic symptoms. 压力有时会表现为身体或躯体症状。

The study focuses on somatic cells rather than reproductive cells. 这项研究侧重于体细胞而非生殖细胞。

somber.meaning: adj. 阴暗的；忧郁的；严肃的
somber.note:
The walls were painted in a somber shade of grey. 墙壁被涂成了一种忧郁的灰色调。

The news created a somber mood throughout the office. 这条消息在整个办公室里营造了一种凝重忧郁的气氛。

sonata.note:
She played a difficult Beethoven piano sonata with great skill. 她以高超的技巧弹奏了一首高难度的贝多芬钢琴奏鸣曲。

The classical concert featured a beautiful violin sonata. 音乐会的主打节目是一首优美的小提琴奏鸣曲。

sonnet.note:
Shakespeare is famous for writing brilliant English sonnets. 莎士比亚以创作出色的英国十四行诗而闻名。

She read a romantic sonnet during the literature class. 她在文学课上朗读了一首浪漫的十四行诗。

soot.note:
The inside of the fireplace was blackened with thick soot. 壁炉内部被厚厚的煤烟熏黑了。

Exhaust pipes can emit dark soot if the engine is poorly tuned. 如果发动机调校不当，排气管会排出黑色的煤烟。

soothe.meaning: v. 抚慰；缓和；减轻（痛苦）
soothe.note:
Soft music helped to soothe the crying baby. 轻柔的音乐有助于抚慰哭泣的婴儿。

A warm bath can help to soothe aching muscles. 洗个热水澡有助于缓解酸痛的肌肉。

sop.meaning: n. 贿赂；湿块；v. 浸湿
sop.note:
He used bread to sop up the delicious sauce on his plate. 他用面包蘸着吃盘子里美味的酱汁。

The financial grant was seen merely as a sop to critics. 这笔财政拨款被视为仅仅是对批评者的安抚贿赂。

sophism.note:
His argument was dismissed as a clever piece of sophism. 他的论点被当作一段聪明的诡辩而遭到反驳。

Do not let tricky sophism obscure the clear truth. 不要让狡猾的诡辩掩盖清晰的真相。

sophistication.note:
Her speech showed a high degree of political sophistication. 她的演讲显示出很高的政治成熟度与老练。

The new technology brings a new level of sophistication to manufacturing. 这项新技术给制造业带来了更高水平的复杂精密性。

sophistry.note:
The politician's speech was full of empty rhetoric and sophistry. 这位政治家的演讲充满了空洞的修辞和诡辩。

We must see through his elaborate sophistry. 我们必须看穿他精心编造的诡辩。

soporific.meaning: adj. 催眠的；n. 安眠药
soporific.note:
The boring lecture had a distinctly soporific effect on the audience. 这场沉闷的讲座对观众产生了明显的催眠效果。

Warm milk is often used as a natural soporific. 温牛奶常被用作天然的安眠饮品。

sopping.note:
He arrived home with his clothes sopping wet from the rain. 他冒雨回家，衣服都被雨水湿透了。

Wring out the sopping towel before hanging it up. 把湿透的毛巾拧干再挂起来。

sorcery.note:
The fairy tale is about a young wizard fighting dark sorcery. 这个童话故事讲述了一个年轻巫师对抗黑暗巫术的故事。

Ancient villagers feared the practice of witchcraft and sorcery. 古代村民害怕巫术和魔法的施展。

sordid.meaning: adj. 肮脏的；卑鄙的；龌龊的
sordid.note:
The newspaper exposed the sordid details of the political scandal. 报纸揭露了这起政治丑闻的卑鄙细节。

They lived in a sordid apartment in a poor neighborhood. 他们住在贫民区一间肮脏破旧的公寓里。

souvenir.note:
She bought a small wooden carving as a souvenir of her trip. 她买了一个精致的小木雕作为旅行的纪念品。

Tickets can serve as a nice souvenir of a memorable concert. 门票可以作为难忘音乐会的一份美好纪念品。

sovereign.meaning: adj. 具有主权的；最高权力的；n. 君主
sovereign.note:
The country declared itself an independent and sovereign state. 该国宣布自己是一个独立自主的主权国家。

The historic treaty was signed by the reigning sovereign. 这份历史性条约由当朝君主签署。

sovereignty.note:
The government vowed to protect national sovereignty at all costs. 政府发誓不惜一切代价捍卫国家主权。

Territorial disputes often threaten regional peace and national sovereignty. 领土争端往往威胁到地区和平与国家主权。

spackle.meaning: n. 墙面修补膏；v. 修补墙面
spackle.note:
Use spackle to fill in the small holes in the wall before painting. 刷漆前用墙面修补膏填平墙上的小洞。

He spackled the cracks in the drywall and sanded them smooth. 他用修补膏补好了干墙上的裂缝并将其打磨平整。

span.meaning: n. 跨度；期间；v. 持续；贯穿
span.note:
Her professional career spanned over three decades. 她的职业生涯跨越了三十多年。

The bridge has a single span crossing the wide river. 这座桥有一跨横跨宽阔的河流。

sparing.note:
Be sparing with the salt when cooking this dish. 做这道菜时盐要放得节约一点。

He was sparing in his praise for the new employee. 他对新员工的表扬显得有些吝啬。

sparring.meaning: n./v. 实战练习；争论；争辩
sparring.note:
The boxers engaged in light sparring during the training session. 拳击手在训练期间进行了轻度的实战对抗练习。

The two politicians enjoyed verbal sparring during the interview. 这两位政治家在采访中喜欢进行口头上的针锋相对。

sparse.note:
Vegetation is rather sparse in the dry desert region. 干燥的沙漠地区植被相当稀疏。

Details about the new project remain sparse at this stage. 现阶段有关新项目的细节仍然很少。

spartan.meaning: adj. 简朴的；刻苦的；斯巴达式的
spartan.note:
The monks lived a spartan life with very few material comforts. 修士们过着简朴的生活，几乎没有什么物质享受。

The training camp had spartan conditions with basic accommodation. 训练营条件十分简朴，只有基本的住宿设施。

spat.meaning: n./v. 小争吵；口角；吐唾沫
spat.note:
The couple had a brief spat over who should wash the dishes. 这对夫妇为谁洗碗发生了一场小口角。

They quickly made up after their minor domestic spat. 在那次家庭小争吵之后，他们很快就和好了。

spate.meaning: n. 大量；爆发；接连发生
spate.note:
A spate of burglaries hit the neighborhood last week. 上周该社区发生了一连串入室盗窃案。

The company announced a new spate of products for the autumn. 公司宣布在秋季推出一系列新产品。

spatial.meaning: adj. 空间的；存在于空间的
spatial.note:
Architects must have a strong sense of spatial awareness. 建筑师必须具备很强的空间意识感。

The exhibition explores the spatial relationship between art and architecture. 展览探讨了艺术与建筑之间的空间关系。

spear.meaning: n. 矛；标枪；v. 用矛刺
spear.note:
Ancient hunters used a sharp spear to catch fish in the river. 古代猎人使用锋利的标枪在河里捕鱼。

He managed to spear a piece of meat with his fork. 他设法用叉子叉起了一块肉。

specialize.note:
The clinic chooses to specialize in sports medicine. 这家诊所选择专攻运动医学。

Many law firms specialize in corporate intellectual property. 许多律师事务所专门从事公司知识产权业务。

specialized.note:
The job requires specialized training and technical skills. 这项工作需要专门的培训和技术技能。

Surgeons use specialized instruments for delicate operations. 外科医生在精细手术中使用专用器械。

specifics.note:
We need to discuss the financial specifics of the contract. 我们需要讨论合同的具体财务细节。

He gave general instructions without going into specifics. 他给出了总体指示，没有深入具体细节。

specimen.note:
Scientists collected a rare plant specimen in the rainforest. 科学家在雨林中收集到了一份珍稀植物标本。

The doctor asked the patient to provide a blood specimen. 医生要求患者提供一份血液样本。

specious.meaning: adj. 似是而非的；华而不实的
specious.note:
His argument sounded impressive, but it was completely specious. 他的论点听起来很impressive，但完全是似是而非的。

Do not be misled by specious promises from unreliable sources. 不要被不可靠来源发出的华而不实的承诺所误导。

speck.note:
There was a tiny speck of dust on the camera lens. 相机镜头上有一粒极小的灰尘斑点。

Not a speck of cloud could be seen in the blue sky. 蔚蓝的天空中连一丝云彩也看不到。

specter.meaning: n. 幽灵；挥之不去的恐惧；幻影
specter.note:
The specter of economic recession hung over the global market. 经济衰退的阴影笼罩着全球市场。

Old family secrets haunted him like a lingering specter. 古老的家族秘密像一个挥之不去的幽灵一样困扰着他。

spectrum.note:
The political party appeals to a broad spectrum of voters. 这个政党吸引了范围广泛的选民。

White light can be separated into a spectrum of colors. 白光可以被分解成各种颜色的光谱。

spendthrift.meaning: n. 挥霍无度的人；adj. 浪费的
spendthrift.note:
He was a notorious spendthrift who wasted all his inheritance. 他是一个声名狼籍的挥霍者，败光了所有的遗产。

Her spendthrift habits left her deeply in debt. 她挥霍无度的习惯让她陷入了严重的债务危机。

spike.meaning: n. 尖刺，激增；v. 猛增，钉上钉子
spike.note:
There was a sudden spike in electricity consumption this summer. 今年夏天电力消耗突然激增。

Running shoes usually have metal spikes on the soles for grip. 跑步鞋鞋底通常有金属钉以增加抓地力。

spin.meaning: v./n. 旋转；纺织；对事件的片面解读
spin.note:
The washing machine began to spin at a very high speed. 洗衣机开始以极高的速度旋转。

Politicians often try to put a positive spin on bad news. 政治家经常试图对坏消息进行美化和正面解读。

spindly.note:
The young tomato plant had a tall and spindly stem. 这棵年轻的番茄苗长着一根细长的茎。

He walked on his long, spindly legs across the room. 他迈着细长瘦弱的腿穿过了房间。

spineless.meaning: adj. 没骨气的；懦弱的；无脊椎的
spineless.note:
He was criticized for his spineless response to the crisis. 他因面对危机时表现得懦弱无骨气而受到批评。

Jellyfish are classified as spineless marine creatures. 水母被归类为无脊椎海洋生物。

spiny.note:
Cacti are well known for their thick and spiny leaves. 仙人掌以其厚实带刺的叶子而闻名。

The committee had to deal with a spiny legal question. 委员会不得不处理一个棘手的法律问题。

spire.note:
The church spire could be seen from miles away. 从数英里外就能看到这座教堂的尖顶。

Sharp stone spires rose high into the cloudy sky. 尖锐的石头尖塔高耸入云。

spiritual.meaning: adj. 精神的；心灵的；宗教的
spiritual.note:
Yoga helps many people achieve physical and spiritual balance. 瑜伽帮助许多人实现了身心平衡。

She found deep spiritual comfort in meditation. 她在冥想中找到了深厚的心灵慰藉。

spleen.note:
The doctor examined the patient's enlarged spleen. 医生检查了病人的肿大脾脏。

He vented all his political spleen in a long opinion piece. 他在一篇长篇评论文章中宣泄了自己所有的政治怨气。

splendor.note:
They visited the palace to admire its architectural splendor. 他们参观了宫殿以赞叹其建筑的宏伟壮丽。

Autumn leaves display a natural splendor of colors. 秋叶展现出一种大自然的色彩辉煌。

splice.note:
The technician had to splice the broken cables back together. 技术员必须把断裂的电缆重新拼接起来。

Film editors spliced the interview clips into a single documentary. 剪辑师将采访片段拼接成了一部完整的纪录片。

splint.meaning: n. 夹板；v. 用夹板固定
splint.note:
The paramedic used a wooden splint to stabilize the broken arm. 医护人员使用木制夹板固定了骨折的手臂。

Doctors splinted the finger to prevent any further movement. 医生用夹板固定了手指以防止进一步活动。

split.note:
They decided to split the restaurant bill evenly among themselves. 他们决定平摊餐厅的账单。

The heavy blow caused the wooden block to split in two. 重击导致木块一分为二。

splurge.note:
She decided to splurge on an expensive designer handbag. 她决定狠狠心买一款昂贵的设计师手提包。

After getting her bonus, she went on a shopping splurge. 拿到奖金后，她进行了一场疯狂的大采购。

spoil.meaning: v. 损坏；溺爱；变质；n. 战利品
spoil.note:
Milk will quickly spoil if left out of the refrigerator in summer. 夏天如果不放冰箱，牛奶很快就会变质。

Grandparents often love to spoil their grandchildren. 祖父母通常很喜欢溺爱孙辈。

spoke.meaning: n. 车轮辐条；speak的过去式
spoke.note:
One of the bicycle wheel spokes was broken in the crash. 撞车事故中，自行车车轮的一根辐条断了。

He spoke clearly to the audience during the presentation. 他在演示期间对观众发表了清晰的讲话。

spongy.note:
The cake had a light and spongy texture. 这块蛋糕有着轻盈且松软的口感。

The ground remained spongy after days of heavy continuous rain. 经过数天连续大雨后，地面依然是海绵般松软的。

spontaneity.meaning: n. 自发性；自然；无拘束
spontaneity.note:
She valued the spontaneity of unplanned weekend trips. 她很珍视未经计划的周末旅行所带来的随性与自发性。

His acting lacked natural spontaneity and felt rehearsed. 他的表演缺乏自然的自发感，显得排练过度。

spoof.note:
The comedy movie is a clever spoof of classic spy films. 这部喜剧电影是对经典间谍片的一部巧妙恶搞。

They made a funny spoof video that went viral online. 他们制作了一段在网上走红的搞笑恶搞视频。

sporadic.note:
The region experienced sporadic rainfall throughout the summer. 该地区整个夏天都经历了零星的降雨。

Communication was difficult due to sporadic internet connections. 由于网络连接断断续续，通讯变得很困难。

sprain.note:
He managed to sprain his ankle while playing basketball. 他在打篮球时一不小心扭伤了脚踝。

A bad sprain will require weeks of rest and physical therapy. 严重的扭伤需要数周的休息和物理治疗。

sprawling.meaning: adj. 蔓延的；庞大杂乱的
sprawling.note:
The city is a sprawling metropolis with millions of residents. 这座城市是一个拥有数百万居民的庞大蔓延都市。

The estate had a sprawling mansion surrounded by gardens. 这座庄园有一座被花园环绕的庞大豪宅。

sprig.note:
She decorated the dessert with a fresh sprig of mint. 她用一小枝新鲜薄荷装饰了甜点。

A small sprig of green leaves sprouted from the old stump. 老树桩上长出了一小枝绿叶。

sprightly.meaning: adj. 愉快的；活泼的；精神抖擞的
sprightly.note:
Despite her advanced age, she remained sprightly and active. 尽管年事已高，她依然精神抖擞、活力充沛。

He walked with a sprightly step down the morning street. 他迈着轻快活泼的步伐走在早晨的街上。

spruce.meaning: n. 云杉；v. 打扮整洁；使整洁
spruce.note:
Tall evergreen spruce trees covered the mountain slopes. 高大的常绿云杉树覆盖了山坡。

He took a few minutes to spruce up before the interview. 他花了几分钟在面试前把仪表收拾整洁。

spur.meaning: n. 马刺；刺激；激励；v. 鞭策；激励
spur.note:
The government offered tax cuts to spur economic growth. 政府提供减税政策以刺激经济增长。

On the spur of the moment, they decided to book a flight. 他们临时起意，决定订一张机票。

spurious.meaning: adj. 虚假的；伪造的；欺骗性的
spurious.note:
Police discovered that the painting was a spurious imitation. 警察发现这幅画是一件伪造的赝品。

His argument relied on spurious data and false claims. 他的论点依赖于虚假的数据和不实的声明。

squabble.note:
The children had a silly squabble over who got the toy. 孩子们为了谁得到玩具而发生了一场无聊的争吵。

Neighbors often squabble about parking spaces on the street. 邻居们经常为街上的停车位争吵不休。

squalid.meaning: adj. 肮脏的；污秽的；悲惨的
squalid.note:
Many refugees lived in squalid conditions in the camp. 许多难民在营地里过着肮脏污秽的生活。

The report highlighted the squalid state of local prisons. 报告强调了当地监狱破败肮脏的状况。

squall.note:
A sudden squall caught the sailors off guard in the bay. 一场突如其来的暴风让海湾里的水手们措手不及。

The infant began to squall loudly in the middle of the night. 婴儿在半夜里大声啼哭起来。

squalor.meaning: n. 肮脏；龌龊；悲惨环境
squalor.note:
The family escaped from extreme poverty and squalor. 这个家庭摆脱了极端贫困和肮脏的环境。

Stray animals often live in neglect and squalor. 流浪动物通常生活在遭受忽视和肮脏的环境中。

squeeze.note:
She used a lemon squeezer to squeeze fresh juice. 她用榨汁机榨新鲜柠檬汁。

He managed to squeeze into the crowded elevator. 他设法挤进了拥挤的电梯。

squelch.meaning: v. 镇压；掐熄；发没声响地踩；n. 啪唧声
squelch.note:
The government moved quickly to squelch the growing protest. 政府迅速采取行动镇压了不断扩大的抗议活动。

Her boots made a squelch sound in the deep mud. 她的靴子在深泥里踩出了啪唧的声响。

squint.note:
He had to squint to read the tiny print on the label. 他不得不眯起眼睛看标签上的小字。

Bright sunlight made her squint as she walked outside. 灿烂的阳光让走在户外的她眯起了眼睛。

staccato.meaning: adj./adv. 断音的；断断续续的
staccato.note:
The sound of gunfire had a sharp and staccato rhythm. 枪声带着尖锐而断断续续的节奏。

She played the piano passage in a distinct staccato style. 她以清晰的断音风格弹奏了这段钢琴曲。

stagnant.meaning: adj. 停滞的；不流动的；呆滞的
stagnant.note:
Mosquitoes often breed in stagnant water pools. 蚊子经常在不流动的积水潭里滋生。

The company suffered from stagnant sales during the quarter. 这家公司在该季度遭遇了销售额停滞不前的问题。

staid.meaning: adj. 沉着古板的；一本正经的
staid.note:
He worked for a staid financial firm in downtown London. 他在伦敦市中心一家古板稳健的金融公司工作。

The traditional newspaper has a rather staid editorial style. 这家传统报纸拥有相当一本正经的社论风格。

stale.meaning: adj. 陈旧的；不新鲜的；走味的
stale.note:
The bread had been left out too long and gone stale. 面包放的时间太长，已经变得不新鲜了。

The office routine felt stale and needed creative changes. 办公室的日常工作显得老套陈旧，需要进行创造性的改变。

stalemate.meaning: n. 僵局；僵持；v. 使陷入僵局
stalemate.note:
Peace talks reached a complete stalemate after three days. 经过三天后，和平谈判陷入了彻底的僵局。

Neither team could score, and the match ended in a stalemate. 双方均未进球，比赛以僵局告终。

stalk.meaning: n. 植物的茎；v. 悄悄跟踪；高视阔步
stalk.note:
The tiger began to stalk its prey through the thick brush. 老虎开始穿过茂密的灌木丛悄悄追踪猎物。

She cut a long green stalk of celery for the soup. 她为汤切了一根长长的绿色西芹茎。

stall.meaning: n. 货摊；畜栏；发动机熄火；v. 拖延；抛锚
stall.note:
He bought some fresh fruit at the market stall. 他在集市摊位上买了一些新鲜水果。

The car engine tended to stall in cold winter mornings. 汽车发动机在寒冷的冬日早晨容易熄火。

stalwart.meaning: adj. 坚定的；强壮的；n. 忠实支持者
stalwart.note:
She remained a stalwart supporter of environmental reforms. 她依然是环保改革的坚定支持者。

The castle was defended by a group of stalwart soldiers. 城堡由一群强壮坚定的士兵防守。

stammer.note:
He tended to stammer slightly when speaking in public. 他在公开演讲时往往会有点口吃。

She answered with a nervous stammer during the interview. 面试时她带着紧张结巴的语气回答了问题。

stanch.note:
The nurse applied pressure to stanch the bleeding from the cut. 护士施加压力以止住伤口流血。

Measures were taken to stanch the flow of corporate funds. 采取了措施以制止公司资金的外流。

stanza.note:
Each stanza of the poem contained four rhyming lines. 这首诗的每一节都包含四个押韵的行。

She recited the first stanza from memory with confidence. 她自信地背诵出了第一节诗。

starchy.meaning: adj. 含淀粉的；板滞的；过于拘谨的
starchy.note:
Potatoes and rice are examples of starchy foods. 土豆和米饭是富含淀粉食物的例子。

He disliked the starchy formality of the dinner party. 他不喜欢晚宴上那种过于拘谨的正式感。

stark.meaning: adj. 荒凉的；严酷的；完全的
stark.note:
The winter landscape looked stark and desolate under the grey sky. 灰色天空下，冬日的景致显得荒凉而凄清。

The report provided a stark contrast between rich and poor. 报告揭示了贫富之间鲜明的对比。

stasis.note:
The economy has been in economic stasis for several years. 经济已经陷入停滞状态好几年了。

The biological system remained in stable stasis. 生物系统保持着稳定的平衡状态。

static.meaning: adj. 静止的；呆板的；n. 静电；干扰噪声
static.note:
Prices have remained static throughout the entire year. 价格在整整一年里一直保持不变。

There was a lot of radio static during the storm. 暴风雨期间收音机里有很多静电噪音。

statuary.meaning: n. 雕像总称；雕塑艺术
statuary.note:
The museum courtyard was decorated with ancient Greek statuary. 博物馆庭院里装饰着古希腊雕像群。

He admired the intricate bronze statuary inside the temple. 他赞赏寺庙内部精致的青铜雕塑群。

stature.meaning: n. 身高；崇高的地位；声誉
stature.note:
Despite his short stature, he was a giant in business. 尽管身材矮小，他在商界却是个巨头。

The university grew in academic stature over the decades. 这所大学的学术声誉在几十年里不断提升。

statute.note:
The company operated in compliance with local environmental statutes. 该公司在遵守当地环保法规的前提下运营。

New statutes were enacted to protect consumer rights. 颁布了新的法令以保护消费者权益。

statutory.meaning: adj. 法定的；法律规定的
statutory.note:
Employees are entitled to statutory paid annual leave. 员工有权享受法定的带薪年假。

The company failed to meet its statutory reporting obligations. 该公司未能履行其法定的报告义务。

steadfast.meaning: adj. 坚定的；忠实的；不渝的
steadfast.note:
She remained steadfast in her commitment to the project. 她对该项目的承诺始终坚定不移。

He showed steadfast loyalty to his friends through hard times. 在艰难时期，他对朋友表现出了忠贞不渝的忠诚。

stealth.meaning: n. 秘密；隐秘；偷偷摸摸
stealth.note:
The cat moved with incredible stealth toward the mouse. 猫以不可思议的隐蔽动作朝老鼠靠近。

The military aircraft is designed with advanced stealth technology. 这架军用飞机采用先进的隐形技术设计。

stellar.meaning: adj. 星星的；杰出的；极佳的
stellar.note:
Astronomers study stellar evolution in distant galaxies. 天文学家研究遥远星系中的恒星演化。

She delivered a stellar performance that earned rave reviews. 她奉献了一场赢得极高评价的出色表演。

stem.meaning: n. 茎；干；v. 起源于；堵住；遏制
stem.note:
The flower had a long green stem with several leaves. 这朵花有一根带几片叶子的长绿茎。

Strict measures were introduced to stem the tide of inflation. 推行了严厉措施以遏制通货膨胀的势头。

stench.note:
A terrible stench came from the overflowing garbage bin. 垃圾桶溢出了一股可怕的恶臭。

Chemical factories often produce a strong stench in the area. 化工厂经常在该地区产生强烈的恶臭。

stencil.meaning: n. 模板；型板；v. 用模板印
stencil.note:
She used a paper stencil to paint patterns on the wall. 她用纸模板在墙上绘制图案。

His name was neatly stenciled on the wooden storage box. 他的名字被整齐地用模板喷印在木制收纳盒上。

stentorian.meaning: adj. 声音洪亮的；震耳欲聋的
stentorian.note:
The coach spoke in a stentorian voice across the sports field. 教练在运动场上用洪亮的声音说话。

He shouted with stentorian tones to get everyone's attention. 他用洪亮的嗓音大喊以引起每个人的注意。

stereotype.meaning: n. 刻板印象；老套；v. 对…抱有刻板印象
stereotype.note:
We should avoid creating a false stereotype about any group. 我们应该避免对任何群体产生虚假的刻板印象。

Media often tends to stereotype people based on appearance. 媒体往往倾向于根据外表对人刻板化。

sterilize.note:
Doctors must carefully sterilize all instruments before surgery. 外国医生必须在手术前仔细给所有器械消毒。

Pet owners often choose to sterilize their cats or dogs. 宠物主人通常选择给猫狗做绝育手术。

stethoscope.note:
The doctor placed a stethoscope against the patient's chest. 医生把听诊器放在病人的胸口上。

She listened carefully to the heartbeat through the stethoscope. 她通过听诊器仔细聆听心跳声。

stickler.meaning: n. 坚持细节的人；一丝不苟的人
stickler.note:
Our professor is a strict stickler for grammatical accuracy. 我们的教授是个对语法准确性有着严格要求的人。

He is a stickler for punctuality and hates people being late. 他是个非常注重守时的人，讨厌别人迟到。

stifle.note:
She tried hard to stifle a yawn during the long speech. 在长篇演讲中，她努力压抑着打哈欠的冲动。

Heavy bureaucracy can stifle innovation within a company. 繁文缛节会扼杀公司内部的创新。

stigma.note:
There is still a social stigma attached to mental illness. 精神疾病仍然附带着某种社会污名。

Efforts are being made to remove the stigma of seeking help. 人们正在努力消除寻求帮助所带来的耻辱感。

stigmatize.note:
We should not stigmatize people who make mistakes. 我们不应该给犯错误的人贴上耻辱的标签。

Society tends to unfairly stigmatize former prisoners. 社会往往对刑满释放人员存在不公正的污名化。

stilted.meaning: adj. （文风或谈吐）生硬的；不自然的
stilted.note:
Their conversation was awkward and stilted at first. 他们一开始的对话显得尴尬而生硬。

The book was written in a rather stilted literary style. 这本书是用一种相当生硬做作的文学风格写的。

stimulant.meaning: n. 兴奋剂；刺激物；adj. 刺激性的
stimulant.note:
Coffee and tea contain caffeine, which acts as a mild stimulant. 咖啡和茶含有咖啡因，它是一种温和的兴奋剂。

Caffeine is a popular mental stimulant used in the morning. 咖啡因是早晨常用的一种提神刺激物。

stimulus.note:
Financial incentives act as a powerful economic stimulus. 财务激励措施起到了强有力的经济刺激作用。

Plants grow in response to external environmental stimulus. 植物在外部环境刺激下生长。

stinginess.note:
His financial stinginess made him unpopular with colleagues. 他在金钱上的吝啬让他在同事中不受欢迎。

She complained about the company's stinginess with bonuses. 她抱怨公司在奖金发放上的吝啬。

stint.meaning: v. 节省；吝惜；n. 定量工作；期限
stint.note:
He served a two-year stint in the military before college. 他在上大学前服过两年兵役。

Do not stint on quality when buying essential safety gear. 购买必要的安全装备时不要吝惜质量。

stipple.meaning: v. 点画；用小点涂抹；n. 点画法
stipple.note:
The artist used a brush to stipple color onto the canvas. 艺术家用画笔在画布上进行点画上色。

The wall surface was finished with a textured stipple paint. 墙面采用了一种有质感的点画涂料进行粉刷。

stipulate.note:
The contract will stipulate delivery dates and payment terms. 合同将规定交货日期和付款条款。

Regulations stipulate that all workers must wear helmets. 法规规定所有工人都必须佩戴安全帽。

stipulation.note:
One key stipulation of the agreement was a strict confidentiality clause. 该协议的一个关键条款是严格的保密条款。

He accepted the job offer without any additional stipulations. 他接受了这份工作offer，没有任何附加条件。

stir.note:
Remember to stir the soup occasionally so it does not burn. 记得偶尔搅拌一下汤以免烧焦。

The scandalous news caused quite a stir in the small town. 这条丑闻在小镇上引起了不小的轰动。

stock.meaning: n. 库存；股票；家畜；v. 存货
stock.note:
The supermarket shelves are fully stocked with fresh groceries. 超市货架上摆满了新鲜杂货。

She invested a large portion of her savings in company stock. 她将大部分积蓄投资了公司股票。

stockade.meaning: n. 原木栅栏；军事监狱
stockade.note:
Early settlers built a wooden stockade to protect the village. 早期的定居者建造了一个木制栅栏来保护村庄。

The rowdy soldier was locked up in the military stockade. 那个粗鲁的士兵被关进了军事监狱。

stocky.note:
He was a short and stocky man with immense physical strength. 他是一个身材矮短粗壮、力大无穷的男子。

The rugby player had a stocky build suited for the sport. 这名橄榄球运动员拥有适合该运动的粗壮体格。

stodgy.meaning: adj. 沉重难消化的；古板沉闷的
stodgy.note:
He felt sleepy after eating a heavy and stodgy lunch. 吃了一顿厚重且难消化的午饭后，他感到昏昏欲睡。

The committee meeting followed a stodgy and formal routine. 委员会会议遵循着古板沉闷的常规程序。

stoic.meaning: adj. 坚忍的；克己的；n. 斯多葛学派的人
stoic.note:
She maintained a stoic silence despite experiencing severe pain. 尽管经受剧烈疼痛，她依然保持着坚忍的沉默。

He faced his misfortunes with a calm and stoic attitude. 他以冷静坚忍的态度面对自己的不幸。

stoke.meaning: v. 添柴加火；激起；煽动
stoke.note:
He opened the furnace door to stoke the coal fire. 他打开炉门给煤火添煤加火。

Media coverage helped to stoke public anger over the issue. 媒体的报道助长了公众对该问题的愤怒情绪。

stolid.meaning: adj. 冷漠的；感情迟钝的；坚定的
stolid.note:
He remained stolid and expressionless throughout the trial. 整个审判过程中，他一直表情冷漠、麻木不仁。

Her stolid demeanor hid a deeply anxious personality. 她那木讷冷漠的外表下隐藏着一个极其焦虑的性格。

stonewall.note:
Politicians tried to stonewall the investigation by withholding files. 政治家试图通过扣留文件来阻挠调查。

The official chose to stonewall questions from reporters. 这位官员选择对记者的提问采取敷衍拖延的态度。

stout.meaning: adj. 强壮的；粗胖的；坚定的；n. 烈性黑啤酒
stout.note:
He offered stout resistance to the unfair company policies. 他对不公的公司政策进行了坚决的抵抗。

She ordered a glass of dark stout at the traditional pub. 她在传统酒吧里点了一杯深色烈性黑啤酒。

stowaway.note:
The ship crew discovered a hidden stowaway on board the cargo ship. 船员们在货船上发现了一个藏匿的偷渡者。

Security caught the stowaway trying to sneak onto the plane. 安检人员抓住了试图偷偷溜上飞机的偷渡客。

strait.meaning: n. 海峡；困境（通常用複数）
strait.note:
Cargo ships sailed carefully through the narrow strait. 货轮小心翼翼地穿过狭窄的海峡。

Poor investments left the family in severe financial straits. 不良投资让这个家庭陷入了严重的经济困境。

strand.meaning: n. 缕；股；海滨；v. 使滞留；使搁浅
strand.note:
A single strand of hair fell across her forehead. 一缕头发垂落在她的额头上。

Flight cancellations left hundreds of passengers stranded at the airport. 航班取消导致数百名乘客滞留在机场。

stranded.note:
Rescue teams searched for hikers stranded in the snowstorm. 救援队搜寻在暴风雪中滞留的远足者。

The whale was found stranded on the sandy beach. 那头鲸鱼被发现在沙滩上搁浅。

stratagem.note:
The military commander used a clever stratagem to confuse the enemy. 这位军事指挥官用了一个巧妙的计谋来迷惑敌人。

Business negotiations required various tactical stratagems. 商业谈判需要各种策略性的谋略。

stratum.note:
Geologists studied the fossil records in each rock stratum. 地质学家研究了每一层岩石中的化石记录。

The policy change affects every stratum of society. 政策变动影响到社会的各个阶层。

stray.meaning: v. 迷路；走失；adj. 迷路的；孤立的
stray.note:
A stray dog wandered into our backyard looking for food. 一只流浪狗游荡进我们的后院寻找食物。

Be careful not to stray from the designated hiking path. 小心不要偏离指定的远足小路。

stream.meaning: n. 小溪；流；v. 流出；流动
stream.note:
A clear blue stream flowed gently through the green valley. 一条清澈的蓝色小溪静静流淌在绿色山谷中。

Tears began to stream down her face when she heard the news. 听到这个消息时，泪水开始从她脸上流淌下来。

strew.note:
Autumn leaves were strewn across the path in the park. 秋叶散落在公园的小路上。

Books and papers were strewn haphazardly across his desk. 书籍和文件杂乱无章地散落在他桌子上。

striate.meaning: adj. 有条纹的；有细纹的
striate.note:
The mineral specimen had a distinct striate surface pattern. 该矿物标本表面有明显的条纹状图案。

Biologists observed striate muscle tissue under the microscope. 生物学家在显微镜下观察了横纹肌组织。

striated.meaning: adj. 有条纹的；带细纹的
striated.note:
Skeletal muscles are often described as striated muscle tissue. 骨骼肌通常被描述为横纹肌组织。

The rock featured beautifully striated layers of minerals. 这块岩石具有优美条纹状的矿物层。

stricture.meaning: n. 严厉批评；束缚；限制
stricture.note:
The budget imposed strict financial strictures on all departments. 预算对所有部门施加了严格的财务限制。

He faced harsh strictures from critics regarding his latest book. 他因最新一本书受到了批评家们的严厉指摘。

stride.note:
He walked with a confident stride across the room. 他迈着自信的大步走过房间。

The country has made great strides in technology recently. 该国近年来在技术方面取得了巨大进展。

strident.meaning: adj. 刺耳的；强硬的；尖锐的
strident.note:
Her strident voice could be heard above the crowd noise. 她的尖锐声音在人群喧闹声中清晰可闻。

The editorial adopted a strident tone against the new policy. 该社论采取了针对新政策的强硬刺耳语气。

strife.note:
Civil strife tore the country apart for over a decade. 内乱将这个国家撕裂了十多年。

Internal corporate strife threatened to ruin the business. 公司内部的冲突威胁到了这门生意的存亡。

strive.note:
We must always strive for excellence in everything we do. 我们在所做的每一件事情上都必须力求卓越。

She continued to strive against heavy odds to reach her goal. 她顶住重重困难，继续为达成目标而奋斗。

strut.meaning: v./n. 昂首阔步；炫耀；支撑杆
strut.note:
The model began to strut down the fashion runway. 模特开始在时尚T台上昂首阔步走秀。

A metal strut was added to reinforce the airplane wing. 增加了一个金属支撑杆来加固飞机机翼。

studied.meaning: adj. 刻意的；故意的；有准备的
studied.note:
He maintained a studied calm throughout the awkward interview. 在整个尴尬的采访中，他保持着一种刻意的冷静。

Her casual response was actually the result of studied preparation. 她随意的回答实际上是刻意准备的结果。

stuffy.meaning: adj. 不通风的；闷热的；保守古板的
stuffy.note:
The small office felt stuffy because the windows were closed. 因为窗户关着，这间小办公室让人感觉闷热不通风。

He thought the traditional club atmosphere was too stuffy. 他认为传统俱乐部的气氛过于古板保守。

stultify.meaning: v. 使显得愚笨；使失效；阻碍
stultify.note:
Excessive rules can stultify creativity in young minds. 过多的规矩会扼杀年轻人心中的创造力。

Monotonous work tends to stultify human intellect over time. 枯燥单调的工作往往会随着时间推移使人的智力变得呆滞。

stunning.meaning: adj. 极好的；惊艳的；极具吸引力的
stunning.note:
She wore a stunning red dress to the evening gala. 她穿着一件惊艳的红裙出席晚会。

The mountain view from the top was simply stunning. 山顶上的景色简直美得惊人。

stunt.meaning: v. 阻碍发育；n. 特技动作；噱头
stunt.note:
Malnutrition can stunt the growth of young children. 营养不良会阻碍幼儿的发育生长。

The movie featured dangerous motorcycle stunt scenes. 这部电影包含了危险的摩托车特技场景。

stupor.meaning: n. 昏迷；知觉麻木；恍惚
stupor.note:
He woke up from a drunken stupor late the next morning. 他第二天清晨从酒醉昏迷中醒来。

The extreme heat left everyone in a dazed stupor. 极端的酷热让每个人都处于茫然恍惚的状态。

stutter.meaning: v./n. 口吃；结巴；断断续续发声
stutter.note:
He began to stutter when asked to speak in front of the class. 当被要求在全班面前讲话时，他开始结巴起来。

The old engine gave a slight stutter before starting. 老发动机在启动前发出了轻微的断续声。

stygian.meaning: adj. 阴暗的；漆黑的（源自冥河）
stygian.note:
They entered the deep cave shrouded in stygian darkness. 他们进入了笼罩在漆黑阴暗中的深洞。

The abandoned mine had a stygian atmosphere that frightened them. 那座废弃的矿井有一种令他们害怕的黑暗阴森氛围。

stymie.meaning: v. 阻碍；妨碍；使陷入困境
stymie.note:
Technical problems continued to stymie the research project. 技术问题继续阻碍着这项研究项目。

Bad weather stymied their plans to climb the mountain. 恶劣天气阻碍了他们登山的计划。

subdue.note:
Police managed to subdue the aggressive suspect safely. 警察设法安全地制服了那个有攻击性的嫌疑人。

She tried to subdue her sudden surge of panic. 她试图克制住自己突然涌现的恐慌情绪。

subdued.meaning: adj. 温和的；减弱的；情绪低落的
subdued.note:
The team returned home in a subdued mood after the loss. 输掉比赛后，球队以低落的心情回到了家。

The restaurant had soft lighting and subdued music playing. 餐厅有着柔和的灯光和播放着舒缓低沉的音乐。

subjective.note:
Art appreciation is largely a matter of subjective judgment. 艺术欣赏在很大程度上属于主观判断的问题。

He gave a subjective review based entirely on personal feelings. 他做出了一个完全基于个人感受的主观评价。

subjugate.note:
Invading armies tried to subjugate the local population. 入侵军队试图征服当地居民并使其屈服。

He learned to subjugate his personal desires for the common good. 他学会了为了共同利益而克制自己的个人欲望。

sublime.meaning: adj. 崇高的；壮丽的；极佳的
sublime.note:
The sunset over the mountain range was a sublime sight. 山脉上空的日落是一处壮丽崇高的景象。

She cooked a meal with sublime flavors that delighted everyone. 她做了一顿美味绝伦、让每个人都喜悦的饭菜。

subliminal.meaning: adj. 潜意识的；阈下觉察的
subliminal.note:
Advertisements often rely on subliminal messaging to influence buyers. 广告经常依靠潜意识信息来影响买家。

The sound had a subliminal effect on his mood. 这种声音对他的情绪产生了潜移默化的影响。

suborn.meaning: v. 收买；唆使（做坏事或作伪证）
suborn.note:
He tried to suborn a witness to lie during the trial. 他试图在审判期间收买证人说谎。

Criminal networks often attempt to suborn public officials. 犯罪网络经常企图收买公职人员。

subpoena.meaning: n. 传票；v. 传唤；传讯
subpoena.note:
The court issued a subpoena requiring him to testify. 法院下达了一张传票，要求他出庭作证。

Prosecutors decided to subpoena the key bank records. 检察官决定传唤关键的银行记录文件。

subsidiary.meaning: adj. 附属的；辅助的；n. 子公司
subsidiary.note:
The large retail group operates several foreign subsidiaries. 这家大型零售集团经营着数家海外子公司。

This is a subsidiary matter that we can discuss later. 这是一个我们可以稍后讨论的次要辅助问题。

subsistence.note:
Many rural families rely solely on subsistence farming. 许多农村家庭仅靠自给自足的农业维持生计。

Their income was barely enough to ensure basic subsistence. 他们的收入勉强足够维持基本的生存需要。

substance.note:
Water is a chemical substance essential for all known life. 水是所有已知生命所必需的化学物质。

His speech lacked real substance and offered no clear solutions. 他的演讲缺乏真正的实质内容，没有提供清晰的解决方案。

substantiate.note:
There is no physical evidence to substantiate his claim. 没有实际证据来证实他的说法。

She presented data to substantiate her theory about climate change. 她出示了数据来佐证她关于气候变化的理论。

substantive.meaning: adj. 实质性的；重大的；真实的
substantive.note:
The two countries made substantive progress in trade talks. 两国在贸易谈判中取得了实质性进展。

We need substantive evidence before taking legal action. 在采取法律行动之前，我们需要实质性的证据。

subsume.note:
Various independent local groups were subsumed into a single national organization. 各种独立的地方组织被纳入了一个单一的国家组织中。

This broader category can easily subsume these smaller items. 这个更广泛的类别可以轻易地将这些小项目包含在内。

subterfuge.note:
He obtained the confidential documents through deceit and subterfuge. 他通过欺骗和诡计获取了机密文件。

She refused to use political subterfuge to win the election. 她拒绝使用政治花招来赢得选举。

subterranean.note:
Miners worked long hours in deep subterranean tunnels. 矿工们在深深的地下隧道里工作了很长时间。

Rainwater carved out a complex subterranean river system. 雨水侵蚀出复杂的地下河流系统。

subvert.meaning: v. 颠覆；暗中破坏；瓦解
subvert.note:
The conspirators plotted to subvert the democratic government. 阴谋分子策划颠覆民主政府。

Critics argued that the film tries to subvert traditional values. 批评人士认为这部电影试图颠覆传统价值观。

succor.note:
Volunteers rushed to bring food and succor to earthquake victims. 志愿者们赶忙给地震灾民送去食物和救援。

She offered succor to refugees fleeing from political violence. 她为逃离政治暴力的难民提供了救济帮助。

suffice.note:
A simple apology will suffice to mend the broken friendship. 一个简单的道歉就足以修补破裂的友谊。

Two hours of study a day should suffice for the exam. 每天学习两个小时应对考试就足够了。

sufficient.note:
Make sure you have sufficient funds before booking the holiday. 确保你在预定度假前有充足的资金。

There is sufficient evidence to prove his innocence. 有充足的证据证明他是无辜的。

suffrage.note:
Women's suffrage became a major political movement in the 20th century. 女性选举权在20世纪成为一项重大的政治运动。

Universal suffrage is a core principle of modern democracy. 普选权是现代民主的核心原则。

suffragist.meaning: n. 争取妇女参政权者
suffragist.note:
Early suffragist leaders fought bravely for voting rights. 早期的妇女参政权运动领导人为了投票权进行了勇敢的斗争。

A museum exhibition honors the history of local suffragists. 博物馆展览纪念了当地女性争取参政权者的历史。

suffuse.note:
A warm glow of happiness began to suffuse her face. 一股幸福的暖意开始浮现在她的脸上。

The morning sky was suffused with soft shades of pink and orange. 清晨的天空弥漫着柔和的粉色和橙色调。

suggestive.meaning: adj. 暗示的；引起联想的；猥亵的
suggestive.note:
Her smile was suggestive of hidden secrets. 她的微笑暗示着隐藏的秘密。

The research results are highly suggestive of a deeper trend. 研究结果非常暗示着一种更深层次的趋势。

suitcase.note:
He packed his heavy winter clothes into a large suitcase. 他把厚重的冬衣打包进了一个大行李箱。

She forgot her travel documents inside the locked suitcase. 她把旅行证件忘在锁着的行李箱里了。

sulky.meaning: adj. 生气的；面露愠色的；阴沉的
sulky.note:
The child sat in the corner with a sulky expression on his face. 孩子坐在角落里，脸上带着一副生气的神情。

He gave a sulky response when asked to help with chores. 当被要求帮忙做家务时，他给出了一个没好气的回应。

sullen.meaning: adj. 阴郁的；闷闷不乐的；沉闷的
sullen.note:
He remained in a sullen mood all through the morning. 他整个早晨都保持着闷闷不乐的心情。

A sullen grey sky threatened heavy rain over the hills. 阴沉的灰色天空预示着山丘上方将有大雨降临。

sultry.meaning: adj. 闷热的；酷热的；撩人的
sultry.note:
The afternoon weather grew heavy and sultry before the storm. 暴风雨来临前，下午的天气变得又闷又热。

Jazz music played softly in the sultry summer evening. 爵士乐在闷热的夏夜里轻柔地播放着。

summarily.meaning: adv. 即刻地；草率地；概要地
summarily.note:
The rebellious employee was summarily dismissed by management. 那名叛逆的员工被管理层当即开除了。

His request for a transfer was summarily rejected. 他要求调职的请求被草率地拒绝了。

summation.meaning: n. 总结；总括；最后陈述
summation.note:
The lawyer delivered a powerful summation at the trial. 律师在审判结束时发表了强有力的总结陈词。

This book serves as a brilliant summation of his life's work. 这本书是他毕生工作的一部精彩总结。

summon.meaning: v. 召唤；传唤；鼓起（勇气）
summon.note:
The manager decided to summon an emergency staff meeting. 经理决定召开一次紧急员工会议。

She tried to summon the courage to speak in public. 她努力鼓起勇气在公众面前发言。

sumptuous.meaning: adj. 奢侈的；华丽的；丰盛的
sumptuous.note:
The wedding guests enjoyed a sumptuous banquet at the hotel. 婚礼宾客在酒店享用了丰盛奢华的宴席。

The hotel room featured sumptuous decor and velvet furnishings. 酒店客房采用华丽的装潢和天鹅绒家具。

superb.meaning: adj. 极好的；卓越的；华丽的
superb.note:
The chef prepared a superb meal for the anniversary celebration. 主厨为周年庆典准备了一顿极佳的饭菜。

She showed superb leadership skills during the crisis. 她在危机期间表现出了卓越的领导能力。

supercilious.meaning: adj. 目空一切的；傲慢的
supercilious.note:
He treated the waitstaff with a supercilious attitude. 他对服务生采取了一种傲慢目中无人的态度。

Her supercilious remarks made everyone at the table uncomfortable. 她傲慢的话语让桌上的每个人都感到不舒服。

superficiality.note:
He grew tired of the superficiality of high-society parties. 他厌倦了上流社会派对的肤浅虚浮。

The critic pointed out the superficiality of the film's plot. 批评家指出了电影情节的肤浅性。

superfluity.note:
We need to trim the superfluity from our daily budget. 我们需要削减日常预算中多余的开支。

His speech suffered from a superfluity of unnecessary details. 他的演讲充斥着过多不必要的细节。

superimpose.note:
She decided to superimpose text over the background image. 她决定在背景图像上叠加文字。

The artist superimpsed two different photographs to create art. 艺术家将两张不同的照片叠加在一起创造艺术品。

superintend.note:
He was hired to superintend the construction of the new bridge. 他被聘请来监督新桥的建设施工。

Managers superintended the daily operations of the warehouse. 经理们监督仓库的日常运营。

superiority.note:
The team demonstrated a clear technical superiority in the match. 这支球队在比赛中表现出了明显的技战术优势。

He had an annoying air of intellectual superiority. 他有一种令人讨厌的知识优越感。

supernova.note:
Astronomers observed a brilliant supernova in a distant galaxy. 天文学家在一个遥远的星系中观测到了一颗耀眼的超新星。

When massive stars die, they often explode as a magnificent supernova. 当大质量恒星死亡时，它们经常作为壮丽的超新星爆炸。

supine.meaning: adj. 仰卧的；怠惰的，麻木不仁的
supine.note:
He lay supine on the grass, looking up at the clouds. 他仰卧在草地上，抬头看着云彩。

The government was supine in the face of such lawlessness. 面对这种无法无天的行为，政府表现得麻木不仁。

supplant.note:
Printed books may eventually be supplanted by e-books. 印刷书籍最终可能会被电子书取代。

New technology has rapidly supplanted older methods. 新技术已经迅速取代了旧方法。

supple.meaning: adj. 柔软的，柔韧的；灵活的
supple.note:
Yoga helps to keep your body supple. 瑜伽有助于保持身体柔韧。

She has a supple mind that easily adapts to changes. 她有着灵活的头脑，能轻易适应变化。

suppliant.meaning: adj. 恳求的，哀求的 / n. 恳求者，哀求者
suppliant.note:
He made a suppliant gesture to the king. 他向国王做出恳求的手势。

The suppliant begged for mercy on her knees. 恳求者跪下祈求宽恕。

supplicant.note:
The supplicant asked the gods for rain. 恳求者向神明祈求降雨。

Standing at the temple doors, the supplicant waited patiently. 恳求者站在庙门口耐心等待。

supplicate.note:
They gathered to supplicate for divine protection. 他们聚集在一起祈求神灵的庇护。

She did not want to supplicate anyone for help. 她不想向任何人低头哀求帮助。

supremacy.meaning: n. 至高无上，优势，霸权
supremacy.note:
The team fought to maintain its supremacy in the league. 这支队伍为保持在联盟中的霸权而战。

Economic supremacy often brings political influence. 经济优势往往会带来政治影响力。

supreme.meaning: adj. 至高无上的，极度的，最重要的
supreme.note:
Confidence is of supreme importance in sports. 自信在体育运动中至关重要。

The supreme court made a historic decision. 最高法院做出了一项历史性裁决。

surfeit.meaning: n. 过量，饮食过度 / v. 使饮食过量，使厌腻
surfeit.note:
A surfeit of rich food made him feel sick. 过量油腻的食物使他感到恶心。

We should not surfeit ourselves with luxury. 我们不应沉溺于穷奢极欲。

surge.meaning: n. 汹涌，剧增 / v. 急剧上升，蜂拥
surge.note:
There was a sudden surge in housing prices. 房价突然出现了暴涨。

Waves surged against the rocky shore. 海浪汹涌地拍打着岩石海岸。

surgeon.note:
The surgeon performed a complex heart operation. 外科医生实施了一台复杂的心脏手术。

She trained for years to become a neurosurgeon. 她经过多年训练成为了一名神经外科医生。

surly.meaning: adj. 脾气坏的，粗暴的，阴郁的
surly.note:
The waiter gave a surly response and walked away. 服务员粗暴地回了一句便走开了。

Behind his surly exterior, he was actually quite kind. 在他阴郁的外表下，其实心地挺善良。

surmise.meaning: v. 推测，猜测 / n. 推测，猜度
surmise.note:
We can only surmise what happened based on the clues. 我们只能根据线索推测发生了什么。

His surmise turned out to be completely correct. 他的推测结果完全正确。

surmount.meaning: v. 克服，战胜；居于…之上
surmount.note:
She managed to surmount all the obstacles in her career. 她设法克服了职业生涯中的所有障碍。

A statue surmounts the top of the column. 纪念柱顶部耸立着一尊雕像。

surplus.meaning: n. 剩余，盈余 / adj. 过剩的，剩余的
surplus.note:
The country has a major trade surplus this year. 该国今年拥有巨大的贸易顺差。

We sold our surplus equipment to a local business. 我们将多余的设备卖给了一家当地企业。

surrender.meaning: v. 投降，放弃 / n. 投降，交出
surrender.note:
The enemy forces were forced to surrender. 敌军被迫投降。

He had to surrender his passport to the authorities. 他不得不向有关当局交出护照。

surreptitious.meaning: adj. 秘密的，偷偷摸摸的
surreptitious.note:
She cast a surreptitious glance at her watch. 她偷偷地看了一眼手表。

He made a surreptitious exit from the room. 他悄悄地离开了房间。

surveyor.meaning: n. 测量员，勘测员，房屋鉴定人
surveyor.note:
The building surveyor inspected the foundation of the house. 房屋鉴定员检查了房子的地基。

Surveyors mapped out the new route for the highway. 测量员为高速公路绘制了新路线图。

survive.note:
Few animals can survive in extreme desert conditions. 极少数动物能在极端的沙漠环境中生存。

She managed to survive the financial crisis. 她设法在金融危机中挺了过去。

susceptibility.meaning: n. 易感性，敏感性，感情脆弱处
susceptibility.note:
Elderly people have a higher susceptibility to infections. 老年人对感染的易感性更高。

Be careful not to hurt his artistic susceptibilities. 注意别伤害了他艺术上的敏感神经。

suspect.meaning: v. 怀疑，猜想 / n. 嫌疑人 / adj. 可疑的
suspect.note:
Police suspect that he was involved in the robbery. 警方怀疑他参与了这起抢劫案。

The quality of this product is highly suspect. 这个产品的质量非常可疑。

suspend.note:
The company decided to suspend production for a week. 公司决定暂停生产一周。

A lamp was suspended from the high ceiling. 一盏灯悬挂在高高的天花板上。

suspense.note:
The thriller film kept the audience in suspense until the end. 这部惊悚片让观众一直悬着心直到最后。

Don't keep me in suspense; tell me what happened! 别吊我的胃口了，快告诉我发生了什么！

suspicion.note:
His strange behavior aroused the suspicion of the police. 他奇怪的举动引起了警察的怀疑。

There is a suspicion that the rules might change. 有人怀疑规则可能会改变。

suspicious.note:
She was suspicious of his motives from the very beginning. 从一开始她就对他的动机产生怀疑。

Neighbors reported a suspicious vehicle parked on the street. 邻居报告说街上停了一辆可疑车辆。

sustained.note:
The project requires a sustained effort from everyone. 这个项目需要每个人持续不断的努力。

After sustained applause, the actor came back on stage. 在持续的掌声中，演员回到了舞台上。

sustenance.note:
Plants need water and sunlight for sustenance. 植物需要水和阳光来维持生存。

She found spiritual sustenance in her faith. 她在信仰中找到了精神寄托。

suture.meaning: n. 缝合，缝合线 / v. 缝合
suture.note:
The doctor used a suture to close the deep wound. 医生用缝合线缝合了深可见骨的伤口。

They had to suture the cut immediately. 他们必须立刻将切口缝合起来。

svelte.meaning: adj. 苗条的，体态优雅的
svelte.note:
She maintained a svelte figure through strict diet and exercise. 她通过严格的饮食和锻炼保持着苗条的身材。

The model walked down the runway in a svelte dress. 模特穿着一件修身的连衣裙走下T台。

swagger.meaning: v. 大摇大摆，自大 / n. 威风，大摇大摆的步态
swagger.note:
He walked into the room with a confident swagger. 他带着自信且大摇大摆的步态走进了房间。

He tends to swagger when he achieves success. 他取得成功时往往喜欢大摇大摆、不可一世。

swallow.meaning: v. 吞咽，轻信 / n. 燕子
swallow.note:
He had a sore throat and found it hard to swallow. 他喉咙痛，觉得很难咽下东西。

A single swallow does not make a summer. 一只燕子成不了夏天。

swell.meaning: v. 肿胀，膨胀 / n. 隆起，波浪起伏
swell.note:
His ankle began to swell after the twist. 扭伤后他的脚踝开始肿胀。

Rivers swelled with the heavy spring rains. 春季的大雨使河水上涨膨胀。

sweltering.note:
We stayed indoors during the sweltering afternoon heat. 我们在酷热的午后高温中待在室内。

The workers toiled under the sweltering sun. 工人们在闷热的太阳下辛苦劳作。

swill.meaning: v. 痛饮，涮洗 / n. 泔水，猪食
swill.note:
They sat at the pub to swill beer all night. 他们坐在酒吧里整晚痛饮啤酒。

Farmers used household scraps as swill for pigs. 农民把家里的剩菜剩饭当做猪食。

swindle.meaning: v. 诈骗，骗取 / n. 诈骗，骗局
swindle.note:
He was convicted of trying to swindle elderly people out of money. 他因企图诈骗老人的钱财而被定罪。

The investment scheme turned out to be a massive swindle. 那个投资计划原来是一场巨大的骗局。

swine.note:
Wild swine roam freely in the deep forest. 野猪在密林中自由漫步。

He called his business partner a selfish swine. 他骂他的商业伙伴是个自私的混蛋。

swirl.meaning: v. 打旋，盘旋 / n. 漩涡，旋涡状
swirl.note:
Smoke began to swirl up from the chimney. 烟雾开始从烟囱里盘旋上升。

She watched the coffee swirl around in her cup. 她看着咖啡在杯子里打转。

sybarite.meaning: n. 贪图享乐者，奢侈度日者
sybarite.note:
Living like a true sybarite, he spent his fortune on luxury villas. 他过着真正享乐主义者的生活，把财富花在豪华别墅上。

The resort is designed for wealthy sybarites. 这个度假村是为富有的享乐者设计的。

sybaritic.meaning: adj. 荒淫享乐的，奢侈的
sybaritic.note:
They enjoyed a sybaritic lifestyle on the private island. 他们在私人岛屿上享受着奢侈享乐的生活方式。

The banquet was filled with sybaritic excess. 宴会上充满了骄奢淫逸的过度享乐。

sycophant.note:
The CEO was surrounded by sycophants who praised his every idea. 首席执行官身边围满了对他的每一个想法大加赞赏的马屁精。

He despised sycophants and preferred honest critics. 他鄙视马屁精，更喜欢诚实的批评者。

syllabus.meaning: n. 教学大纲，课程大纲
syllabus.note:
The professor handed out the syllabus on the first day of class. 教授在开学第一天分发了教学大纲。

This novel is included in the high school literature syllabus. 这部小说被列入了高中文学教学大纲中。

symbiosis.note:
Certain fungi and trees live in close symbiosis. 某些真菌和树木存在着紧密的共生关系。

The two companies have a profitable economic symbiosis. 这两家公司有着互利共赢的经济共生关系。

symphony.note:
Beethoven composed his famous Ninth Symphony in later life. 贝多芬在晚年创作了他的名作《第九交响曲》。

The orchestra will perform a classical symphony tonight. 乐队今晚将演奏一部古典交响乐。

synchronous.meaning: adj. 同步的，同时发生的
synchronous.note:
The online class requires synchronous participation from students. 这门在线课程要求学生同步参与。

Synchronous translation is essential for international summits. 同步翻译对国际峰会至关重要。

synergic.meaning: adj. 协同的，产生协同作用的
synergic.note:
The departments worked in a synergic effort to cut costs. 各部门协同努力以削减成本。

Their combined skills created a powerful synergic effect. 他们结合的技能产生了强大的协同效应。

synopsis.note:
Please provide a brief synopsis of your research paper. 请提供一份你研究论文的简短摘要。

The book jacket contains a helpful plot synopsis. 书的护封上包含了一个很有帮助的情节概要。

synoptic.note:
The meteorologist studied synoptic charts to forecast the weather. 气象学家研究了天气图来预测天气。

We looked at a synoptic overview of the entire project. 我们看了一下整个项目的概要概览。

syringe.meaning: n. 注射器，针筒 / v. 用注射器冲洗
syringe.note:
The nurse filled the syringe with the vaccine. 护士把疫苗装进注射器里。

The doctor used a sterile syringe to clean the cut. 医生用无菌注射器清洗了伤口。

table.meaning: n. 桌子，表格 / v. 搁置，提交讨论
table.note:
They sat around the dining table for dinner. 他们围坐在餐桌旁吃晚饭。

The government decided to table the controversial bill for now. 政府决定暂时搁置这项有争议的法案。

taboo.meaning: n. 禁忌，避讳 / adj. 忌讳的，禁忌的
taboo.note:
Discussing salary openly is still a taboo in many offices. 公开讨论薪水在许多办公室里仍然是个禁忌。

Certain cultural topics remain taboo in polite conversation. 某些文化话题在礼貌的交谈中依然是禁忌。

tacit.meaning: adj. 默许的，心照不宣的
tacit.note:
Their agreement was based on a tacit understanding. 他们的协议基于一种心照不宣的默契。

She took his silence as tacit approval. 她把他的沉默当作是默认。

tackiness.note:
The paint still had a slight tackiness to it. 油漆摸上去仍然有点黏手。

Critics complained about the tackiness of the decoration. 批评者抱怨装饰过于俗气。

tact.note:
It required a lot of tact to handle the delicate situation. 处理这个微妙的局面需要极大的机智。

She showed great tact in dealing with the angry customer. 她在处理愤怒的顾客时表现得非常老练。

tadpole.note:
The children caught tadpoles in the pond. 孩子们在池塘里抓蝌蚪。

We watched the tadpole slowly develop its legs. 我们看着蝌蚪慢慢长出腿来。

tag.meaning: n. 标签，附属物 / v.加标签于，跟随
tag.note:
Check the price tag before buying the jacket. 买夹克前先看看价格标签。

He decided to tag along with us on the trip. 他决定跟我们一起去旅行。

taking.meaning: adj. 迷人的，吸引人的 / n. 收入，营业额
taking.note:
She has a very taking smile that brightens the room. 她有着迷人的微笑，使整个房间都明亮起来。

The store's daily takings dropped significantly due to rain. 由于下雨，商店的日营业额大幅下降。

talisman.note:
He carried a lucky coin as a talisman in his pocket. 他口袋里揣着一枚幸运硬币作为护符。

She views her grandmother's ring as a protective talisman. 她把祖母的戒指视为护身符。

tally.meaning: n. 记账，得分 / v. 符合，吻合，计算
tally.note:
The witness's story did not tally with the police report. 目击者的叙述与警方报告不符。

Keep a tally of all the expenses you make. 把你所有的开销都记下账来。

talon.note:
The eagle clutched its prey in its sharp talons. 雄鹰用锐利的利爪抓住了猎物。

The hawk swept down with claws extended. (注：同义替换语境) 鹰伸出利爪俯冲而下。

tambourine.note:
She shook the tambourine to the rhythm of the music. 她随着音乐的节奏摇晃着铃鼓。

The folk band featured a lively sound of the tambourine. 这个民间乐队带有一种欢快的铃鼓声。

tame.meaning: adj. 驯服的，温顺的 / v. 驯服，使顺从
tame.note:
It takes patience to tame a wild animal. 驯服野生动物需要耐心。

The tiger looked tame, but it was still dangerous. 这只老虎看起来很温顺，但依然很危险。

tamp.note:
He used a tool to tamp down the soil in the garden. 他用工具把花园里的土壤夯实。

The coffee grounds need to be tamped before brewing espresso. 煮浓缩咖啡前需要压紧咖啡粉。

tamper.meaning: v. 篡改，胡乱摆弄，干预
tamper.note:
Someone tried to tamper with the voting machines. 有人试图篡改投票机。

Do not tamper with the electrical wiring. 不要随意摆弄电线。

tan.meaning: v. 晒黑，硝皮 / adj. 黄褐色的 / n. 晒黑的皮肤
tan.note:
He likes to lie in the sun and get a tan. 他喜欢躺在太阳底下晒成小麦色。

Her skin turned a deep tan after weeks at the beach. 在海滩待了几周后，她的皮肤晒成了深棕褐色。

tangential.meaning: adj. 切线的，离题的，微弱相关的
tangential.note:
His comments were only tangential to the main topic of discussion. 他的评论与讨论的主题关系微弱。

We touched on a few tangential issues during the meeting. 我们在会议上顺便提到了几个离题的问题。

tangle.meaning: v. 缠结，陷入混乱 / n. 纠缠，乱团
tangle.note:
My hair always gets into a tangle when the wind blows. 起风时我的头发总是缠成一团。

He managed to untangle the fishing lines. 他设法把鱼线解开了。

tango.note:
They danced an energetic tango on the stage. 他们在舞台上跳了一支充满活力的探戈舞。

It takes two to tango, just like in negotiations. 就像谈判一样，一个巴掌拍不响。

tangy.meaning: adj. 刺鼻的，浓烈开胃的，酸溜溜的
tangy.note:
The salad dressing had a tangy lemon flavor. 沙拉酱带有浓郁开胃的柠檬风味。

She enjoyed the tangy taste of the fresh oranges. 她喜欢新鲜橘子那刺激好吃的酸味。

tantalize.meaning: v. 逗引，使干着急，撩拨
tantalize.note:
The smell of fresh baking began to tantalize us. 新烤面包的香味开始诱惑着我们。

She was tantalized by the possibility of winning the prize. 赢得奖品的可能性一直撩拨着她。

tantamount.meaning: adj. 相等的，同等的，相当于
tantamount.note:
His silence was tantamount to an admission of guilt. 他的沉默等同于认罪。

Ignoring the problem is tantamount to making it worse. 忽视这个问题无异于使其恶化。

tantrum.meaning: n. 发脾气，发怒（尤指幼儿）
tantrum.note:
The toddler threw a tantrum when he didn't get his toy. 小孩没拿到玩具便大发雷霆。

She threw a massive tantrum over the delayed flight. 因为航班延误，她发了一通大脾气。

taper.meaning: v. 逐渐变细，逐渐减少 / n. 细蜡烛
taper.note:
The road begins to taper as it climbs the mountain. 道路在爬山时开始变得越来越窄。

Production will taper off towards the end of the year. 到年底时产量会逐渐减少。

tapestry.meaning: n. 挂毯，织锦，丰富多彩的系列
tapestry.note:
An antique medieval tapestry hung on the castle wall. 一张中世纪古董挂毯挂在城堡的墙上。

History is a rich tapestry of human experiences. 历史是人类经历丰富多彩的交织。

tardy.note:
He received a warning for his tardy arrival. 他因迟到而受到了警告。

The government took tardy action to address the crisis. 政府对该危机采取了迟缓的应对行动。

tare.meaning: n. 皮重，空重，有害杂草
tare.note:
The scale automatically subtracts the tare weight of the container. 秤会自动扣除容器的皮重。

The farmer pulled out weeds and tares from the wheat field. 农民从麦田里拔出了杂草和毒麦。

tarnish.meaning: v. 玷污，使失去光泽 / n. 光泽暗淡，污点
tarnish.note:
Silver will tarnish if exposed to air for too long. 银器如果暴露在空气中太久会失去光泽。

The scandal threatened to tarnish his political reputation. 这桩丑闻威胁到了他的政治声誉。

tarpaulin.note:
They covered the woodpile with a heavy tarpaulin. 他们用厚防水帆布把木柴堆盖好。

Protect your boat with a waterproof tarpaulin. 用防水帆布保护你的小船。

tart.meaning: adj. 酸的，尖刻的 / n. 果馅饼，水果塔
tart.note:
The lemon tart was deliciously crisp and sour. 柠檬塔美味酥脆且酸甜可口。

She gave a tart reply to his rude comment. 她对他的粗鲁评论做出了尖刻的回应。

tasty.note:
She prepared a tasty dinner for the guests. 她为客人们准备了一顿美味的晚餐。

The soup smelled very tasty and rich. 汤闻起来非常香浓可口。

tatty.meaning: adj. 破旧的，寒酸的，劣质的
tatty.note:
He wore a tatty old jacket with worn elbows. 他穿着一件肘部磨损的破旧夹克。

The once-grand hotel now looked rather tatty. 这家曾经富丽堂皇的酒店现在看起来相当破旧。

taut.meaning: adj. 拉紧的，绷紧的，整洁的
taut.note:
Pull the rope taut and tie it securely. 把绳子拉紧并牢牢系好。

The sail was held taut in the strong wind. 在强风中，帆被绷得紧紧的。

tauten.note:
His muscles began to tauten as he prepared to run. 随着他准备起跑，他的肌肉开始紧绷起来。

Tauten the strings of the guitar before playing. 弹奏前把吉他弦调紧。

tawdry.meaning: adj. 俗气的，花哨而卑劣的
tawdry.note:
The stage decorations looked cheap and tawdry. 舞台布景看起来廉价又俗气。

She was involved in a tawdry political scandal. 她卷入了一场卑劣的政治丑闻中。

taxing.meaning: adj. 费力的，繁重的，伤脑筋的
taxing.note:
Studying for final exams can be a taxing experience. 准备期末考试可能是一段繁重伤脑筋的经历。

He found the marathon to be physically taxing. 他发现这场马拉松对体能消耗极大。

taxonomist.note:
The taxonomist discovered a brand-new species of beetle. 分类学家发现了一种全新的甲虫物种。

Taxonomists classify organisms based on shared characteristics. 分类学家根据共同特征对生物进行分类。

technocrat.meaning: n. 技术专家，技术官僚
technocrat.note:
The government appointed several technocrats to manage the economy. 政府任命了几位技术官僚来管理经济。

A technocrat focuses on practical, data-driven solutions. 技术专家专注于实用且以数据驱动的解决方案。

tedious.meaning: adj. 沉闷的，冗长乏味的
tedious.note:
Data entry can be a very tedious task. 数据录入可能是一项非常枯燥乏味的任务。

The speech was so tedious that many people fell asleep. 演讲太冗长了，许多人都睡着了。

tedium.note:
Music helped her escape the tedium of daily housework. 音乐帮她逃离了日常家务的单调乏味。

He read books to relieve the tedium of long journeys. 他靠读书来排解长途旅行的无聊。

teeter.meaning: v. 摇晃，蹒跚，颤抖着犹豫
teeter.note:
The company seemed to teeter on the brink of bankruptcy. 这家公司似乎在破产边缘摇摇欲坠。

She teetered on her high heels across the pavement. 她穿着高跟鞋摇摇晃晃地走在人行道上。

telling.meaning: adj. 有说服力的，显露内情的 / n. 讲述，宣告
telling.note:
He made a telling point during the debate. 他在辩论中提出了一个极具说服力的观点。

Her facial expression was telling of her true feelings. 她的面部表情泄露了她真实的感受。

temerity.meaning: n. 鲁莽，冒失，厚颜无耻
temerity.note:
He had the temerity to question the expert's decision. 他竟敢冒失地去质疑专家的决定。

She lacked the temerity to speak up in front of the board. 她没有勇气在董事会面前直言不讳。

temp.meaning: n. 临时工 / v. 做临时工
temp.note:
She worked as a temp at the office while looking for a permanent job. 她在寻找正式工作的同时在办公室当临时工。

He has been temping for several months now. 他当临时工已经好几个月了。

temper.meaning: n. 脾气，情绪 / v. 调和，使缓和
temper.note:
He has a quick temper and gets angry easily. 他脾气急躁，很容易生气。

Justice should be tempered with mercy. 司法应当与仁慈相调和。

tempest.note:
A violent tempest destroyed several ships at sea. 一场猛烈的暴风雨摧毁了海上的几艘船只。

His speech created a tempest of criticism. 他的演讲引发了一场狂风暴雨般的批评。

tempestuous.meaning: adj. 暴风雨般的，剧烈动荡的
tempestuous.note:
They had a tempestuous relationship full of arguments. 他们有一段充满争吵的剧烈动荡的关系。

Planes were grounded due to tempestuous weather. 由于风暴天气，飞机停飞了。

tempo.note:
The music picked up a faster tempo. 音乐加快了节奏。

We need to increase the tempo of our work to meet the deadline. 我们需要加快工作节奏以赶上截止日期。

temporal.meaning: adj. 时间的，世俗的，暂时的
temporal.note:
Human beings are bound by temporal limits. 人类受制于时间的限制。

The king held both spiritual and temporal power. 国王掌握着精神和世俗的双重权力。

temporize.meaning: v. 拖延，敷衍，见风使舵
temporize.note:
He tried to temporize in order to gain more time for negotiation. 他试图拖延时间以便为谈判争取更多空间。

Politicians often temporize when faced with difficult questions. 政治家在面对棘手问题时经常采取敷衍态度。

temptation.note:
She managed to resist the temptation to eat the cake. 她设法抵制住了吃蛋糕的诱惑。

Money and power can be powerful temptations. 金钱和权力可能是巨大的诱惑。

tenable.meaning: adj. 站得住脚的，可防守的
tenable.note:
His argument is no longer tenable in light of new evidence. 鉴于新证据，他的论点已不再站得住脚。

The fortress was no longer tenable against the siege. 这座堡垒在围攻下已无法继续坚守。

tend.meaning: v. 往往，倾向于；照料，护理
tend.note:
People tend to get tired after a long day of work. 人们在工作一整天后往往会感到疲惫。

The nurse tended to the injured patients with care. 护士悉心照料着受伤的病人。

tendentious.meaning: adj. 有倾向性的，宣传性的，偏颇的
tendentious.note:
The documentary was criticized for its tendentious viewpoint. 这部纪录片因其带有倾向性的观点而受到批评。

He wrote a tendentious article defending the policy. 他写了一篇为该政策辩护的倾向性文章。

tender.meaning: adj. 温柔的，脆弱的，嫩的 / v. 提出，投标
tender.note:
The meat was cooked until it was tender and juicy. 肉煮得很嫩而且多汁。

He decided to tender his resignation to the board. 他决定向董事会递交辞呈。

tenet.note:
Personal freedom is a core tenet of democracy. 个人自由是民主的核心信条。

Non-violence is a central tenet of his philosophy. 非暴力是他哲学的核心原则。

tenor.meaning: n. 男高音；大意，基调，脉络
tenor.note:
He sang the leading tenor role in the opera. 他在歌剧里唱男高音主角。

The general tenor of the meeting was optimistic. 会议的总体基调是乐观的。

tension.meaning: n. 紧张，张力，局势紧张
tension.note:
There is growing political tension between the two countries. 两国之间日益出现政治紧张局势。

Yoga helps to release physical tension in muscles. 瑜伽有助于释放肌肉中的身体紧张。

tepid.meaning: adj. 微温的，温热的；热忱不高的
tepid.note:
She washed her face with tepid water. 她用温水洗了脸。

The new policy received only a tepid response from the public. 这项新政策只得到了公众冷淡的反应。

terminal.meaning: adj. 末端的，晚期的，不治的 / n. 终点站，航站楼
terminal.note:
He arrived at Terminal 3 of the airport. 他抵达了机场的3号航站楼。

She was diagnosed with a terminal illness. 她被诊断患有绝症。

terminate.note:
The company decided to terminate his contract early. 公司决定提前终止他的合同。

Her pregnancy was terminated for medical reasons. 由于医疗原因，她的妊娠被终止了。

termination.note:
The sudden termination of the project shocked everyone. 项目的突然终止让所有人感到震惊。

Employees will receive severance pay upon termination. 员工在被解雇时将获得遣散费。

terminology.note:
The manual is full of complex technical terminology. 这本手册充满了复杂的专业术语。

Medical terminology can be difficult for laymen to understand. 医学术语对外行人来说很难理解。

terminus.note:
The train is approaching its final terminus. 火车正在接近终点站。

Bus line 42 starts its route from this city-center terminus. 42路公交车从这个市中心终点站开始发车。

termite.note:
Termites can cause severe structural damage to wooden houses. 白蚁会对木结构房屋造成严重的结构性破坏。

The floorboards were eaten away by termites. 地板被白蚁蛀空了。

terrace.meaning: n. 露台，阳台，阶地 / v. 做成梯田
terrace.note:
They sat on the rooftop terrace and enjoyed the view. 他们坐在屋顶露台上欣赏风景。

Farmers terraced the hillside to plant rice. 农民在山坡上筑成梯田来种水稻。
